latest.title: Peran Self-Control Dalam Memoderasi Pengaruh Lifestyle dan User Experience Terhadap Impulsive Buying Pada Generasi Z Pengguna Shopee
latest.abstract: Impulsive buying among Generation Z on Shopee is influenced by lifestyle and user experience; however, previous findings are inconsistent, and the role of self-control as a moderator has not been tested together with both factors. This study aims to analyze the role of self-control in moderating the effects of lifestyle and user experience on impulsive buying among Generation Z on Shopee. The study employs an associative-causal quantitative approach with purposive sampling of 100 active Generation Z Shopee users. Data were analyzed using PLS-SEM (SmartPLS 4), complemented by ANOVA (F-test) to examine the simultaneous effects. The results show that lifestyle and user experience have positive and significant effects on impulsive buying, both partially and simultaneously together with self-control and its two interactions (F = 12.325; p < 0.001). Self-control has a negative and significant effect and negatively and significantly moderates the effects of lifestyle and user experience, thereby weakening both relationships. The novelty of this study lies in its integrated model, which simultaneously examines lifestyle and user experience with self-control as a moderator. The better Generation Z's self-control, the lower the tendency toward impulsive buying, even when influenced by lifestyle and an engaging online shopping experience. These findings are expected to provide insights for consumers and e-commerce platform managers in understanding and managing purchasing behavior.

latest.title: Picture, picture on the screen: a between-subjects experiment on AI-generated vs human images on Generation Z consumers’ impulse buying intention
latest.venue: Young Consumers Insight and Ideas for Responsible Marketers
latest.abstract: Purpose The rapid advancement of artificial intelligence (AI) has transformed digital marketing strategies, particularly in the tourism industry, where AI-enhanced imagery is increasingly used to influence consumer behaviour. However, little research has examined how AI-generated images affect impulse travel purchases compared with human-generated images. This study aims to examine the effect of AI-enhanced versus human-generated images on impulse travel purchase decisions among Generation Z travellers, using Stimulus–Organism–Response (S-O-R) theory and consumption value theory as a theoretical lens. Design/methodology/approach Through a between-person experimental design, 580 participants were randomly assigned to view either AI-enhanced or human-generated images of a non-iconic travel destination. This study analysed results using partial least squares structural equation modelling. Findings The study found that preference value and social value directly and significantly influenced impulse purchase intentions, while all consumption values, including preference, social, emotional and functional values, affected impulse purchasing through travellers’ inspiration. Additionally, AI-enhanced images led to a higher preference value for impulse purchases, whereas human-generated images were perceived as having higher social value and visual aesthetic appeal. Originality/value By integrating the S-O-R framework with consumption value theory, this study offers fresh theoretical insights into the mediating role of traveller inspiration and the distinct value perceptions elicited by AI versus human-generated visuals. These findings also offer critical insights for tourism marketers using AI-driven visual content, consumers navigating increasingly AI-mediated travel promotions

latest.title: Normalizing sustainable fashion innovations: environmental messages and dynamic norms in circular fashion adoption
latest.abstract: Purpose This study aims to investigate whether informational messages promote interest in fashion products made from agri-food waste and whether dynamic norm cues strengthen persuasion in a trend-sensitive, ambiguous market. Design/methodology/approach Overall, 183 Italian adults were randomly assigned to control, environmental message or environmental plus dynamic norm message conditions. Participants reported purchasing intention and willingness to pay a premium price. Pro-environmental self-identity and identification with sustainable fashion consumers were tested as moderators. Findings Only the combined environmental and dynamic norm message increased purchasing intention, whereas neither message affected willingness to pay, suggesting a distinction between motivational interest and financial commitment. Exploratory analyses suggested that the environmental message was more effective among participants with low identification with sustainable fashion consumers. Pro-environmental self-identity did not moderate message effects. Research limitations/implications Self-reported intentions and a highly educated Italian sample limit generalisability. Future studies should use behavioural measures, field experiments, longitudinal designs and diverse samples to test whether initial openness persists and translates into purchasing and price acceptance. Practical implications Environmental messages combined with dynamic norm cues can increase initial interest in agri-food waste fashion, but the promotional strategy did not increase willingness to pay, highlighting the importance of product, price and audience segmentation. Originality/value The study shows that integrating dynamic norm cues into environmental appeals can increase initial openness toward novel sustainable fash

latest.title: Learner Choice, Not Learning Styles: Why giving learners a say in how they learn is better supported by evidence than matching them to a "style"
latest.venue: Zenodo (CERN European Organization for Nuclear Research)
latest.abstract: Matching teaching to a learner’s preferred sensory “style” remains popular, yet it is not supported by well-designed experiments, and belief in it remains widespread among educators. This white paper proposes a better-supported alternative: letting learners choose their route through a course while the learning outcomes and assessment stay the same for everyone. Drawing on research on choice, choice overload, self-determination theory and instructional guidance, it sets out five design principles, seven learning approaches, a worked example, guidance for institutions and a practitioner checklist. The paper is a conceptual synthesis and does not report new empirical data.

latest.title: A Study on Consumer Buying Behaviour in the Era of E-Commerce
latest.abstract: The rapid growth of e-commerce has changed how consumers recognise needs, search for information, evaluate alternatives, purchase products and evaluate their experience afterwards. This paper examines consumer buying behaviour in the era of e-commerce by synthesising established theories of consumer decision-making with contemporary research on online retail. It reviews the classical five-stage decision process, the Technology Acceptance Model, the Theory of Planned Behaviour and trust-based models, and then analyses the main factors that shape online buying behaviour: perceived usefulness and ease of use, trust and perceived risk, price and promotions, online reviews, personalisation, payment convenience, delivery and returns, and social influence. The paper proposes an integrated conceptual framework and six testable hypotheses, and outlines a mixed-method research design that can be used to validate the framework empirically. The analysis suggests that, while convenience and price remain the dominant drivers, trust, social proof and post-purchase service increasingly determine whether a first-time buyer becomes a loyal customer. The paper concludes with managerial implications for e-retailers, policy implications for regulators, and directions for future research.

latest.title: INFLUENCE OF AUDIENCE ENGAGEMENT ON CONSUMER DECISION-MAKING IN ILORIN METROPOLIS
latest.abstract: This study investigated the impact of social media marketing on consumer decision-making with specific focus on online retail businesses in Ilorin, Kwara State Nigeria. Descriptive survey research design was adopted and the population of the study was 1200 consumers who use the different social medial handles to buy products at Mamtess Mega Shopping Mall in Ilorin as at March, 2026. Taro Yamane (1967) formula was used to determine the sample size of 300 and out of which 250 copies of the well-structured questionnaire were retrieved. Descriptive statistics was used to analyze data in tabular form and representing the data in frequencies and percentage. The inferential statistics make use of simple linear and multiple regression for its analysis. Findings showed that social media marketing variables have impact on consumer decision-making. And the study therefore, concluded that social media marketing has significant impact on consumer purchase decision-making. Findings also revealed that audience engagement has more impact on consumer decision than content quality and platform frequency. Based on the conclusion of the study, it was recommended that business owners should extensively leverage on the social media marketing variables in order to influence the purchase intention, repeat purchase, and patronage of the consumer.

latest.title: The Effect of Virtual Try-On Technologies on Purchase Intention in Fashion Retailing: The Mediating Role of Perceived Product Fit
authors: L G D T B Thundeniya
latest.abstract: The rapid development of online fashion stores has added more challenges to the reality that consumers cannot physically analyse something like a piece of fashionable dress and buy it, especially in a size that fits. One of the biggest factors that prevents purchase intention and causes dissatisfaction and high turnover among consumers is the uncertainty related to the fittings. In turn, fashion retailers have been steadily developing virtual try-on (VTO) technologies as a new tool for assessing online products. However, the empirical findings on the usefulness of virtual try-on technologies in influencing purchase intention remain mixed, which justifies the need for a more focused conceptual framework. This concept paper examines the influence of virtual try-on technologies on purchase intention in online fashion retailing and how perceived product fit mediates this effect. The paper presents a summary of the potential theoretical and empirical sources on the subject and argues that virtual try-on technologies do not directly impact purchase intention; instead, they have an indirect impact, as they enhance consumers' confidence in the garment fit. The perceived product fit concept is theorised as being an important thinking process which minimises the uncertainty of the fit and maximises the confidence in making the decision. The article introduces a well-organised conceptual framework that relates the features of virtual try-on technology and perceived product fit to purchase intention, offering both theoretical and empirical insights and implications for online retailers interested in maximising the purchasing experience.

latest.title: Beyond Personalisation: Understanding the Influence of Artificial Intelligence-Driven Social Media Marketing on Consumer Engagement, Brand Trust and Purchase Intention among Generation Z Consumers in India
latest.venue: Stanzaleaf International Journal of Multidisciplinary Studies
latest.abstract: The increasing integration of artificial intelligence (AI) into social media marketing has transformed the ways in which brands communicate with consumers, personalise promotional content and influence purchasing decisions. AI-driven marketing technologies, including recommendation algorithms, predictive analytics, automated chatbots and generative AI content, enable organisations to deliver personalised and interactive marketing experiences. However, the effectiveness of these technologies in influencing consumer purchase intention depends not only on technological capabilities but also on consumers' psychological responses, particularly their engagement with brands and trust in AI-mediated marketing communication. This paper develops a conceptual understanding of the relationship between AI-driven social media marketing and consumer purchase intention among Generation Z consumers in India, with particular emphasis on the mediating roles of consumer engagement and brand trust. Drawing upon the Stimulus–Organism–Response (S-O-R) framework, consumer engagement theory and trust-based perspectives, the paper proposes an integrated conceptual model explaining how AI-enabled marketing stimuli influence consumers' cognitive, emotional and behavioural responses and subsequently shape purchase intention. The paper adopts a conceptual research approach supported by a critical review of relevant academic literature. It identifies AI-enabled personalisation, content relevance, interactivity and perceived transparency as important characteristics of AI-driven social media marketing. Consumer engagement and brand trust are proposed as complementary mediating mechanisms through which marketing stimuli may influence purchase intention. latest.title: Consumer purchasing decisions in the used motorcycle market: evidence from service quality, price, and location
latest.venue: ECOBIZTECH Journal of Economics Business and Technology
latest.abstract: Purpose: to analyze how service quality, price, and location influence consumer purchasing decisions at the Prima Motor Bogor used motorcycle showroom, both individually and within an integrated research model. Method: a quantitative approach with an explanatory research design. Data were collected through questionnaires distributed to 89 respondents using purposive total sampling. The data were analyzed using partial least squares structural equation modeling (PLS-SEM) in SmartPLS, evaluating the measurement (outer) and structural (inner) models to test the proposed hypotheses. Findings: service quality and price positively and significantly influence consumer purchasing decisions at Prima Motor Bogor, while location does not have a significant influence. These results indicate that consumers place greater emphasis on service professionalism, transaction transparency, and price suitability than on the showroom's physical accessibility when deciding to purchase used motorcycles. Implications: Prima Motor Bogor's management should improve service quality, maintain competitive and transparent pricing strategies, and optimize showroom accessibility and digital visibility to strengthen consumer confidence, enhance purchasing decisions, and improve business competitiveness. Originality: lies in integrating service quality, price, and location to examine consumer purchasing decisions specifically within the used motorcycle showroom context.

latest.title: Consumers’ well-being in livestreaming commerce: antecedents and consequences
latest.abstract: Livestreaming commerce represents an increasingly important form of digital retailing. This study examines relationships among informational and emotional support, streamer characteristics (expertise, trustworthiness and attractiveness), livestreaming environmental characteristics (interactivity, perceived crowdedness and social presence), consumers’ perceived value, shopping well-being and continuance intention. Survey data from 301 livestreaming consumers in China were analysed using partial least squares structural equation modelling (PLS-SEM), necessary condition analysis (NCA) and combined importance-performance map analysis (cIPMA). Perceived value and shopping well-being were positively related to continuance intention, and perceived value was positively related to shopping well-being. Expertise, interactivity, perceived crowdedness and social presence showed significant positive relationships with perceived value. The direct relationships for informational support, emotional support, trustworthiness and attractiveness were non-significant. Integrating PLS-SEM with NCA and cIPMA differentiated important predictors from minimum conditions associated with higher perceived value. The findings extend understanding of shopping well-being as a quality-of-life evaluation in livestreaming commerce.

latest.title: AI-Driven Consumer Decision-Making among Higher Education Students: Examining the Roles of Adoption, Trust and Personalization
latest.venue: International Journal of Science Strategic Management and Technology
latest.abstract: The digital space where higher-education students find products, compare them, get personalised recommendations and make online purchases is becoming more and more interwoven with artificial intelligence. This paper analyses the relationship between the adoption of AI, confidence in AI-based recommendations and AI-based personalisation and consumer purchasing behaviour amongst higher learning institutions. Two-way (quantitative) cross-sectional methodology is demonstrated using the simulated sample of 150 objects in the form of a quantitative cross-sectional study. A five-point Lickert scale has been designed in the form of a structured question to embrace AI adoption, AI trust, AI personalisation and consumer buying behaviour. Applying reliability analysis, descriptive statistics, Pearson correlation, one-way ANOVA and exploratory multiple regression. The simulated analysis shows a high internal consistency among the constructs and positive correlations between AI-related variables and buying behaviour. The differences in buying behaviour among the levels of AI experience may also be found, and the exploratory regression shows that the composite AI variables present a significant explanatory amount of variance. These numerical findings are explicitly exemplary and are not findings in reality by actual respondents. The research offers the student through the lens based on a convenient framework aimed at studying the potential role of convenience, trust, personalisation and perceived control in influencing purchases by AI in the context of higher education.

latest.title: Islamic Financial Product Acceptance and the Effectiveness of Inflation Targeting in Kenya: A Theoretical and Calibration Analysis of Monetary Policy Transmission.
latest.venue: International Journal of Social Science and Humanities Research (IJSSHR)
latest.abstract: Kenya's forecasting- and policy-based inflation-targeting regime has developed alongside a slow but accelerating formalisation of Islamic, or Sharia-compliant, finance: fully fledged Islamic banks operating since 2008, a growing number of Islamic windows in conventional banks and, in July 2024, the listing of Linzi Sukuk, the first Sharia-compliant product admitted to the Nairobi Securities Exchange. This paper examines how growing acceptance of Islamic financial products interacts with the transmission of the Central Bank Rate (CBR) to inflation and output. It develops a dual-banking-augmented small open-economy New Keynesian framework in which an Islamic product acceptance intensity variable enters household financing choices, firm marginal cost, bank rate setting and the central bank's policy problem. From an explicit household budget constraint, a bank repricing problem and a central bank loss function, the paper derives an attenuated IS curve, a financing-cost-augmented Phillips curve, a partial-adjustment rule linking Islamic profit rates to the policy rate, and a closed-form compensatory policy coefficient. Acceptance itself is modelled with a Bass diffusion equation. The paper reviews the cross-country evidence that Islamic financing responds less than conventional financing to policy-rate changes and that Islamic profit rates track conventional rates imperfectly, and finds that neither the Central Bank of Kenya's Quarterly Projection Model nor its macroeconometric model currently treats Sharia-compliant intermediation as a distinct block. latest.title: A EVOLUÇÃO TECNOLÓGICA E O NOVO COMPORTAMENTO DO CONSUMIDOR, QUE AGORA É MONITORADO POR ALGORITMOS
latest.venue: Anais do Congresso Brasileiro de Iniciação Científica
latest.abstract: The expansion of digital platforms has transformed entertainment consumption, as algorithms recommend content based on user habits. This study aims to understand how these systems influence choices and behaviors, considering the effects of personalization and cultural diversity. The research draws upon the ideas of Marshall McLuhan, Theodor Adorno, Zygmunt Bauman, and Pierre Bourdieu. It notes that while platform recommendations facilitate access to content and help broaden exposure to different cultures, they also foster the creation of digital bubbles and the repetition of preferences. The study concludes that, despite their convenience, algorithms can steer consumer choices, underscoring the importance of maintaining a critical and conscious relationship with these platforms.

latest.title: From Virtual to Valuable: How Influencer Type and Product Type Shape Consumer Value Co‐Creation Intention
latest.abstract: Virtual and human influencers offer distinct social and experiential cues, but their relative effectiveness may depend on how consumers evaluate the endorsed product. Drawing on the cognitive‐affective‐behavioral framework, this research integrates social information processing theory and cognitive‐affective system theory to examine consumer value co‐creation intention. Across three between‐subjects experiments ( N = 994), results reveal a consistent matching effect: virtual influencers have a relative advantage for search products, whereas human influencers have a relative advantage for experience products. This matching effect operates through parasocial interaction and empathy: forming a parasocial representation may make an influencer's perspective and affective cues more accessible, providing a relational basis for subsequent empathy. Consistent with this sequence, both the indirect effect through parasocial interaction and the serial indirect effect through parasocial interaction and empathy follow this product‐dependent pattern across both product categories, whereas the indirect effect through empathy alone favors human influencers only for experience products. Together, these findings identify product type as a boundary condition linking relational and affective processes to consumer value co‐creation intention, offering practical insights for aligning influencer selection with product characteristics.

latest.title: INFLUENCE OF BRAND DIFFERENTIATION STRATEGIES ON CUSTOMER PATRONAGE OF AUTOMOBILE PRODUCTS: A STUDY OF TOYOTA AND HONDA MOTOR MANUFACTURING COMPANIES N FEDERAL CAPITAL TERRITORY ABUJA, NIGERIA
latest.abstract: This research analyzed how brand differentiation approaches affect consumer patronage toward automobile brands in Abuja, Nigeria's capital region. The study focused specifically on examining whether the design quality and performance quality of Toyota and Honda cars shape how customers relate to these brands—measured through their confidence in the brands, inclination to buy again, and willingness to recommend them to others. Using a survey methodology, 300 individuals participated in the research through convenience-based selection. Questionnaires were used to gather information, which was then processed using Linear Regression analysis via SPSS 22. The results indicated that both design quality and performance quality of Toyota and Honda automobiles significantly and positively affect customer loyalty toward these brands. The study recommends that company leaders prioritize investment in research and development focused on improving design and performance quality as a key marketing approach to win over new customers and maintain existing ones.

latest.title: The Role of Tabligh Trait and Consumer Trust in Increasing Broiler Chicken Sales at Batang Kuis Market : PERAN SIFAT TABLIGH DAN KEPERCAYAAN KONSUMEN TERHADAP PENINGKATAN PENJUALAN AYAM POTONG DI PASAR BATANG KUIS
latest.abstract: This study is grounded in the urgency of implementing Islamic business ethics, particularly information transparency (tabligh) and halal product assurance, to sustain traditional market trading. This research aims to analyze the partial and simultaneous roles of the tabligh trait and consumer trust in increasing broiler chicken sales at Batang Kuis Market, Deli Serdang Regency. Utilizing a quantitative associative approach, this study involved a population of broiler chicken buyers, with a sample of 125 respondents selected via purposive sampling. Primary data were gathered through validity- and reliability-tested questionnaires, and analyzed using classical assumption tests, multiple linear regression, t-test, F-test, and coefficient of determination. The findings reveal that the tabligh trait has a positive and significant partial effect on sales increase. Consumer trust also exhibits a positive and significant partial influence, serving as the most dominant contributor. Simultaneously, both variables significantly drive sales growth, explaining a substantial portion of sales variations while the remainder is influenced by external factors. In conclusion, consistent application of muamalah transparency and halal trust guarantees effectively enhances trader turnover and business sustainability in traditional markets. Abstrak. Penelitian ini didasari oleh urgensi penerapan etika bisnis Islam, khususnya keterbukaan informasi (tabligh) dan jaminan kehalalan produk, guna menjaga keberlanjutan perdagangan di pasar tradisional. Penelitian ini bertujuan untuk menganalisis peran sifat tabligh dan kepercayaan konsumen secara parsial maupun simultan terhadap peningkatan penjualan ayam potong di Pasar Batang Kuis, Kabupaten Deli Serdang. Menggunakan pendekatan kuantitatif asosiat

latest.title: A Story to Sell: The Mediating Role of Storytelling in Consumer Purchase Intention toward Regional Woven Fabrics
latest.venue: Journal of Economics Entrepreneurship Management Business and Accounting
latest.abstract: Purpose – This study examines the associations of Perceived Government Support and influencer marketing with consumer purchase intention toward traditional woven fabrics from East Nusa Tenggara, Indonesia, considering storytelling as a mediating variable. Design/methodology/approach – A quantitative survey involving 347 consumers of East Nusa Tenggara woven fabrics was conducted. Data were analyzed using Partial Least Squares Structural Equation Modeling (PLS-SEM) to assess direct and indirect relationships. Finding/Results – Perceived Government Support showed no significant direct association with purchase intention (β = 0.049; p = 0.433) but was positively associated with storytelling (β = 0.574; p < 0.001). Influencer marketing positively related to storytelling (β = 0.222; p = 0.019) and purchase intention (β = 0.166; p = 0.002). Storytelling significantly predicted purchase intention (β = 0.695; p < 0.001) and demonstrated indirect-only mediation for government support (β = 0.399; p < 0.001) and complementary mediation for influencer marketing (β = 0.154; p = 0.012). Originality/Value – This study integrates government support, influencer marketing, and cultural storytelling into a unified framework explaining purchase intention toward traditional cultural products. It highlights storytelling as a strategic marketing approach for governments and SMEs while providing a foundation for future cross-cultural and longitudinal research.

latest.title: The Role of Green Marketing of Electric Vehicles in Influencing Buying Intention in Indonesia
latest.venue: International Journal of Social Science and Human Research
latest.abstract: This study investigates the role of green marketing in influencing the buying intention of electric vehicles (EVs) in Indonesia. Using a quantitative approach with Structural Equation Modeling (SEM), data from 330 respondents across Indonesia were collected via an online questionnaire to assess the relationship between the 4Ps of green marketing (Product, Price, Place, Promotion), Electric Vehicle Knowledge, and Environmental Attitude toward Green Buying Intention. The findings reveal that Green Product, Green Price, and Green Place have a significant and positive effect on EV buying intention, while Green Promotion and Electric Vehicle Knowledge did not show a statistically significant impact. Furthermore, although Environmental Attitude was found to have a strong direct influence on Green Buying Intention, it did not significantly moderate any of the tested relationships. The results imply that while Indonesians with strong environmental attitudes are more inclined to purchase EVs, promotional campaigns and general product knowledge from the 4Ps of green marketing may not yet be powerful enough to shift consumer behavior alone.

latest.title: U.S.-Canada Trade Tensions And Their Influence On Canadian Perception, National Sentiment And Consumer Behaviour
latest.venue: International Journal of Business & Management Studies
latest.abstract: This study investigates how recent U.S. threatened and imposed tariffs under the Trump administration have influenced Canadian public sentiment and consumer behaviour. While traditional economic analysis of tariffs focuses on macro-level indicators such as GDP and trade balances, this research explores the sociopsychological and behavioural impacts of economic protectionism on individuals. Specifically, it examines the extent to which Canadian consumers’ awareness of tariffs correlates with negatives perceptions of Americans, increased nationalism, consumer ethnocentrism and retaliatory purchasing behaviour. Drawing upon theories such as social identity theory, consumer ethnocentrism and reactance theory, the study develops a conceptual framework linking tariff awareness to five key hypotheses. A cross-sectional, quantitative survey was conducted with 123 Canadian residents, collecting data on demographic variables, attitudes toward the U.S., national sentiments and purchasing patterns. The validated instruments consisted of both self-developed scales and pre-established scales including the CETSCALE (Shimp & Sharma, 1987) and Kosterman & Feshbach’s Nationalism scale (1989). Statistical analyses revealed significant relationships across several variables. Greater awareness of U.S. tariffs was associated with more negative perceptions of Americans, heightened national pride, a stronger preference for Canadian products and reduced support for U.S. brands. Notably, consumer behaviour in Canada has shifted, with increasing domestic product loyalty and signs of consumer boycott activity, evidenced by retail behaviour. Regression models confirmed that tariff awareness significantly predicts these attitudinal and behavioural outcomes. These findings offer insights into how eco

latest.title: Toward a targeted localization framework: branding strategy replication in the Asia-Pacific bubble tea industry
latest.abstract: This study investigates how multinational corporations replicate branding strategies across culturally and institutionally diverse markets in the Asia-Pacific, specifically comparing Taiwan (a mature market) and Indonesia (an emerging market) via the bubble tea industry. Utilizing structural equation modeling (SEM) and multi-group analysis on 293 consumers with prior brand interaction, the research tests the sequential associations of brand equity components and the moderating role of national institutional maturity. The research confirms a consistent brand equity structural framework: Brand Image (BI) is positively associated with Brand Satisfaction (BS), which in turn correlates with Brand Trust (BT) and sequentially predicts Purchase Intention (PI). Furthermore, institutional contingencies moderate these pathways. In emerging markets with higher information asymmetry, purchase intention is heavily image-driven, relying on BI as a heuristic signal to mitigate risks. Conversely, mature markets are satisfaction-driven, emphasizing personal experiential validation over social signaling. This study introduces the Targeted Localization framework. While the strategic weights of brand image and satisfaction shift dramatically across contexts (supporting Targeted Localization), the empirical rejection of contextual differences in brand trust reveals its role as a universally critical baseline for transnational purchase intentions.

latest.title: The Hidden Economics of Digital Lending: Algorithmic Credit Intermediation, Consumer Choice and Regulatory Accountability under India’s Digital Lending Framework
latest.abstract: India’s 2025 digital-lending framework expressly addresses transparency in the presentation of loan offers. This article explores the transparency of digital marketplaces for loans. It relies on doctrinal, institutional economics and behavioral economics theories and concepts to substantiate its arguments. The article argues that, despite similarities in the wording of multiple loan offers, there may exist differences in the priorities and values of the offers, and borrowers may not be able to consider all those factors. The article considers the 2025 framework issued by the Reserve Bank of India (RBI) as a positive development to regulate lending marketplaces. However, the article identifies an imbalance where regulated entities remain responsible for LSP oversight, but verifying the operation of those controls may be difficult. The article describes a “price-choice-accountability” triad to illustrate that lending marketplaces should establish reasonable processes based on prior notice, and control misleading practices. The article does not examine the extent to which lending marketplaces, guided by the 2025 Directions, have introduced loan offer interfaces that bias against borrowers.

latest.title: Beyond Mutual Consent: Reconstructing Tarādin in Islamic Price Ethics amid Luxury Branding and Symbolic Consumption
latest.abstract: Premium price acceptance in the luxury product market is driven not only by functional utility, but also by brand heritage, exclusivity, and symbolic value—creating a pricing paradox in which elevated prices enhance rather than deter consumer desirability. Within Islamic economics, this phenomenon challenges classical assessments of consumer consent (tarāḍin), which primarily evaluate formal contractual assent and overt willingness to pay. This study aims to reconstruct tarāḍin within Islamic price ethics by shifting its analytical focus from formal agreement to the procedural integrity of value formation amid luxury branding and symbolic consumption. Employing a qualitative-conceptual library research method, this study systematically selected and synthesized foundational Qur’anic and fiqh al-mu‘āmalāt texts alongside peer-reviewed literature on Islamic business ethics, luxury branding, and symbolic consumption through thematic coding and comparative conceptual synthesis. From this analytical procedure, the study derives four interdependent dimensions in the proposed normative model of reconstructed tarāḍin: informational transparency, voluntary consent, value representation, and ethical price justice. Addressing the luxury pricing paradox, these four dimensions demonstrate that genuine consent requires evaluating whether symbolic prestige is communicated without deception (tadlīs), manufactured scarcity coercion, or gross price disparity (ghabn fāḥisy). This study offers a theoretical contribution to Islamic economic thought by extending tarāḍin beyond classical doctrines of honesty and contractual validity into an evaluative framework for contemporary luxury marketing. Because this framework represents a proposed normative model derived from conceptual synthesis, fut

latest.title: THE ROLE OF CONSUMER TRUST AS A MEDIATOR IN THE RELATIONSHIP BETWEEN ONLINE CONSUMER REVIEWS (ELECTRONIC WORD OF MOUTH) AND PERCEIVED VALUE ON PURCHASE DECISIONS FOR CULINARY PRODUCTS IN BOGOR
latest.abstract: This study aims to examine whether consumer trust mediates the relationship between electronic word of mouth (e-WOM) and purchase decisions, as well as the relationship between perceived value and purchase decisions for culinary products in Bogor. The study involved 100 respondents who had previously purchased culinary products in Bogor, selected using a purposive sampling technique. Data were analyzed using Partial Least Squares–Structural Equation Modeling (PLS-SEM). PLS-SEM was selected because it does not require the assumption of normally distributed data. In addition, PLS-SEM is suitable for relatively small to medium sample sizes, approximately 80–160 respondents, while still providing stable parameter estimates (Hair et al., 2016). The results indicate that consumer trust significantly mediates the relationship between e-WOM and purchase decisions. This finding suggests that e-WOM influences purchase decisions indirectly through consumer trust. Consumer trust also significantly mediates the relationship between perceived value and purchase decisions.

latest.title: ANALISIS PENGARUH STRATEGI DIGITAL MARKETING, MARKETING EVENT TERHADAP BRAND AWARENESS PADA PT MULTI MAYAKA JAKARTA
latest.abstract: This study aims to analyze the influence of digital marketing and marketing events on brand awareness at PT Multi Mayaka, a company specializing in the distribution of industrial and technical equipment. The research is grounded in the company's need to enhance brand visibility through integrated marketing approaches. A quantitative method was employed using a survey of 100 respondents, consisting of business partners and customers. Data analysis techniques included multiple linear regression, t-tests, F-tests, and classical assumption tests. The results indicate that digital marketing has a positive and significant impact on brand awareness, while marketing events exert a more dominant influence. Simultaneously, both variables contribute significantly to increasing brand recognition. These findings support the theories of (Keller & Kotler, 2022) and (Aaker, 2020) regarding the effectiveness of marketing communication in shaping brand perception. The study offers practical contributions for companies in designing more integrated marketing strategies, as well as academic contributions to the development of B2B marketing models based on digital and experiential approaches. The study is limited to a single company and two primary variables. Future research is recommended to explore additional factors such as customer engagement and brand loyalty using a longitudinal approach.

latest.title: Determinants of Green Purchase Intention and Green Purchase Behavior Among College Students in Fujian, China
latest.abstract: Purpose: This study addresses the limited evidence on factors influencing green purchase intention and green purchase behavior among college students in a regional vocational education context in China. Research design, data and methodology: A quantitative survey was conducted among 500 students from the Department of Automation Engineering at Meizhouwan Vocational Technology College. A non-probability sampling approach combining purposive, quota, and convenience sampling was adopted. A pilot test involving 30 participants was conducted, and content validity and reliability were assessed using the Item Objective Congruence method and Cronbach’s alpha. Confirmatory factor analysis and structural equation modeling using AMOS were employed to evaluate the measurement model and test the hypothesized relationships. Results: Perceived behavioral control, subjective norms, attitude, environmental concern, and environmental knowledge significantly influenced green purchase intention (p < .05). Perceived behavioral control showed the strongest effect (β = 0.577), followed by subjective norms (β = 0.369). Green purchase intention significantly predicted green purchase behavior (β = 0.516). Conclusions: The findings demonstrate the importance of perceived behavioral control, social influence, and environmental awareness in strengthening green purchase intention, which subsequently promotes green purchase behavior. Universities and policymakers should implement targeted educational and campus-based initiatives to encourage sustainable consumption among students.

latest.title: Determinants of Customer Satisfaction and Repurchase Intention in Live Streaming Commerce: Evidence from Hangzhou, China
latest.abstract: Purpose: This article aims to examine the factors influencing customer satisfaction and repurchase intention toward live streaming commerce platforms among residents in Hangzhou, China. Research design, data and methodology: This study adopts a quantitative research design and collects data through an online questionnaire survey administered to 500 residents across four major urban districts of Hangzhou, China. A multi-stage non-probability sampling approach was employed, including judgmental sampling to select the study areas, quota sampling to determine the sample size, and convenience sampling for data collection. Structural equation modeling and confirmatory factor analysis were applied to examine the measurement and structural models. Model fit, construct reliability, and convergent and discriminant validity were rigorously assessed to ensure the robustness of the analytical results. Results: The empirical findings indicate that real-time interaction, flow, value, quality, and trust all have significant positive effects on customer satisfaction in live streaming commerce. Customer satisfaction, in turn, has a strong and significant influence on repurchase intention (β = 0.472). In addition, the five antecedent factors indirectly affect repurchase intention through customer satisfaction. Conclusions: All six proposed hypotheses were supported, confirming the achievement of the research objectives. The findings highlight customer satisfaction as a key mechanism linking platform-related and experiential factors to repurchase intention. Enhancing real-time interaction, immersive experiences, perceived value, service quality, and trust can effectively improve platform competitiveness in live streaming commerce.

latest.title: Building Trust: The Key to Purchase Intention Among Vocational College Students
latest.abstract: Purpose: Aims to identify the key role of building trust in live-streaming e-commerce scenarios, and to clarify the mechanism through which trust drives purchase intention among vocational college students. Specifically, an integrated conceptual framework is developed to examine the structural relationships among influencer characteristics, perceived value, trust, and behavioral intentions, thereby providing actionable implications for improving live-streaming sales effectiveness. Research Design, Data and Methodology: A quantitative survey (N = 500) was conducted among students from vocational colleges in Kaili, China, using purposive, quota, and convenience sampling. Confirmatory Factor Analysis was applied to assess measurement reliability and validity, and Structural Equation Modeling was employed to test hypothesized relationships and evaluate overall model fit. Results: The findings indicate that Popularity (β = 0.281), Professionalism (β = 0.368), Interactivity (β = 0.272), Perceived Usefulness (β = 0.294), and Price Discounts (β = 0.305) have significant positive influences on Trust. Meanwhile, Trust has a significant positive influence on purchase intentions (β = 0.620). Conclusions: This study reveals a mechanism of building trust to purchase intentions, extends trust-related theories. It contributes to the academic literature and provides practical guidance for influencers and platforms, empowering them to building trust and enhance conversion performance in competitive live streaming e-commerce environments.

latest.title: DINAMIKA PERILAKU KONSUMEN FASHION GENERASI Z : STUDI KOMPARATIF ANTARA FAST FASHION DAN BRAND LOKAL INDONESIA
latest.abstract: Transformasi digital dalam industri fashion turut mengubah pola konsumsi Generasi Z ketika menentukan pilihan antara fast fashion dan brand fashion lokal. Studi ini membandingkan preferensi terhadap kedua kategori tersebut sekaligus menganalisis peran Media Sosial dan Sustainability Awareness dalam Keputusan Pembelian Fashion. Sebanyak 320 responden Generasi Z berusia 17–27 tahun dilibatkan melalui purposive sampling. Data dianalisis dengan Paired Samples T-Test dan regresi linear berganda. Hasil analisis menemukan perbedaan preferensi yang signifikan (p = 0,022), dengan rata-rata brand lokal sebesar 17,69 dan fast fashion sebesar 16,36. Media Sosial dan Sustainability Awareness juga menunjukkan pengaruh positif dan signifikan terhadap Keputusan Pembelian Fashion, dengan kemampuan model menjelaskan 39% variasi keputusan pembelian. Temuan tersebut memperlihatkan bahwa pilihan fashion Generasi Z berkaitan dengan preferensi kategori produk, lingkungan digital, dan pertimbangan keberlanjutan.

latest.title: Closing the Knowledge Gap: How Moral Obligations, Perceived Benefits, and Dispositional Greed Shape Influencer Advertising Code Compliance
latest.abstract: The rapid growth of influencer marketing has outpaced regulatory enforcement and has increased the risk of noncompliance through misleading promotions and inadequate sponsorship disclosures. This study investigates whether and how enhancing influencers’ advertising code knowledge affects their intentions to comply with advertising regulations. Specifically, it examines whether increased knowledge enhances compliance intentions, whether this relationship is mediated by moral obligations and perceived benefits, and whether dispositional greed moderates these mediating pathways. Across four studies, involving 1,082 U.K.-based social media influencers, we employed diverse research designs. Study 1 uses a single-session pre–post design (N = 154); Study 2 adopts a two-wave pre–post design (N = 213); Study 3 applies a third-person, between-subjects design (N = 228); and Study 4 employs a randomized experimental design (N = 487). The findings reveal that greater advertising code knowledge significantly increases influencers’ intentions to comply. This effect is mediated by stronger moral obligations and heightened recognition of the compliance benefits. Furthermore, dispositional greed moderates the influence of knowledge on both moral obligations and perceived benefits. These findings highlight the importance of targeted education and training that build influencers’ advertising code knowledge as a lever for strengthening ethical conduct and regulatory compliance.

latest.title: Sustainable talent attraction in hospitality: configurational pathways to Generation Z career intention
latest.abstract: Sustainable hospitality requires young people to perceive hospitality work as a viable, responsible, and socially acceptable long-term career. Building a responsible employer value proposition (EVP) is central to sustainable talent attraction, yet prior research largely treats employer attributes as independent, linear predictors. This study adopts a configurational approach to examine how sustainable EVP signals shape Generation Z hospitality career intention in Thailand. Data from 180 hospitality students and recent graduates were analysed using partial least squares structural equation modelling (PLS-SEM) and fuzzy-set Qualitative Comparative Analysis (fsQCA). Financial rewards, flexibility, and ethical commitment were combined into an exploratory higher-order construct, Core Employer Value (CEV), representing a bundled baseline of responsible employment. PLS-SEM identified career feasibility as the sole significant predictor. fsQCA converged on this: career feasibility appeared in every pathway to high intention but was never sufficient alone, always requiring two of the remaining mutually substitutable conditions (CEV, well-being support, or social endorsement). Conversely, low intention followed an asymmetric ‘dealbreaker’ logic driven by absent career feasibility despite other positive signals. This exploratory study extends signalling theory toward composite signal bundles, demonstrates the value of pairing symmetric and asymmetric methods, and reframes these attributes as social sustainability indicators.
latest.subfield: Organizational Behavior and Human Resource Management

latest.title: Social Media Influencers in Corporate Social Responsibility and Sustainability Communication: A Hybrid Bibliometric and Thematic Review
latest.abstract: Addressing global sustainability challenges and advancing the United Nations Sustainable Development Goals (SDGs), particularly SDG 12 and SDG 13, requires communication that can support pro‐environmental behaviour and responsible consumption. Social media influencers (SMIs) increasingly mediate such communication by translating CSR and sustainability issues into messages linked to everyday practices. This study conducts a hybrid bibliometric and systematic thematic review following the SPAR‐4‐SLR protocol. The bibliometric corpus comprised 206 peer‐reviewed journal articles and reviews indexed in Scopus and Web of Science. Six citation communities comprising 129 documents were retained for interpretation of the citation network, while 86 studies were selected for full‐text thematic synthesis. Performance analysis and science mapping using Bibliometrix (R), VOSviewer, and Gephi were integrated with full‐text thematic synthesis. The review identifies three themes, namely influencer‐driven sustainable communication from a communication perspective, influencer‐driven sustainable consumption from a marketing perspective, and influencer‐driven CSR communication. Across these themes, source credibility, authenticity, congruence, and parasocial relationships form recurring persuasion mechanisms, while the salience and involvement of the organisation vary. The evidence base is concentrated on environmental issues, responsible consumption, and short‐term audience outcomes, with less attention to social equity, economic and legal CSR responsibilities, and verifiable sustainability outcomes. By using organisational involvement to integrate the three streams while preserving CSR's corporate boundary, the review extends embeddedness theory and proposes a potential tension between or

latest.title: When Consumers Use Apples to Judge Oranges: How Frequency Information About Missing Product Attributes Biases Consumer Choice
latest.venue: DigitalCommons - Kennesaw State University (Kennesaw State University)

latest.title: TOUTING THE AMERICAN DREAM TO MOVE PROSPECTS DOWN THE PATH TO PURCHASE USING A CONCEPTUAL DECISION-MAKING FRAMEWORK
latest.venue: DigitalCommons - Kennesaw State University (Kennesaw State University)
latest.abstract: The American dream is a concept that is echoed across our society, and while the data shows Americans do not overwhelmingly believe in the dream, marketers continue to include it and the issue of economic prosperity in their agendas.Through a novel framework that overlaps a deeply studied mass communication theory with a decision-making framework used in marketing, this paper explores a new lens to understand how marketers identify strategies and tactics, build agendas, and make sales by touting the American dream.These concepts are important to understand because of the power and influence each has, which, as separate entities are powerful enough, but together, can create an environment that is powerfully persuasive.The conceptual model presented in this paper helps to visualize these interconnected processes in a way that has not been done before in today's modern media landscape.This model is an important visualization of the power marketers have when they build strategies and plan tactics to move an individual down the path of purchase. Keywords -American dream,

latest.title: IMPACT OF SOCIAL MEDIA MARKETING ON YOUTH BUYING PATTERN
latest.abstract: The study examines the impact of social media marketing on the buying pattern of youth. It focuses on the influence of social media advertisements, influencer promotions, online reviews, platform preferences and impulsive buying behaviour. The study adopts a descriptive and empirical research design and uses primary data collected through a structured questionnaire. The project reports responses from 115 respondents and applies percentage analysis, tabulation and graphical presentation to interpret the data. The findings indicate that social media is an important source of product information for young consumers. Instagram is reported as the most-used platform, while reviews, offers, influencer content and short videos are among the factors shaping purchase decisions. The study also identifies fake advertisements and product-quality concerns as important problems. The results highlight the need for transparent digital promotions and informed consumer decision-making.

latest.title: Line curvilinearity–masculinity associations on packaging influence expected taste intensity of green tea
latest.abstract: Visual cues on product packaging play an important role in shaping consumers’ sensory expectations before they consume. Although line curvilinearity is commonly used in green tea packaging, little research has examined how angular versus rounded lines influence expected taste intensity or the psychological mechanisms. This research aims to examine how line curvilinearity ​(Angular vs. Rounded) affects expected taste intensity in green tea packaging. It also investigates the roles of perceived femininity and masculinity in this relationship. Three online experiments were conducted with 458 participants recruited through the Credamo platform in China. Participants viewed green tea packaging featuring angular or rounded lines and rated expected taste intensity, perceived masculinity and femininity, and willingness to purchase. Across three studies, angular lines (vs. rounded lines) were associated with higher expected taste intensity. They were also associated with higher perceived masculinity ( B = 1.66, p < .001 in S1; B = 2.21, p < .001 in S2; B = 1.76, p < .001 in S3) and lower perceived femininity ( B = -1.32, p < .001 in S1; B = -1.72, p < .001 in S2; B = -1.25, p < .001 in S3). Perceived masculinity consistently accounted statistically for the relationship between line curvilinearity and expected taste intensity, whereas perceived femininity did not. Expected taste intensity was also positively associated with willingness to purchase. This research offers insights into how tea enterprises can optimize their packaging design. This research examines how a common design element in green tea packaging (Angular vs. Rounded lines) influences consumers’ expected taste intensity and highlights the unique mediating role of perceived masculinity.

latest.title: Building Customer Loyality for Marning Corn in Bulukumba: The Impact of Brand Image, Service Quality, and Product Quality on Purchase Decisions and Customer Satisfaction
latest.venue: Journal of Global Innovations in Agricultural Sciences
latest.abstract: Marning corn products, typical food, and souvenirs from the Bulukumba district are packaged simply without complete product information. Yet by integrating well-designed packaging with clear and relevant product information that can improve product quality, brands can improve the overall consumer experience, build trust, and foster long-term loyalty. This research aims to analyze the direct and indirect influence of brand image, service quality, and product quality on purchasing decisions and consumer satisfaction on consumer loyalty to making corn. The research method used quantitative analysis with structured interview techniques using a sample of corn buyers in Bulukumba Regency. The data analysis used is structural equation modeling (SEM) analysis using the AMOS application. The research results show that consumer satisfaction and brand image have a significant direct influence on loyalty. Brand image and service quality have an impact on purchasing decisions. Product quality, service quality, and brand image influence consumer satisfaction. Meanwhile, the variables of service quality and production quality do not have a significant effect on consumer loyalty through purchasing decisions and consumer satisfaction as intervening variables of brand image, service quality, and production quality. Increasing income in the Morning Corn business can be achieved by prioritizing brand image, service quality, and product quality so that later it can increase the number of buyers and increase consumer loyalty. Keywords: Customer loyalty, buying decision, customer satisfaction, brand image, service quality, product quality and marning corn.

latest.title: Coping with sustainability information overload: The role of generative artificial intelligence literacy
latest.venue: Ho Chi Minh City Open University Journal of Science- Economics and Business Administration
latest.abstract: Consumers can use sustainability information to consume responsibly; however, excessive and complex sustainability claims might confuse consumers and hinder proper evaluations. Based on cognitive appraisal theory, this study empirically investigates the impacts of sustainability information overload (SIO) on green information avoidance (GIA) and green information verification behavior (GIVB) and examines the moderating role of generative AI literacy (GAIL) and the associations of GIA and GIVB with green purchase decision confidence (GPDC). Data from an online cross-sectional survey of 468 adult consumers in Ho Chi Minh City, Vietnam, were analyzed using partial least squares structural equation modeling. Findings revealed that SIO positively influenced GIA, and GIA negatively influenced GPDC. However, SIO did not negatively influence GIVB on average. GAIL significantly moderated the SIO-GIVB relationship: SIO was negatively associated with GIVB at low GAIL but not significantly at mean or high GAIL.GIVB positively influenced GPDC. An indirect effect of SIO on GPDC through GIA is significant, but the indirect effect through GIVB is not significant unconditionally. These results suggest that sustainability information overload is associated with distinct coping responses. From a practical perspective, sustainability portals and shopping applications involving GenAI should emphasize evaluability and verifiability rather than enhancing disclosures. Through defining GAIL as a digitally mediated capability from the consumer’s perspective which can serve as a coping tool, this paper builds on cognitive appraisal theory in the context of AI-mediated sustainable consumption and explains the critical engagement of consumers with sustainability information amid overload situations

latest.title: The impact of environmental knowledge on water waste in restaurants on complaining behavior intention: The mediating role of perceived motivation and skepticism
latest.venue: Journal of Tourism Leisure and Hospitality
latest.abstract: This study aims to examine the impact of environmental knowledge about water waste in restaurants on consumers' intentions to complain, while also elucidating the mediating roles of perceived motivation and skepticism in this relationship. A scenario-based experimental research design was employed, and data were gathered from 388 restaurant goers through an online survey. Participants were randomly assigned to two restaurant scenarios: one in which water-saving practices were not observable and another in which they were prominently displayed. The data were analyzed using structural equation modeling and bootstrapped mediation analyses in SPSS 26 and AMOS 23. The research findings demonstrate that, in the first scenario—characterized by the absence of visible communication about water conservation—environmental knowledge had no direct, significant influence on the intention to display complaint behavior. Environmental knowledge increased perceived motivation and skepticism. Perceived motivation did not directly and significantly influence the intention to engage in complaint behavior; however, skepticism increased the intention to engage in such behavior. In the second scenario, where water-saving methods were visible, environmental knowledge directly and positively affected the intention to complain, perceived motivation, and skepticism; furthermore, perceived motivation and skepticism partially mediated the relationship between environmental knowledge and the intention to complain. The findings suggest that restaurants must not only implement eco-friendly practices but also communicate them to consumers in a transparent, visible, and trustworthy way. In this context, restaurant managers should create informative visuals and communication strategies that promote water

latest.title: Youth engagement with algorithmic consumerism cultures: A systematic psychological review.
latest.abstract: This article presents a systematic literature review and a conceptual framework for understanding how youth engage with and are influenced by algorithmic consumerism cultures on social media. We integrate findings from 72 quantitative , experimental, and qualitative psychological studies to examine a relatively new form of consumer culture that has been advanced by social media and algorithmic technologies, in which novel marketing methods and the strategic targeting of youth through social media influencers are increasingly prevalent. We conceptualize this as algorithmic consumerism cultures that are unique in their pace, individualization , user engagement, and implicitness. The results show that youth engagement with consumerism online is shaped by three main psychological processes: intrapersonal processes influencing identity and well-being , social processes influencing motivation and persuasion , and cognitive and moral developmental processes influencing critical engagement and advertising literacy . Advancing this field requires methodologies that capture the reciprocal influence between algorithm-driven consumerist content on social media and youth’s active navigation of this content. This requires conceptualizing such spaces as subcultures with their own norms and practices that need to be investigated through the perspectives of the “ natives ” of those cultures: youth.

latest.title: A Study on Lead Management and Customer Engagement Practices in the Residential Real Estate Sector
latest.venue: International Journal of Creative and Open Research in Engineering and Management
latest.abstract: Residential real estate is a high-involvement purchase in which customers generally compare several projects, evaluate affordability and consult family members before making a decision. For a channel partner, the quality of lead management and customer engagement therefore plays an important role in moving an enquiry towards a site visit and, ultimately, a booking. This paper examines the lead management and customer engagement practices observed at Thee House Of Real Estate Solutions Pvt. Ltd., Pune, during the internship undertaken by Om Sunil Tiwari. The study follows a descriptive and exploratory approach. Primary information was drawn from participant observation, customer requirement calls, follow-up activities, property presentations, virtual interactions, site-visit coordination and discussions with the sales team. Secondary information was drawn from project brochures, available sales material and relevant concepts of customer relationship management, relationship marketing and consumer buying behaviour. The analysis is qualitative because detailed company-wide conversion statistics and complete commercial records were not available. The observations indicate that lead conversion is influenced by the quality of the initial enquiry, accurate understanding of customer requirements, clarity of pricing and project information, timely follow-up, product knowledge and coordination for site visits. Customers evaluate properties on factors such as budget, location, configuration, purchase purpose, possession expectations and developer credibility. The paper recommends structured lead qualification, updated customer records, planned follow-up, personalised communication and verified property information. The findings are specific to the internship experience and should

hot.title: Sustainable Consumption and Branding for Gen Z: How Brand Dimensions Influence Consumer Behavior and Adoption of Newly Launched Technological Products
hot.abstract: Generation Z is emerging as a powerful force in shaping global consumer behavior, particularly in the market of digital and technological products. This study examines how specific branding dimensions, such as online brand experience, engagement, image, trust, loyalty, awareness, behavioral intention, and brand knowledge, influence Gen Z’s purchase intention, emphasizing sustainable consumption. Sustainable consumption, in this context, refers to the preference for tech products that minimize the environmental impact through eco-friendly design, energy efficiency, and responsible sourcing. Using a quantitative approach, this cross-sectional research explores the effects of online brand experience, engagement, image, trust, loyalty, awareness, behavioral intention, and knowledge on purchasing newly launched technological products that align with sustainability. Data were collected from a Gen Z sample using a combination of convenience and systematic sampling, and multiple regression analysis identified the most significant predictors of purchase intention. The results indicate that online brand experience, brand image, brand trust, and brand loyalty play the most crucial roles, having a greater effects on Gen Z’s purchase intention, while brand awareness and knowledge also contribute. However, brand engagement and behavioral intention have weaker effects. These findings suggest that brands targeting Gen Z should prioritize building a strong, trustworthy, and engaging online presence while highlighting their sustainability efforts, and when Gen Z consumers have favorable digital interactions with a brand, perceive its image positively, trust it, and feel loyal to it, they are more likely to consider purchasing its sustainable offerings. This study enhances the understandi

hot.title: Leading in the Digital Age: The Role of Leadership in Organizational Digital Transformation
hot.abstract: In the modern digital age, organizations face unprecedented challenges and possibilities while managing the intricacies of digital transformation. Accelerated technological developments, changing customer preferences, heightened competition, and dynamic regulatory environments necessitate companies to synchronize their business goals with technological innovations. Leadership is crucial in steering businesses through changes, requiring a deep understanding of change processes and the capacity to adjust leadership accordingly. This research addresses the central question: How does leadership effectively promote organizational digital transformation? The study examines how leaders can effectively promote the adoption of advanced technologies and the promotion of innovation, by first exploring the nature of digital transformation within organizations and then analyzing the evolving dynamics of leadership in this context. An integrative review of the Web of Science (WoS) and Scopus databases was conducted, using the search terms: “Leadership” and “Digital Transformation”. The findings emphasize that effective leadership is crucial for managing the minutiae of digital transformation, integrating technology into organizational processes to facilitate learning, collaboration, and agility, enabling companies to adapt to market shifts, reduce uncertainty, and enhance decision-making for sustainable growth. By using the right tools and with the right frequency, leaders may develop team cohesion—even at a distance. Attentive digital-age leaders will know how to leverage the right mechanisms, and herein, we hope to give some indication of how that may be achieved, so that digital transformation increases rather than decreases team motivation levels.
hot.subfield: Organizational Behavior and Human Resource Management

hot.title: The moderating role of personalized recommendations in the trust–satisfaction–loyalty relationship: an empirical study of AI-driven e-commerce
hot.abstract: Purpose This study investigates the effects of trust, satisfaction, and loyalty on AI-driven e-commerce, with a particular focus on how personalized recommendations moderate these relationships. It aims to explore how personalized AI features reshape consumer perceptions and decision-making. Design/methodology/approach A quantitative research approach was used to collect data from a diverse group of e-commerce users who had interacted with AI-based recommendation systems. An online survey employing standardized scales for trust, satisfaction, loyalty, and personalization was administered, and data were analyzed using structural equation modeling (SEM) to test the hypotheses. Findings The study reveals that trust has a significant positive influence on both satisfaction and loyalty. Personalization further strengthens these relationships by moderating the trust–satisfaction–loyalty dynamic. Satisfaction partially mediates the relationship between trust and loyalty, with the model’s explanatory power improving by 5% when personalization is included as a moderator. These results highlight the pivotal role of personalized recommendations in shaping consumer trust and satisfaction in AI-driven e-commerce. Practical implications Businesses can use personalized recommendation systems to enhance trust and satisfaction, thereby fostering loyalty. For example, platforms like Amazon and Netflix have successfully employed personalized AI algorithms to boost customer retention and engagement. Transparency features, such as explaining why certain products are recommended, and cultural sensitivity in algorithm design can further enhance customer trust and acceptance. e-commerce organizations should also invest in data privacy measures and clear algorithms to maintain consumer confiden

hot.title: Factors of Customer Loyalty and Retention in the Digital Environment
hot.venue: Journal of theoretical and applied electronic commerce research
hot.abstract: Customer loyalty and retention are crucial for digital platforms, yet systematic studies integrating technological innovation and loyalty strategies remain scarce. This study addresses this gap by conducting a bibliometric analysis of key factors influencing customer retention in the digital environment. Our research employs a quantitative bibliometric approach using the Biblioshiny and Bibliometrix tools (RStudio 2022.02), analyzing 300 scientific articles from the Web of Science database (2021–2024). This study applies bibliometric techniques such as descriptive metrics, bibliographic coupling, co-citation, and scientific collaboration mapping to identify trends and thematic clusters. Our findings indicate that emerging technologies, including artificial intelligence and big data, significantly impact customer experience, trust, and engagement. Personalization and digital innovation emerge as fundamental drivers of customer retention, offering strategic insights for companies aiming to strengthen competitiveness in the global digital market.

hot.title: Mapping the greenwashing research landscape: a theoretical and field analysis
hot.abstract: This study provides a comprehensive overview of greenwashing research in business and management, focusing on its conceptual and theoretical foundations. Through a systematic literature review of 97 peer-reviewed articles from Scopus and Web of Science, we use bibliometric analysis to map the evolution of greenwashing studies and network analysis and identify four thematic clusters: (1) symbolic management and CSR communication, (2) environmental regulations and institutional complexity, (3) performance and sustainable practices, and (4) marketing, perception, and trust. Additionally, we perform a full-text analysis to map the theoretical frameworks employed across these clusters, revealing the dominance of macro-level theories (e.g., legitimacy, institutional, and stakeholder theories) and their cross-level interactions with meso- and micro-level approaches. By developing a multi-level theoretical framework, we provide a structured approach to understanding greenwashing across different analytical layers. Then, focusing on the theories used to investigate greenwashing, we identify some avenues for future research. This study has practical implications for understanding how greenwashing affects corporate governance, financial performance, and stakeholder trust, providing insights for enhancing transparency and accountability in sustainable business practices.

hot.title: Transformasi Ekonomi Digital dan Evolusi Pola Konsumsi: Tinjauan Literatur tentang Perubahan Perilaku Belanja di Era Internet
hot.abstract: Transformasi ekonomi digital telah mengubah pola konsumsi masyarakat secara fundamental, terutama dengan meningkatnya penggunaan e-commerce, layanan berbasis sharing economy, serta metode pembayaran digital yang semakin mempermudah transaksi. Penelitian ini merupakan tinjauan pustaka dengan pendekatan kualitatif dan analisis deskriptif yang bertujuan untuk mengkaji perubahan perilaku belanja di era internet. Data penelitian diambil dari Google Scholar untuk periode 2015–2025, dengan total 50 artikel yang diseleksi menjadi 24 artikel yang relevan. Hasil penelitian menunjukkan bahwa digitalisasi telah mendorong pergeseran preferensi konsumen dari belanja konvensional ke belanja daring, dengan faktor utama seperti kenyamanan, efisiensi, dan personalisasi layanan. Media sosial dan pemasaran berbasis influencer memainkan peran penting dalam keputusan pembelian, sementara model bisnis baru seperti cloud kitchen dan layanan pesan-antar semakin mengubah pola konsumsi, terutama di industri makanan dan minuman. Namun, fenomena ini juga menghadirkan tantangan, termasuk peningkatan belanja impulsif, risiko keamanan data, dan dampak negatif terhadap sektor ritel tradisional. Implikasi dari penelitian ini menyoroti pentingnya adaptasi bisnis terhadap tren digital, perlunya regulasi yang lebih kuat untuk melindungi konsumen, serta peningkatan literasi digital dan keuangan bagi masyarakat. Penelitian ini memiliki keterbatasan dalam cakupan data sekunder dan tidak menggali aspek demografis atau budaya yang dapat memengaruhi adopsi digitalisasi. Oleh karena itu, studi lanjutan dengan pendekatan empiris diperlukan untuk memperoleh pemahaman yang lebih mendalam mengenai transformasi konsumsi di era digital.

hot.title: Influence of short video content on consumers purchase intentions on social media platforms with trust as a mediator
hot.abstract: Short videos on social media platforms have boomed with the rapid growth of the video consumption industry and have become an important marketing tool for businesses. With the rise of platforms such as TikTok or Douyin, short videos have profoundly impacted consumer behavior, making it crucial to understand their role in shaping consumer purchase intention. However, there is still a need for further research on how short video content promotes consumer purchase intent. Based on the Stimulus-Organism-Response (SOR) model, this study constructs a structural model to explore the impact of short video content on consumer purchase intention, focusing on the mediating role of consumer trust. The model incorporates usefulness, ease of use, and entertainment as external stimuli, consumer trust as internal psychological responses, and purchase intention as the final behavioral outcome. This study collected 372 valid data from Chinese consumers through an online questionnaire and empirically analyzed it using structural equation modeling. The study results show that short-form video content's usefulness, ease of use, and entertainment significantly affect consumers' trust and purchase intention. Moreover, consumer trust positively affects purchase intention and mediates the relationship between short video content and purchase behavior. This research extends the application of the SOR model to the context of social media short videos, highlighting the crucial role of consumer trust in shaping consumer purchase decisions. Based on these findings, we propose actionable strategies for businesses to optimize short video content and build consumer trust, ultimately enhancing marketing effectiveness and driving consumer purchases.

hot.title: The Role of Artificial Intelligence in Personalizing Social Media Marketing Strategies for Enhanced Customer Experience
hot.abstract: This paper explores the role of artificial intelligence (AI) in personalizing social media marketing strategies and its impact on customer experience, with a focus on consumers within the MENA region. Using data collected from an online questionnaire completed by 893 individuals, the study confirms that AI significantly enhances social media marketing by offering personalized content, optimizing influencer selection, and enabling real-time consumer interaction. These capabilities not only increase customer awareness but also improve user experience and purchase intentions. Key AI tools such as influencer marketing, content optimization, and customization are effective in capturing consumer attention, although further research is necessary to deepen understanding. By examining AI's ability to analyze vast datasets and support targeted marketing efforts, the study contributes to both academic and practical discourse, offering insights that businesses can use to refine their AI-driven social media strategies. Ultimately, the research aims to guide marketers through the complexities of AI deployment, ensuring its benefits are fully realized for consumers.

hot.title: Impact of Influencer Marketing on Consumer Behavior and Online Shopping Preferences
hot.venue: Journal of theoretical and applied electronic commerce research
hot.abstract: Influencer marketing has emerged as a crucial element in digital marketing, significantly shaping consumer behavior and online shopping preferences. This study examined the multidimensional impact of influencer marketing by analyzing engagement metrics, marketing effectiveness, and consumer decision-making processes, based on consumers in the Greek sector. Through a structured methodological framework, the research employed a questionnaire-based survey, statistical modeling, and Fuzzy Cognitive Mapping (FCM) scenarios to assess consumer interactions with influencer-driven content. Findings highlight that while influencer marketing enhances brand engagement and sales, its effectiveness varies based on content authenticity, transparency, and user trust. Additionally, consumer purchasing decisions are influenced by social media visibility, personalized marketing strategies, and digital platform usability. This study underscores the need for strategic influencer selection and information-driven marketing optimization to sustain long-term consumer engagement. These insights provide practical implications for businesses aiming to enhance digital marketing strategies and contribute to the ongoing discourse on social commerce and consumer-centric marketing models.
