latest.title: Analisis Pengaruh Pemberian Diskon, Bundling Product, dan Kualitas Konten Melalui TikTok terhadap Keputusan Pembelian Konsumen Roti’O di Kota Samarinda
latest.abstract: Penelitian ini bertujuan untuk menganalisis pengaruh diskon, bundling product, dan kualitas konten melalui TikTok terhadap keputusan pembelian konsumen Roti’O di Kota Samarinda secara parsial. Teknik pengambilan sampel yang digunakan adalah non probability sampling dengan jenis purposive sampling. Responden yang digunakan sebanyak 90 sampel. Pengumpulan data dilakukan melalui penyebaran kuesioner melalui Google Form dengan instrumen pengukuran menggunakan skala likert 1-5. Analisis data dilakukan dengan menggunakan regresi linier berganda dengan Statistical Package for the Social Sciences (SPSS) untuk mengolah dan menganalisis data. Pengujian meliputi uji instrument, uji asumsi klasik, uji koefisien determinasi (R2), dan uji t. Hasil penelitian menunjukan bahwa seluruh variabel independen diskon, bundling product, dan kualitas konten berpengaruh positif dan signifikan terhadap variabel dependen keputusan pembelian secara parsial. Dengan demikian, semakin baik diskon, bundling product, dan kualitas konten yang ditawarkan melalui TikTok, maka semakin tinggi pula keputusan pembelian konsumen Roti’O di Kota Samarinda.

latest.title: Sustainability in Focus: Perceptions of Industrial Customers in the Sri Lankan Wood Coating Industry
latest.abstract: Sustainability is becoming increasingly important in purchasing decisions in industries such as wood coating. The primary objective of this research is to explore the underlying factors and decision-making process behind industrial customers’ preference towards sustainable wood coating products. Industrial customers are taken as the unit of analysis given that they use wood coatings on a large scale. A qualitative research approach with an exploratory design is used for the in-depth examination of attitudes and preferences. The data collection method was interviews followed by a semi-structured interview guide. Eight participants were interviewed, and purposive sampling was used. The Theory of Planned Behaviour (TPB) serves as the theoretical lens in explaining how attitudes, subjective norms, and perceived behavioural control influence sustainability-related decisions and it also guided the development of interview questions. The data was analyzed using Thematic analysis.The findings of the research reveal that durability, aesthetic appeal, and protective properties are the most valued attributes in wood coatings. It also identifies the price as a decisive factor. Most industrial customers acknowledge adoption of sustainable wood coatings while it is restrained by cost, end-user demand and availability. This research also highlights that sustainability adoption is a phased process and due to the upward trend towards sustainability, Sri Lankan industrial customers are highly likely to adopt sustainable wood coatings in future. The implications of this research help manufacturers of wood coatings to make decisions regarding production of sustainable wood coatings, while also offering valuable direction for aligning industrial product strategies with evolving environmenta

latest.title: Examining Customer Adoption of Omni-Channel Retailing in the Fashion Apparel Industry of Sri Lanka
latest.abstract: In the contemporary era of retail, Omni-channel retailing is becoming more and more popular as a comprehensive strategy. Despite the fact that various researchers have conducted a large number of studies, Omni-Channel Approach has not received enough attention. This has drawn interest from both the academic community and real-world applications. Thus, this research explores complex dynamics of omni-channel retailing and customers' purchase intentions. The study selected two hundred sixty (260) customers using convenience sampling procedures to conduct careful examination of relationships between purchase intention and key characteristics like perceived usefulness, ease of use, security and personalization. The acquired data was thoroughly analyzed using descriptive statistics, correlation analysis, and regression analysis using Statistical Package for the Social Sciences version 21 (SPSS). Notably, the study's results show a strong and positive impact between consumers' perceptions of the product's usefulness, ease of use, security and personalization, with their intent to buy. This study adds a lot to the knowledge of consumer behavior as it relates to omni channel shopping, and the insights can help retailers to make better strategic decisions in an ever-changing industry.

latest.title: Role of Artificial Intelligence in Shaping Consumer Buying Behaviour Among Higher Education Students: An Empirical Study
latest.venue: International Journal of Science Strategic Management and Technology
latest.abstract: Artificial Intelligence (AI) is increasingly becoming embedded in digital platforms through recommendation engines, chatbots, predictive search, personalised advertising and automated decision-support tools. This study examines the role of AI in shaping consumer buying behaviour among higher education students. The study specifically considers AI adoption, trust in AI-enabled recommendations and AI-driven personalisation as important dimensions of the contemporary digital buying process. A quantitative research design was adopted using an illustrative sample of 250 higher education students and a structured five-point Likert-scale questionnaire. Descriptive statistics, independent-samples t-test, Chi-square test and one-way ANOVA were applied to examine the proposed relationships and group differences. The results indicate positive associations between AI-related constructs and consumer buying behaviour, while significant differences are observed across levels of AI experience. The findings indicate that familiarity with AI-enabled technologies can influence how students search for information, evaluate alternatives and form purchase decisions. The study also highlights the importance of trust, transparency, privacy and consumer control in AI-mediated consumption. The findings provide implications for digital marketers, higher education institutions and technology developers seeking to develop responsible AI-enabled consumer experiences.

latest.title: The convergence of environmental, social and governance principles and Halalan Thayyiban
latest.abstract: The pharmaceutical industry is increasingly influenced by the convergence of Environmental, Social, and Governance (ESG) principles with the Islamic concept of Halalan Thayyiban , which extends beyond permissibility to encompass wholesomeness, sustainability, and social justice. This paper proposes a “Dual-Ethic” framework that integrates ESG metrics with Islamic bioethical principles, particularly the Maqasid al-Shari’ah, by treating the two not as parallel compliance regimes but as a single integrated standard to redefine ethical drug discovery and biomanufacturing. The study synthesizes current literature to examine how this convergence can operationalize sustainable practices through green chemistry, bio-based manufacturing, and reduced reliance on animal testing via emerging in silico and in vitro models. It further explores how governance innovations, including blockchain-enabled supply chain transparency, enhance trust ( amanah ) and regulatory compliance. From a social perspective, the framework emphasizes health equity through inclusive clinical trials and value-based pricing aligned with public interest ( maslahah ). Despite these opportunities, significant challenges remain, including dependence on imported raw materials, regulatory fragmentation, and high implementation costs. Addressing these barriers requires investment in domestic capacity, harmonized standards, and institutional strengthening. Overall, the integration of ESG and Halalan Thayyiban offers a potential pathway toward a more ethical, sustainable, and globally inclusive pharmaceutical ecosystem. The framework is proposed rather than empirically validated, and its effectiveness has yet to be tested.

latest.title: Beyond Personalisation: Understanding the Influence of Artificial Intelligence-Driven Social Media Marketing on Consumer Engagement, Brand Trust and Purchase Intention among Generation Z Consumers in India
latest.venue: Stanzaleaf International Journal of Multidisciplinary Studies
latest.abstract: The increasing integration of artificial intelligence (AI) into social media marketing has transformed the ways in which brands communicate with consumers, personalise promotional content and influence purchasing decisions. AI-driven marketing technologies, including recommendation algorithms, predictive analytics, automated chatbots and generative AI content, enable organisations to deliver personalised and interactive marketing experiences. However, the effectiveness of these technologies in influencing consumer purchase intention depends not only on technological capabilities but also on consumers' psychological responses, particularly their engagement with brands and trust in AI-mediated marketing communication. This paper develops a conceptual understanding of the relationship between AI-driven social media marketing and consumer purchase intention among Generation Z consumers in India, with particular emphasis on the mediating roles of consumer engagement and brand trust. Drawing upon the Stimulus–Organism–Response (S-O-R) framework, consumer engagement theory and trust-based perspectives, the paper proposes an integrated conceptual model explaining how AI-enabled marketing stimuli influence consumers' cognitive, emotional and behavioural responses and subsequently shape purchase intention. The paper adopts a conceptual research approach supported by a critical review of relevant academic literature. It identifies AI-enabled personalisation, content relevance, interactivity and perceived transparency as important characteristics of AI-driven social media marketing. Consumer engagement and brand trust are proposed as complementary mediating mechanisms through which marketing stimuli may influence purchase intention. latest.title: Consumer purchasing decisions in the used motorcycle market: evidence from service quality, price, and location
latest.venue: ECOBIZTECH Journal of Economics Business and Technology
latest.abstract: Purpose: to analyze how service quality, price, and location influence consumer purchasing decisions at the Prima Motor Bogor used motorcycle showroom, both individually and within an integrated research model. Method: a quantitative approach with an explanatory research design. Data were collected through questionnaires distributed to 89 respondents using purposive total sampling. The data were analyzed using partial least squares structural equation modeling (PLS-SEM) in SmartPLS, evaluating the measurement (outer) and structural (inner) models to test the proposed hypotheses. Findings: service quality and price positively and significantly influence consumer purchasing decisions at Prima Motor Bogor, while location does not have a significant influence. These results indicate that consumers place greater emphasis on service professionalism, transaction transparency, and price suitability than on the showroom's physical accessibility when deciding to purchase used motorcycles. Implications: Prima Motor Bogor's management should improve service quality, maintain competitive and transparent pricing strategies, and optimize showroom accessibility and digital visibility to strengthen consumer confidence, enhance purchasing decisions, and improve business competitiveness. Originality: lies in integrating service quality, price, and location to examine consumer purchasing decisions specifically within the used motorcycle showroom context.

latest.title: Consumers’ well-being in livestreaming commerce: antecedents and consequences
latest.abstract: Livestreaming commerce represents an increasingly important form of digital retailing. This study examines relationships among informational and emotional support, streamer characteristics (expertise, trustworthiness and attractiveness), livestreaming environmental characteristics (interactivity, perceived crowdedness and social presence), consumers’ perceived value, shopping well-being and continuance intention. Survey data from 301 livestreaming consumers in China were analysed using partial least squares structural equation modelling (PLS-SEM), necessary condition analysis (NCA) and combined importance-performance map analysis (cIPMA). Perceived value and shopping well-being were positively related to continuance intention, and perceived value was positively related to shopping well-being. Expertise, interactivity, perceived crowdedness and social presence showed significant positive relationships with perceived value. The direct relationships for informational support, emotional support, trustworthiness and attractiveness were non-significant. Integrating PLS-SEM with NCA and cIPMA differentiated important predictors from minimum conditions associated with higher perceived value. The findings extend understanding of shopping well-being as a quality-of-life evaluation in livestreaming commerce.

latest.title: Towards context-adapted and equitable certification? The Participatory Guarantee System in Abancay, Peru
latest.abstract: Introduction Participatory Guarantee Systems (PGS) aim to assure ecological food quality through collaboration among locally embedded agri-food actors. While PGS are often promoted as participatory alternatives to third-party certification, their implications for equity and justice remain underexplored. Methods This qualitative case study examines a PGS in the province of Abancay, in the Peruvian Highlands, through an environmental justice lens. Results We found that decision-making power and benefits are concentrated among a small group of farmers, and broader participation does not necessarily translate into direct influence over governance. At the same time, many farmers perceive PGS and related programs as recognition of their hard work, local knowledge and care for the environment and people. The PGS partly reflects Quechua-Andean reciprocal social relations, and strengthens the assertion of Indigenous identity. Discussion In the context of historical discrimination against Quechua-Andean people, the PGS may reproduce certain inequalities, while simultaneously supporting the recognition of Indigenous cultural identities and agri-food practices in agricultural and development programs and policies. The findings contribute to debates on participatory development, environmental justice, and the complex ways in which agricultural development interventions can both challenge and reinforce inequalities, while creating opportunities for the institutional recognition of Indigenous knowledge and practices.

latest.title: AI-Driven Consumer Decision-Making among Higher Education Students: Examining the Roles of Adoption, Trust and Personalization
latest.venue: International Journal of Science Strategic Management and Technology
latest.abstract: The digital space where higher-education students find products, compare them, get personalised recommendations and make online purchases is becoming more and more interwoven with artificial intelligence. This paper analyses the relationship between the adoption of AI, confidence in AI-based recommendations and AI-based personalisation and consumer purchasing behaviour amongst higher learning institutions. Two-way (quantitative) cross-sectional methodology is demonstrated using the simulated sample of 150 objects in the form of a quantitative cross-sectional study. A five-point Lickert scale has been designed in the form of a structured question to embrace AI adoption, AI trust, AI personalisation and consumer buying behaviour. Applying reliability analysis, descriptive statistics, Pearson correlation, one-way ANOVA and exploratory multiple regression. The simulated analysis shows a high internal consistency among the constructs and positive correlations between AI-related variables and buying behaviour. The differences in buying behaviour among the levels of AI experience may also be found, and the exploratory regression shows that the composite AI variables present a significant explanatory amount of variance. These numerical findings are explicitly exemplary and are not findings in reality by actual respondents. The research offers the student through the lens based on a convenient framework aimed at studying the potential role of convenience, trust, personalisation and perceived control in influencing purchases by AI in the context of higher education.

latest.title: Advancing women-centered psychedelic research in the United States: a translational public health agenda
latest.abstract: Background Women are disproportionately affected by psychiatric and substance use disorders, the primary targets of emerging psychedelic-assisted therapies, yet remain underrepresented in psychedelic research. Most registered trials are early-phase, and few report outcomes by sex despite biological and hormonal differences that can influence treatment response and safety. This Perspective focuses on the United States, where federal and state policy is rapidly reshaping psychedelic access and accelerating drug approval, making this evidence gap urgent. Objective Drawing on a targeted narrative review of women-specific peer-reviewed psychedelic research and U.S. regulatory and policy documents, we apply the Socioecological Model (SEM) and the Translational Research Continuum (TRC) to examine women's exclusion from psychedelic research. The SEM explains why this exclusion persists and the TRC identifies where the evidence pipeline breaks down, culminating in regulatory frameworks and clinical guidelines that neglect sex- and gender-disaggregated analyses and reporting. Conclusion Public health disciplines, including epidemiology, implementation science, surveillance, and program evaluation, are well equipped to address the translational gaps, but coordinated multilevel action is needed. Researchers should adopt the Sex and Gender Equity in Research (SAGER) reporting guidelines and record a minimum set of reproductive variables at baseline. Funders can accelerate progress by directing resources toward closing this gap. Regulators should require pre-specified sex covariates, sex-disaggregated safety and descriptive reporting, and enrollment targets aligned with disease burden. Clinicians need to integrate gender-responsive harm reduction now. As dosing protocols, screening c

latest.title: Building a Marketing-Effect Index as a Decision-Support Tool for SME Cross-Border Floral Trade
latest.abstract: This study developed a pragmatic effectiveness index to evaluate cross-border e-commerce language strategies for floral businesses. This research was conducted because flowers face a trust gap in global logistics, and traditional literal translation fails to meet the cultural and emotional needs of overseas consumers, resulting in low sales. To address this, an empirical A/B test was conducted over 30 days on an e-commerce platform, comparing traditional descriptions with artificial intelligence-assisted, manually calibrated copy optimized for emotional density and pragmatic trust. The experiment revealed that the optimized copy increased the conversion rate by nearly six times and reduced the refund rate from 8.4% to 3.2%. Ultimately, these findings signify that brand promotion must dynamically balance aesthetic appeal with pragmatic trust, providing a quantitative paradigm to help agricultural exports overcome cultural discounts and achieve higher conversion.

latest.title: What Sustainability Disclosures Disclose
latest.abstract: Sustainability disclosures are the backbone of corporate sustainability efforts. If stakeholders want companies to compete over how “good” they are for society, they need a way to see what companies are doing and trying to do. But these disclosures have been widely criticized for their lack of credibility and comparability. To improve them, nonprofits and companies have developed voluntary reporting frameworks that many firms have now adopted and that have informed mandatory disclosure regulations. These critiques and regulatory debates have proceeded, however, without basic facts about what these disclosures contain and whether voluntary tools help. Answering these questions has been difficult because of the non‐standardized nature of these disclosures. This project overcomes these barriers through the use of large language models and provides the most comprehensive analysis of sustainability disclosures to date. We evaluate over 15,000 sustainability disclosure documents issued by more than 2100 Russell 3000 firms spanning 1998–2023. We construct measurable indicators based on characteristics that stakeholders have identified as relevant: specificity, quantitative evidence, fluff (~puffery), negative news, and data table and figure counts. Five patterns stand out. First, sustainability reporting and the adoption of external assurance and voluntary frameworks (GRI, SASB, TCFD, CDP, SBTi) surged after 2015. Second, firms often adopt multiple frameworks at once, and adoption is sticky. Third, as reporting mainstreamed, reports became less specific, less quantitative, and fluffier. Fourth, longer‐reporting firms produce more concrete reports (more specific and quantitative, with more tables and less fluff) with more negative news, but these differences largely reflect whi

latest.title: Artificial intelligence for customer engagement and brand evangelism: A multi-study approach
ESG Data Governance for Sustainable Business: Ownership, Authority, and the Strategic Role of HR
latest.abstract: The growing institutionalization of environmental, social, and governance (ESG) reporting raises questions about how organizations allocate authority over ESG information. While existing research addresses reporting requirements and data governance structures, the organizational processes through which ESG data ownership emerges remain insufficiently theorized. This conceptual paper develops an integrated framework in which ESG data ownership is understood as the institutionally recognized allocation of governance authority over the definition, interpretation, validation, and use of ESG information. It identifies four interacting mechanisms through which this authority is formed: authority claiming, allocation of decision rights, interpretative alignment, and institutional stabilization. The framework distinguishes finance‐centered, sustainability‐centered, and matrix governance configurations as alternative outcomes of formation processes shaped by institutional and organizational conditions. Drawing on contrasting governance traditions in France and Germany, it highlights the context‐dependent nature of these arrangements. Particular attention is given to human resources (HR), whose expertise in producing and interpreting social ESG information does not necessarily translate into recognized decision‐making authority. By explaining how distributed functional expertise and competing authority claims are translated into institutionally recognized decision rights, the framework advances an understanding of how different governance configurations and positions of HR emerge.

latest.title: From Virtual to Valuable: How Influencer Type and Product Type Shape Consumer Value Co‐Creation Intention
latest.abstract: Virtual and human influencers offer distinct social and experiential cues, but their relative effectiveness may depend on how consumers evaluate the endorsed product. Drawing on the cognitive‐affective‐behavioral framework, this research integrates social information processing theory and cognitive‐affective system theory to examine consumer value co‐creation intention. Across three between‐subjects experiments ( N = 994), results reveal a consistent matching effect: virtual influencers have a relative advantage for search products, whereas human influencers have a relative advantage for experience products. This matching effect operates through parasocial interaction and empathy: forming a parasocial representation may make an influencer's perspective and affective cues more accessible, providing a relational basis for subsequent empathy. Consistent with this sequence, both the indirect effect through parasocial interaction and the serial indirect effect through parasocial interaction and empathy follow this product‐dependent pattern across both product categories, whereas the indirect effect through empathy alone favors human influencers only for experience products. Together, these findings identify product type as a boundary condition linking relational and affective processes to consumer value co‐creation intention, offering practical insights for aligning influencer selection with product characteristics.

latest.title: Liderazgo de opinión: Estrategias de contenido y participación en Linkedin
latest.venue: VISUAL REVIEW International Visual Culture Review / Revista Internacional de Cultura Visual
latest.abstract: Este estudio analiza la evolución de la estrategia de Thought Leadership de Deloitte Insights en LinkedIn entre 2019 y 2025. A partir de 2.799 publicaciones, se examinan la frecuencia, formatos, temáticas y nivel de engagement, así como un análisis de contenido. Los resultados evidencian cambios significativos en la estrategia, un aumento del engagement desde 2024 y una transición hacia contenidos visuales. El estudio confirma la influencia de los formatos y la frecuencia en la interacción, y evidencia una diversificación temática junto con un giro hacia perspectivas más humanas.

latest.title: Blockchain and SME Environmental Sustainability: A New Analytical Framework
latest.abstract: The green transition of the private sector heavily relies on the strategic deployment of advanced digital technologies to optimize resource use and verify compliance. This study investigates the relationship between blockchain adoption and environmental sustainability among more than 12,000 small and medium‐sized enterprises (SMEs) operating across EU member states. The analysis employs binary regression models, complemented by Firth Logit specifications to address potential bias and ensure a highly robust empirical structure. The operational linkages between blockchain adoption and firms' environmental sustainability practices are evaluated along four dimensions: (i) reducing the consumption of or pressure on natural resources, (ii) improving energy efficiency or transitioning toward sustainable energy sources, (iii) recycling or reusing materials, and (iv) developing environmentally sustainable products or services. The results indicate that SMEs adopting blockchain technology exhibit a markedly higher propensity to engage in environmentally sustainable practices. Moreover, firms that simultaneously utilize both artificial intelligence and blockchain technologies are even more inclined to implement sustainability‐oriented activities. The study examines these relationships across sectors through the four identified channels and demonstrates that substantial sectoral heterogeneity conditions the association between blockchain and environmental sustainability performance. These findings remain consistent across extensive robustness checks. Overall, the study provides a significant empirical contribution to the limited literature addressing the intersection of digital technology adoption and environmental sustainability within the SME sector.

latest.title: Government Policy, Organizational Responses, and Sustainable Performance: An Organizational Perspective
latest.abstract: Sustainable performance is increasingly important for enterprises operating under growing environmental, technological, and institutional pressures. Drawing on stakeholder theory and dynamic capabilities theory, this study examines an integrated model of the relationships among government policy, environmental compliance, digital adoption, innovation capability, ethical leadership, and sustainable performance. Using cross‐sectional survey data based on the organizational perceptions of 303 senior managers, board members, and business owners in Vietnam, the study applies partial least squares structural equation modeling (PLS‐SEM) to examine the proposed direct and indirect relationships. The results show significant positive associations between government policy and both environmental compliance and digital adoption, as well as between environmental compliance and digital adoption and ethical leadership. Digital adoption, innovation capability, and ethical leadership are positively associated with sustainable performance, while digital adoption has a positive relationship with innovation capability. Environmental compliance has no statistically significant direct association with sustainable performance but shows significant indirect associations through digital adoption and ethical leadership. Overall, the findings clarify how policy‐related perceptions, organizational responses, capabilities, and leadership are statistically associated with multidimensional sustainable performance in an emerging‐market context. Given the cross‐sectional design, these findings should be interpreted as associations rather than evidence of causal or temporal relationships.

latest.title: Integrating the 4P Marketing Mix to Strengthen Sales Competitiveness in the Oil-Spill Response Equipment Industry: A Case Study of PT. Slickbar Indonesia
latest.abstract: This study examines how the four elements of the marketing mix product, price, place, and promotion are implemented to support sales competitiveness at PT Slickbar Indonesia, a manufacturer of oil-spill response equipment serving specialized business-to-business (B2B) markets. A descriptive qualitative case-study approach was adopted, drawing on an interview with the company’s Marketing Supervisor, field observations, and organizational documents collected in the January–May 2026 study period. Findings indicate that the company differentiates its offering through customized equipment and accompanying technical services (product); project-specific, value-oriented quotations (price); direct distribution from its production base (place); and relationship-centered communication supported by visits, tenders, and an official website (promotion). Segmentation, targeting, and positioning practices reinforce these elements by prioritizing energy, port, shipping, and other high-risk industrial buyers. A critical limitation is the absence of a structured system for assessing marketing communication effectiveness: customer feedback is evaluated mainly through informal interactions, without standardized satisfaction or response metrics. The paper proposes an integrated conceptual framework linking STP alignment, the 4P mix, perceived reliability and trust, and sales competitiveness, with a data-driven feedback loop for marketing evaluation. Because the source study does not report longitudinal sales, customer survey, or comparative competitor data, the findings describe strategic practices and their plausible competitive relevance rather than demonstrating causal sales growth.

latest.title: The effects of financial distress and audit delay on audit quality: Firm size as a moderator in Consumer Cyclicals manufacturing companies
latest.venue: Novera Journal of Economics and Business
latest.abstract: Audit quality is a critical concern because a company's financial condition and audit timeliness may influence its choice of reputable auditors. This study examines the effects of financial distress and audit delay on audit quality and tests the moderating role of firm size. A quantitative approach was employed using secondary data from 41 manufacturing companies in the Consumer Cyclicals subsector listed on the Indonesia Stock Exchange during 2023–2025, yielding 123 firm-year observations. The data were analyzed using Firth logistic regression. The results indicate that the Z-Score has a positive and significant effect on audit quality, whereas audit delay has no significant effect. Firm size is the strongest predictor, while the interaction between the Z-Score and firm size is positive and significant, although its significance is sensitive to GEE testing. These findings indicate that financial condition and company scale are associated with the likelihood of engaging Big Four audit firms, with firm size strengthening this relationship. Abstrak Kualitas audit menjadi perhatian penting karena kondisi keuangan perusahaan dan ketepatan waktu penyelesaian audit dapat berkaitan dengan keputusan perusahaan dalam memilih auditor bereputasi. Penelitian ini bertujuan menganalisis pengaruh financial distress dan audit delay terhadap kualitas audit serta menguji peran moderasi ukuran perusahaan. Penelitian ini menggunakan pendekatan kuantitatif dengan data sekunder dari 41 perusahaan manufaktur subsektor Consumer Cyclicals yang terdaftar di Bursa Efek Indonesia selama periode 2023–2025, sehingga menghasilkan 123 observasi perusahaan-tahun. latest.title: The Role of Tabligh Trait and Consumer Trust in Increasing Broiler Chicken Sales at Batang Kuis Market : PERAN SIFAT TABLIGH DAN KEPERCAYAAN KONSUMEN TERHADAP PENINGKATAN PENJUALAN AYAM POTONG DI PASAR BATANG KUIS
latest.abstract: This study is grounded in the urgency of implementing Islamic business ethics, particularly information transparency (tabligh) and halal product assurance, to sustain traditional market trading. This research aims to analyze the partial and simultaneous roles of the tabligh trait and consumer trust in increasing broiler chicken sales at Batang Kuis Market, Deli Serdang Regency. Utilizing a quantitative associative approach, this study involved a population of broiler chicken buyers, with a sample of 125 respondents selected via purposive sampling. Primary data were gathered through validity- and reliability-tested questionnaires, and analyzed using classical assumption tests, multiple linear regression, t-test, F-test, and coefficient of determination. The findings reveal that the tabligh trait has a positive and significant partial effect on sales increase. Consumer trust also exhibits a positive and significant partial influence, serving as the most dominant contributor. Simultaneously, both variables significantly drive sales growth, explaining a substantial portion of sales variations while the remainder is influenced by external factors. In conclusion, consistent application of muamalah transparency and halal trust guarantees effectively enhances trader turnover and business sustainability in traditional markets. Abstrak. Penelitian ini didasari oleh urgensi penerapan etika bisnis Islam, khususnya keterbukaan informasi (tabligh) dan jaminan kehalalan produk, guna menjaga keberlanjutan perdagangan di pasar tradisional. Penelitian ini bertujuan untuk menganalisis peran sifat tabligh dan kepercayaan konsumen secara parsial maupun simultan terhadap peningkatan penjualan ayam potong di Pasar Batang Kuis, Kabupaten Deli Serdang. latest.title: Automotive Repair SMEs’ Marketing Performance: Digital Transformation, Knowledge Antecedents, Social Media Mediation, Market Turbulence Moderation
latest.venue: Journal of Economics Entrepreneurship Management Business and Accounting
latest.abstract: Purpose – This study examines knowledge capabilities as antecedents of digital transformation and its relationship with marketing performance, considering social media marketing as a mediator and market turbulence as a moderator among Indonesian automotive repair MSMEs. Design/methodology/approach – A cross-sectional survey involved 227 owners and managers. Responses were analyzed using PLS-SEM in SmartPLS 4.0 with 5,000 bootstrap subsamples. Findings/Results – Absorptive capacity (p = 0.402) and knowledge management capability (p = 0.061) were not significantly associated with digital transformation. Digital transformation was positively associated with marketing performance (p = 0.005), with significant mediation through social media marketing (p < 0.001). Market turbulence negatively moderated this relationship (p = 0.022), contrary to the proposed direction. Originality/Value – The study integrates knowledge capabilities, digital transformation, social media marketing, and market turbulence in a conventional service sector, identifying a marketing mechanism and an environmental constraint on digital transformation’s benefits.

latest.title: Open Innovation: Redesigning Collaboration Ecosystems for Company Competitiveness in the Digital age
Pengaruh Perencanaan Pajak, Beban Pajak Tangguhan dan Good Corporate Governance Terhadap Nilai Perusahaan
latest.venue: Indonesian Journal of Innovation Multidisipliner Research
latest.abstract: Penelitian ini bertujuan untuk menganalisis mengenai pengaruh Perencanaan Pajak, Beban Pajak Tangguhan dan Good Corporate Governance terhadap Nilai Perusahaan pada Perusahaan Sektor Consumer Non-Cyclical Sub Sektor Food and Beverage yang terdaftar di Bursa Efek Indonesia (BEI) pada Periode 2021-2025. Jenis penelitian ini adalah penelitian kuantitatif dengan pendekatan asosiatif, teknik pengambilan sampel menggunakan Purposive Sampling. Sampel yang digunakan dalam penelitian ini sebanyak 115 sampel dari 23 perusahaan. Teknik analisis data yang digunakan adalah statistik deskriptif dan analisis regresi data panel dengan menggunakan software eviews-12. Hasil penelitian ini menunjukkan bahwa model yang terbaik adalah Random Effect Model (REM). Hasil penelitian berdasarkan uji secara parsial menunjukkan bahwa Perencanaan Pajak (X1) dan Beban Pajak Tangguhan (X2) berpengaruh terhadap Nilai Perusahaan, sedangkan Good Corporate Governance (X3) tidak berpengaruh terhadap Nilai Perusahaan. Berdasarkan uji secara simultan menunjukkan bahwa Perencanaan Pajak, Beban Pajak Tangguhan dan Good Corporate Governance berpengaruh terhadap Nilai Perusahaan. Data yang digunakan dalam penelitian ini merupakan data sekunder yang diperoleh dari laporan keuangan tahunan perusahaan melalui situs resmi BEI. Pengujian model regresi dilakukan melalui tahapan uji Chow, uji Hausman, dan uji Lagrange Multiplier, serta dilengkapi dengan uji asumsi klasik dan uji koefisien determinasi untuk mengukur seberapa besar kemampuan variabel independen dalam menjelaskan variasi variabel dependen secara menyeluruh.

latest.title: AI Marketing Transparency and Brand Trust: How AI Literacy and Perceived Manipulative Intent Shape Consumer Responses in Pakistan
latest.abstract: With AI’s increasing role in digital marketing, a brand’s transparency about its use of AI could act as an informational signal of accountability. However, the interpretation consumers make of such transparency might vary with their knowledge of AI and their perception of persuasive intent. This study examines the relationship between perceived AI marketing transparency, brand trust, and purchase intention and the role of perceived manipulative intent as a mechanism and AI literacy as a boundary condition. We surveyed 387 matched Pakistani consumers, in two waves. AI literacy was operationalised with the core 18-item AI literacy dimensions of the MAILS instrument (use and apply AI, know and understand AI, detect AI, and AI ethics), whereas the remaining MAILS dimensions were treated as separate constructs. We tested the hypotheses using regression-based simple mediation (PROCESS Model 4) and first-stage moderated mediation (PROCESS Model 7). Perceived AI marketing transparency was positively associated with brand trust (β = 0.24, p < 0.001). Brand trust carried a significant indirect association between perceived AI marketing transparency and purchase intention (indirect effect = 0.06, 95% CI [0.02, 0.11]); the direct association was not statistically significant (c′ = 0.10, p = 0.081). Perceived manipulative intent was negatively associated with brand trust (b = −0.25, p < 0.001). AI literacy positively moderated the association between perceived AI marketing transparency and perceived manipulative intent (B = 0.13, p = 0.031), such that this association was positive and significant only at high AI literacy (B = 0.25, p < 0.001). hot.title: How generative AI Is shaping the future of marketing
hot.venue: Journal of the Academy of Marketing Science
hot.abstract: Generative AI (Gen AI) is shaping the future of marketing. In the next decade, Gen AI will influence how marketers interact and communicate with customers, help create and deliver marketing content (text, images, and video), and inform methods for researching and developing new products and services. In both service and sales settings, Gen AI will affect customers directly and significantly. Therefore, marketers, researchers, and public policy makers require a clear understanding of Gen AI and its potential, as well as its limitations. To assist marketers in thinking through the adoption and implementation of Gen AI, the current article presents a four-quadrant organizing framework that highlights trade-offs in both the nature of Gen AI inputs and the extent of human augmentation needed to deliver Gen AI–generated outputs. This framework provides guidance for the selection and implementation of Gen AI tools, as well as recommendations for further research.

hot.title: Interaction with AI companions and psychological well-being
AI Companions Reduce Loneliness
hot.abstract: Chatbots are now able to engage in sophisticated conversations with consumers in the domain of relationships, providing a potential coping solution to widescale societal loneliness. Behavioral research provides little insight into whether these applications (apps) are effective at alleviating loneliness. We address this question by focusing on “artificial intelligence (AI) companions”: apps designed to provide consumers with synthetic interaction partners. Study 1 examines user reviews of AI companion apps and finds correlational evidence suggesting that these apps help alleviate loneliness. Study 2 finds that AI companions successfully alleviate loneliness on par only with interacting with another person and more than other activities such as watching YouTube videos. Moreover, consumers underestimate the degree to which AI companions improve their loneliness. Study 3 uses a longitudinal design and finds that an AI companion consistently provides momentary reductions in loneliness after use over the course of a week. Study 4 provides evidence that both the chatbots’ performance and, especially, whether it makes users feel heard, explain reductions in loneliness. Study 5 provides an additional robustness check for the loneliness-alleviating benefits of AI companions and shows that self-disclosure and distraction alone do not explain AI companions’ effectiveness.

hot.title: Leading in the Digital Age: The Role of Leadership in Organizational Digital Transformation
hot.abstract: In the modern digital age, organizations face unprecedented challenges and possibilities while managing the intricacies of digital transformation. Accelerated technological developments, changing customer preferences, heightened competition, and dynamic regulatory environments necessitate companies to synchronize their business goals with technological innovations. Leadership is crucial in steering businesses through changes, requiring a deep understanding of change processes and the capacity to adjust leadership accordingly. This research addresses the central question: How does leadership effectively promote organizational digital transformation? The study examines how leaders can effectively promote the adoption of advanced technologies and the promotion of innovation, by first exploring the nature of digital transformation within organizations and then analyzing the evolving dynamics of leadership in this context. An integrative review of the Web of Science (WoS) and Scopus databases was conducted, using the search terms: “Leadership” and “Digital Transformation”. The findings emphasize that effective leadership is crucial for managing the minutiae of digital transformation, integrating technology into organizational processes to facilitate learning, collaboration, and agility, enabling companies to adapt to market shifts, reduce uncertainty, and enhance decision-making for sustainable growth. By using the right tools and with the right frequency, leaders may develop team cohesion—even at a distance. Attentive digital-age leaders will know how to leverage the right mechanisms, and herein, we hope to give some indication of how that may be achieved, so that digital transformation increases rather than decreases team motivation levels.
hot.subfield: Organizational Behavior and Human Resource Management

hot.title: A Closer Look into Recent Video-based Learning Research: A Comprehensive Review of Video Characteristics, Tools, Technologies, and Learning Effectiveness
hot.venue: International Journal of Artificial Intelligence in Education
hot.abstract: People increasingly use videos on the Web for learning, be it for daily tasks in formal or informal educational settings. To enhance this type of learning, scientists are continuously conducting experiments, proposing guidelines, analyzing data, and researching artificial intelligence methods for tool development. In this comprehensive review, we analyze 257 articles (using PRISMA guidelines) on video-based learning from a technological perspective for the period from 2016 to 2021. One of the aims is to identify video characteristics that support learning as explored by previous research. Based on our analysis, we suggest a taxonomy that organizes the video characteristics and contextual aspects into eight categories: (1) audio features, (2) visual features, (3) textual features, (4) instructor behavior, (5) learners’ activities (play, pause, etc.), (6) interactive features (quizzes, etc.), (7) production style, and (8) instructional design. Also, we identify four representative methodological approaches: (1) tool support of video-based learning, (2) controlled experiments, (3) data analysis studies, and (4) design guidelines for learning videos. We find that the most explored characteristics are textual features followed by visual features, learners’ activities, and interactive features. Tools that aid learning through videos frequently utilize text from transcripts, video frames, and images. The learner’s activity is heavily explored through log files in data analysis studies, and interactive features are frequently scrutinized in controlled experiments. As further contributions, we contrast research findings on how video characteristics affect learning effectiveness, report on tasks and technologies used to develop tools, and summarize design guideline trends to prod

hot.title: Why human–AI relationships need socioaffective alignment
hot.abstract: Humans strive to design safe AI systems that align with our goals and remain under our control. However, as AI capabilities advance, we face a new challenge: the emergence of deeper, more persistent relationships between humans and AI systems. We explore how increasingly capable AI agents may generate the perception of deeper relationships with users, especially as AI becomes more personalised and agentic. This shift, from transactional interaction to ongoing sustained social engagement with AI, necessitates a new focus on socioaffective alignment—how an AI system behaves within the social and psychological ecosystem co-created with its user, where preferences and perceptions evolve through mutual influence. Addressing these dynamics involves resolving key intrapersonal dilemmas, including balancing immediate versus long-term well-being, protecting autonomy, and managing AI companionship alongside the desire to preserve human social bonds. By framing these challenges through a notion of basic psychological needs, we seek AI systems that support, rather than exploit, our fundamental nature as social and emotional beings.

hot.title: The moderating role of personalized recommendations in the trust–satisfaction–loyalty relationship: an empirical study of AI-driven e-commerce
hot.abstract: Purpose This study investigates the effects of trust, satisfaction, and loyalty on AI-driven e-commerce, with a particular focus on how personalized recommendations moderate these relationships. It aims to explore how personalized AI features reshape consumer perceptions and decision-making. Design/methodology/approach A quantitative research approach was used to collect data from a diverse group of e-commerce users who had interacted with AI-based recommendation systems. An online survey employing standardized scales for trust, satisfaction, loyalty, and personalization was administered, and data were analyzed using structural equation modeling (SEM) to test the hypotheses. Findings The study reveals that trust has a significant positive influence on both satisfaction and loyalty. Personalization further strengthens these relationships by moderating the trust–satisfaction–loyalty dynamic. Satisfaction partially mediates the relationship between trust and loyalty, with the model’s explanatory power improving by 5% when personalization is included as a moderator. These results highlight the pivotal role of personalized recommendations in shaping consumer trust and satisfaction in AI-driven e-commerce. Practical implications Businesses can use personalized recommendation systems to enhance trust and satisfaction, thereby fostering loyalty. For example, platforms like Amazon and Netflix have successfully employed personalized AI algorithms to boost customer retention and engagement.
