latest.title: Klasterisasi Karakteristik Pengguna E-Commerce Berdasarkan Profil Pengguna Menggunakan Algoritma K-Prototypes
latest.abstract: Accurate customer segmentation supports more personalized e-commerce marketing. However, the Recency, Frequency, Monetary (RFM) model focuses on transaction history and may not fully capture shopping motivation or the share of a consumer’s spending allocated to e-commerce (Share of Wallet/SoW). This study aims to cluster e-commerce users based on transaction profiles and consumer behavior using the K-Prototypes algorithm. Data were collected from 198 e-commerce users in Palembang, Indonesia. The clustering variables included RFM, SoW, shopping motivation, and product-category preferences, while age category was used for follow-up analysis. The Elbow Method and Silhouette Score supported a four-cluster solution. The resulting personas were High-Value Promo Hunters, Routine Pragmatic Shoppers, Passive Micro-Spenders, and Urgent Big-Ticket Buyers. The Chi-square test indicated a significant association between age category and persona, with Cramér’s V of 0.274. This suggests that age is associated with shopping patterns but does not fully determine consumer profiles. The findings can inform more targeted promotions and user-experience design. The study is limited to 198 respondents from Palembang, so the findings may not represent e-commerce users in other regions.

latest.title: Pengaruh Green Innovation Terhadap Purchase Intention Melalui Environmental Awareness dan Green Brand Image Pada Konsumen Muda Kopi Janji Jiwa di Samarinda
latest.abstract: This study examines the effect of Green Innovation on Purchase Intention through Environmental Awareness and Green Brand Image among young Kopi Janji Jiwa consumers in Samarinda. A quantitative approach with a cross-sectional design was employed using the Stimulus-Organism-Response (S-O-R) framework. Data were collected through questionnaires from 360 respondents aged 17–30 who had purchased Kopi Janji Jiwa at an outlet in Samarinda within the previous six months. Data were analyzed using Partial Least Squares-Structural Equation Modeling (PLS-SEM) with SmartPLS 4. The study's novelty lies in examining Environmental Awareness and Green Brand Image as parallel mediators in a single model. The results indicate that Green Innovation positively and significantly affects Environmental Awareness, Green Brand Image, and Purchase Intention. Both mediators also positively and significantly affect Purchase Intention and mediate the relationship between Green Innovation and Purchase Intention. The indirect effect through Green Brand Image is greater than that through Environmental Awareness. These findings suggest that Kopi Janji Jiwa should strengthen environmentally friendly innovations and communicate sustainability practices transparently to build a credible green brand image and support purchase intention among young consumers.

latest.title: Pengaruh Personalisasi Rekomendasi Produk Terhadap Perilaku Pembelian Konsumen Dengan Trust Sebagai Variabel Mediasi Pada Pengguna Shopee
latest.abstract: Product recommendation personalization helps e-commerce platform users find products that match their needs and preferences. This study examines the effect of Product Recommendation Personalization on Trust, the effect of Trust on Purchase Behavior, and the mediating role of Trust among Shopee users based on the Stimulus–Organism–Response (S-O-R) framework. A quantitative approach with a cross-sectional design was employed. Data were collected through an online questionnaire using purposive sampling, resulting in 111 eligible respondents, comprising 72.07% male and 27.93% female respondents aged 14–69 years. The data were analyzed using Partial Least Squares Structural Equation Modeling (PLS-SEM) in SmartPLS 4 with 5,000 bootstrap subsamples. The results indicate that Product Recommendation Personalization has a positive and significant effect on Trust (β = 0.696; p < 0.001). Trust also has a positive and significant effect on Purchase Behavior (β = 0.719; p < 0.001). The indirect effect of Product Recommendation Personalization on Purchase Behavior through Trust is also significant (β = 0.501; p < 0.001), confirming the mediating role of Trust. These findings support the S-O-R mechanism and highlight the importance of recommendation relevance and user trust in supporting online purchasing behavior.

latest.title: Pengaruh Ulasan Pelanggan Online dan Persepsi Harga terhadap Niat Beli Konsumen Sudut Kedai di Metland Transyogi
latest.abstract: A sharp increase in menu prices at Sudut Kedai, coupled with shifting customer engagement online, raises a fundamental question: do online reviews and price perception actually influence purchase intention? This study examines both factors among Sudut Kedai consumers in Metland Transyogi. Questionnaires were distributed to 120 respondents who had read online reviews of Sudut Kedai, selected through convenience sampling. Data analysis was conducted using Partial Least Squares-Structural Equation Modeling (PLS-SEM) with SmartPLS 3.0. Online customer reviews demonstrate a positive and significant effect on purchase intention (path coefficient 0.245; T-statistic 3.271; p 0.001), as does price perception (path coefficient 0.373; T-statistic 4.861; p 0.000), with an R-Square of 0.220. Credible and informative reviews build buyer trust; prices perceived as proportional to quality enhance purchase intention. Sudut Kedai needs to actively manage customer reviews and maintain fair pricing to strengthen purchase intention amid an increasingly competitive culinary market.

latest.title: Determinasi Brand Evangelism Hasil Personalisasi, Influencer–Brand Fit, Dan Perceived Authenticity Melalui Consumer Trust
latest.abstract: The emergence of social media as a marketing tool has transformed consumer behavior toward brands. This study aims to analyze the effects of personalization level, influencer–brand fit, and perceived authenticity on brand evangelism, with consumer trust as a mediating variable. This study employs a quantitative approach through a survey of 268 social media users selected using a purposive sampling technique. Data were analyzed using Partial Least Squares–Structural Equation Modeling (PLS-SEM) with the SmartPLS software. The results show that personalization level, perceived authenticity, and consumer trust have a positive effect on brand evangelism. In addition, personalization level, influencer–brand fit, and perceived authenticity have a positive effect on consumer trust. However, influencer–brand fit does not have a significant direct effect on brand evangelism. These findings underscore the importance of personalization, authenticity, and consumer trust in driving brand evangelism on social media.

latest.title: Faktor Penentu Keputusan Investasi Generasi Z Di Pontianak
latest.abstract: This study examines whether financial literacy and media exposure are associated with the investment decisions of Generation Z in Pontianak City. The researchers distributed questionnaires to 154 respondents aged 17–29 who lived in Pontianak, had personal income, and had invested, or were currently investing, in the capital market. Respondents were selected using purposive sampling. The data were analyzed using Partial Least Squares Structural Equation Modeling (PLS-SEM) with SmartPLS, and the measurement model met the criteria for validity and reliability. The results show that both financial literacy and media exposure have a positive and significant relationship with investment decisions, although the effect sizes are small. Because the survey was conducted at a single point in time, these findings indicate association and do not establish causation. Organizers of investment education programs for young people are advised to develop participants’ financial skills while also paying attention to their media habits.

latest.title: Peran Self-Control Dalam Memoderasi Pengaruh Lifestyle dan User Experience Terhadap Impulsive Buying Pada Generasi Z Pengguna Shopee
latest.abstract: Impulsive buying among Generation Z on Shopee is influenced by lifestyle and user experience; however, previous findings are inconsistent, and the role of self-control as a moderator has not been tested together with both factors. This study aims to analyze the role of self-control in moderating the effects of lifestyle and user experience on impulsive buying among Generation Z on Shopee. The study employs an associative-causal quantitative approach with purposive sampling of 100 active Generation Z Shopee users. Data were analyzed using PLS-SEM (SmartPLS 4), complemented by ANOVA (F-test) to examine the simultaneous effects. The results show that lifestyle and user experience have positive and significant effects on impulsive buying, both partially and simultaneously together with self-control and its two interactions (F = 12.325; p < 0.001). Self-control has a negative and significant effect and negatively and significantly moderates the effects of lifestyle and user experience, thereby weakening both relationships. The novelty of this study lies in its integrated model, which simultaneously examines lifestyle and user experience with self-control as a moderator. The better Generation Z's self-control, the lower the tendency toward impulsive buying, even when influenced by lifestyle and an engaging online shopping experience. These findings are expected to provide insights for consumers and e-commerce platform managers in understanding and managing purchasing behavior.

latest.title: David versus Goliath: understanding how consumers navigate their relationship with a brand involved in online moral-panic dynamics
latest.abstract: Purpose Research on brand transgressions has primarily examined consumers’ emotional and behavioural responses at the individual level, yet little is known about how such transgressions unfold as collective phenomena on social media. This study aims to examine how consumers individually and collectively negotiate their relationships with brands during moralised online controversies, focusing on the escalation of brand transgressions into moral-panic dynamics and their implications for the consumer-brand relationship. Design/methodology/approach A nine-month netnography was conducted to analyse Reddit discussions related to the 2022 Balenciaga controversy. Approximately 800 conversational traces posted between November 2022 and August 2024 were unobtrusively collected from the 20 most active and content-rich threads across 16 relevant subreddits. Findings Findings provide evidence of both individual-level (relationship destabilisation, decoupling and rupture) and collective-level negotiation practices (relationship rupture amplification, rupture delegitimisation and reframing). A theoretically informed interpretation explains how consumer-brand relationships are simultaneously personally experienced and socially constructed. Originality/value This study advances brand transgression research by conceptualising moral-panic dynamics as a collective phenomenon unfolding across moralised brand controversies, shifting the focus from individual reactions to collective processes reshaping consumer-brand relationships in digital environments.

latest.title: Toward sustainable agritourism: operational insights from organic farms engaged with tourism
latest.abstract: Purpose This paper examines how integrating organic farming with agritourism can advance sustainable rural development. By examining organic farms engaged with tourism in South Korea through an ecotourism framework, it addresses the need to distinguish genuinely sustainable, ecologically grounded agritourism models from conventional, chemical-intensive practices. Design/methodology/approach The study utilizes a qualitative case study approach combining in-depth interviews with operators of three organic farms and a content analysis of 38 organic farm tourism websites in South Korea. The analysis evaluates farm operations, visitor programming and rural community dynamics against core ecotourism principles, contextualized with recent agritourism literature. Findings Organic agritourism aligns closely with ecotourism by integrating low-impact farming with hands-on environmental education, biodiversity conservation and cultural preservation. Key findings highlight that tourism revenue reinforces organic land stewardship, small-scale operations foster meaningful socio-cultural and educational exchanges and participatory community collaboration enhances rural resilience and local circular economies. Five operational takeaways are identified: ecological conservation, active learning, socio-cultural sustainability, value-based economic viability and inclusive community participation. Originality/value This paper demonstrates that ecotourism serves as an effective guiding paradigm for agritourism on small-scale organic enterprises. It provides actionable operational and policy insights for agritourism operators, planners and government agencies seeking to establish replicable, value-based agritourism models that support environmental integrity, rural vitality and ethical visitor

latest.title: From story to sale: how digital storytelling shapes AR consumers' impulse shopping intention
latest.abstract: Purpose Digital storytelling has emerged as a catalyst and game changer in the transformative marketing ecosystem through integrative efforts with augmented reality. This study addresses this gap by examining how digital storytelling enhances consumer immersion and enjoyment. It also examines the impact of immersion and enjoyment on consumers' impulse shopping intention. Design/methodology/approach 391 responses were collected from active augmented reality users who had experience with brand storytelling in augmented reality. The data were analysed using a combined importance–performance map analysis (cIPMA) in partial least squares structural equation modelling (PLS-SEM). Findings The findings demonstrate that the importance of four dimensions of augmented reality digital storytelling (narrative structure, perceived aesthetics, self-reference, theming and storytelling) significantly influences immersion and enjoyment and leads to consumer impulse shopping intention. Furthermore, necessity logic complements sufficiency logic by demonstrating that perceived aesthetics constitutes a necessary condition for both enjoyment and immersion. Theming and storytelling impose a weak bottleneck constraint solely on immersion. Additionally, enjoyment and immersion are less restrictive in practice for impulsive purchase intention. This suggests that most respondents already meet the minimum requirements. Consequently, these antecedents function more as performance-enhancing factors than as critical bottlenecks requiring immediate managerial intervention. Originality/value This study pioneers research at the intersection of augmented reality marketing and digital storytelling by demonstrating how narrative, aesthetics, self-reference, theming and storytelling elements can shape consum

latest.title: Micro-cultural activism in slow fashion: how influencers reframe sustainable consumption on Instagram
latest.venue: Journal of Fashion Marketing and Management
latest.abstract: Purpose This study examines the activist roles of slow fashion influencers on Instagram, focusing on how they construct and circulate sustainability narratives and reframe sustainable consumption into daily achievable practices. Design/methodology/approach The study employs a qualitative research design, analysing both visual and textual materials from the Instagram posts of slow fashion influencers. Findings The findings reveal that slow fashion influencers operate as micro-cultural activists who perform as educators, advocates and facilitators of ethical consumer practices. By voicing their concerns about workers' rights, animal welfare and textile waste, influencers make complex sustainability issues accessible while encouraging reflection on daily practices such as second-hand shopping, upcycling and recycling. Through their digital narratives, these influencers frame sustainability as an individualized moral identity project, thereby linking their personal consumption choices to lifestyle-oriented ethical advocacy. Research limitations/implications This article contributes to the literature on influencer culture and digital activism by shifting the focus away from short-term behavioural metrics towards cultural meaning-making and demonstrating how influencers use Instagram as a dynamic space for cultural activism. Social implications This paper shows how slow fashion influencers use their digital presence to cultivate environmental, social and ethical awareness among their followers by presenting accessible alternatives to conventional mass consumption. Originality/value This research contributes to the influencer marketing literature by demonstrating how activist roles are enacted through social media and how influencers provide the symbolic tools that enable cons

latest.title: Building productivity in culinary MSMEs through market orientation: the mediating role of value co-creation on marketing performance
latest.venue: International Journal of Productivity and Performance Management
latest.abstract: Purpose This study aims to investigate the impact of responsive and proactive market orientation on the marketing performance of culinary micro, small and medium-sized culinary enterprises (MSMEs) in Indonesia, positioning marketing performance as a proxy for productivity. Specifically, it explores the mediating role of value co-creation, a mechanism that has received limited empirical attention in prior research. Design/methodology/approach This study employed a quantitative survey approach involving 319 respondents, comprising managers or owners of MSMEs. To evaluate the proposed hypotheses and examine both direct and indirect (mediating) relationships, the data were analysed using partial least squares structural equation modelling (PLS-SEM) via SmartPLS 4. All variables were measured using previously validated measurement scales. Findings Proactive market orientation (PMO) significantly enhances value co-creation but lacks a direct effect on marketing performance; its impact is fully mediated by co-creation. Responsive market orientation (RMO) directly improves performance, and this improvement is partially achieved through co-creation. The study confirms co-creation as a pivotal mechanism linking MO to outcomes, with PMO's influence being entirely indirect and RMO's hybrid (direct/indirect). Originality/value This study advances the literature by integrating responsive and proactive market orientation with value co-creation in the context of culinary MSMEs. It highlights value co-creation as a dynamic capability that enables SMEs to translate market insights into productivity gains despite resource constraints, offering both theoretical enrichment and practical guidance for enhancing competitiveness.

latest.title: Parental influence and university choice: a marketing mix perspective from private higher education in Bangladesh
latest.abstract: Purpose In cultures with strong familial values, parents play a crucial role in shaping students’ educational choices. In the higher education context, understanding the factors influencing students’ university selection is essential. This study aims to examine the impact of parental influence and the marketing mix on students’ decision-making when choosing private higher education institutions in Bangladesh. Although marketing mix theory, social cognitive career theory (SCCT) and cultural capital theory have each informed research on university choice separately, their combined application to explain gendered, family-mediated decision-making in a collectivist developing-country context remains largely unexamined. Design/methodology/approach Grounded in SCCT, cultural capital theory and the 7Ps marketing mix framework, this study adopts a quantitative approach using data from 298 students attending private higher education institutions in Bangladesh, analysed through partial least squares structural equation modelling (PLS-SEM) with measurement invariance, multi-group analysis and effect-size (f2, Q2) assessment. Findings The findings identify parental influence as the key determinant in university choice, particularly for female students. Female students tend to rely more on family guidance when evaluating educational quality and tuition fees, whereas male students are more independent in assessing academic programmes and financial considerations. The results also indicate that the location of the university is the least significant factor affecting students’ choices. Research limitations/implications The findings highlight the importance of incorporating socio-cultural factors, particularly parental influence, when applying the marketing mix framework in collectivist

latest.title: Investigating the dynamics between sustainability reporting and social media. A field study
latest.abstract: Purpose This study aims to analyse the interactions between sustainability reporting and social media communication, with particular attention to the actors involved, decision-making processes and strategies adopted to ensure effectiveness, consistency and transparency in sustainability communication. Design/methodology/approach The study is based on a field study conducted in the Italian agri-food sector. Data were collected through 11 semi-structured interviews with managers responsible for sustainability reporting and/or corporate communication across nine Italian agri-food companies. The analysis is guided by an integrated theoretical framework combining communication theory and stakeholder theory. Findings Sustainability reports remain the central, validated repository of sustainability information, while social media are mainly used to amplify and adapt previously approved content. Stakeholder interactions on social media are monitored and managed but do not influence the content of sustainability reports. Sustainability managers act as gatekeepers of content validity and compliance, while social media managers translate information for platform-specific dissemination. Social implications The results highlight tensions among regulatory requirements, reputational risk and increasing expectations for transparency, raising questions about the actual dialogic potential of social media to foster accessible, inclusive sustainability communication. Originality/value The study contributes to the sustainability accounting and communication literature by providing empirical evidence of limited informational circularity between sustainability reporting and social media. It advances an integrated explanation that links communication noise, stakeholder legitimacy consideration

latest.title: The call for signaling of expertise on social media: the case of food influencers
latest.abstract: Purpose A tension exists between engagement-driven platform visibility and consumers’ need for credible dietary advice with direct health implications. This research aims to examine how expertise cues help consumers identify credible food influencer content and how qualified influencers can communicate expertise effectively in social media environments. Design/methodology/approach Across six studies, the authors combine secondary analysis of 397 Instagram recipe posts from 40 qualified and non-qualified food influencers with five experiments involving 1,977 participants: US adults recruited through MTurk (Ns = 231, 309 and 284) and US undergraduates (Ns = 601 and 552). The experiments manipulate source qualifications, message design, expertise-salience cues and measure individual differences in BMI and body-esteem, to examine effects on perceived expertise, health-related outcomes and social media engagement. Findings Consumers often do not distinguish clearly between qualified and non-qualified food influencers when expertise cues are absent. Secondary data analysis shows meaningful differences in the reliability of content produced by these sources. Across the studies, making expertise salient increases perceived expertise and improves both health-related and engagement outcomes. The authors further show that combining informational and motivational message elements strengthens the effect of qualifications on perceived expertise, and that body esteem shapes consumer responsiveness to expertise signals. Research limitations/implications The findings are based primarily on Instagram-related contexts and may not generalize fully to other platforms or audience groups. Future research should examine additional platforms and broader samples. Practical implications The findi

latest.title: Mapping word-of-mouth drivers of investors’ financial behavior: a DEMATEL analysis from an Islamic financial marketing perspective
latest.abstract: Purpose This study aims to identify, prioritize and map the causal interrelationships among word-of-mouth (WOM)-related factors shaping investors’ financial behavior from an Islamic financial marketing perspective. It examines how trust, social interaction, shared vision, family and friends, expert knowledge, risk-taking, past stock performance, financial advertising and investment experience jointly shape investors’ financial decisions. Design/methodology/approach A structured literature-based factor identification process and expert validation were used to identify the relevant WOM-related factors. The Decision-Making Trial and Evaluation Laboratory (DEMATEL) method was then applied to analyze their direct and indirect interrelationships. Judgments from 15 academic and financial-market experts were aggregated to classify the factors into cause and effect groups and construct a causal map. Findings Relational trust, investment experience, risk-taking and social interaction are the most prominent factors in the WOM network. Relational trust, social interaction, shared vision, past stock performance and expert knowledge operate as causal drivers, whereas financial advertising, risk-taking, family and friends and investment experience are mainly influenced by other factors. The results indicate that trust-based communication and credible knowledge sources are central to investors’ learning and risk-related decisions. Research limitations/implications The study relies on expert judgments and may therefore be affected by subjectivity and contextual bias. The Islamic financial marketing perspective is interpretive; specialist Islamic-finance expertise was not documented for the panel. Future research should validate the proposed causal paths with investor survey data, compar

latest.title: Picture, picture on the screen: a between-subjects experiment on AI-generated vs human images on Generation Z consumers’ impulse buying intention
latest.venue: Young Consumers Insight and Ideas for Responsible Marketers
latest.abstract: Purpose The rapid advancement of artificial intelligence (AI) has transformed digital marketing strategies, particularly in the tourism industry, where AI-enhanced imagery is increasingly used to influence consumer behaviour. However, little research has examined how AI-generated images affect impulse travel purchases compared with human-generated images. This study aims to examine the effect of AI-enhanced versus human-generated images on impulse travel purchase decisions among Generation Z travellers, using Stimulus–Organism–Response (S-O-R) theory and consumption value theory as a theoretical lens. Design/methodology/approach Through a between-person experimental design, 580 participants were randomly assigned to view either AI-enhanced or human-generated images of a non-iconic travel destination. This study analysed results using partial least squares structural equation modelling. Findings The study found that preference value and social value directly and significantly influenced impulse purchase intentions, while all consumption values, including preference, social, emotional and functional values, affected impulse purchasing through travellers’ inspiration. Additionally, AI-enhanced images led to a higher preference value for impulse purchases, whereas human-generated images were perceived as having higher social value and visual aesthetic appeal. Originality/value By integrating the S-O-R framework with consumption value theory, this study offers fresh theoretical insights into the mediating role of traveller inspiration and the distinct value perceptions elicited by AI versus human-generated visuals. These findings also offer critical insights for tourism marketers using AI-driven visual content, consumers navigating increasingly AI-mediated travel promotions

latest.title: From tradition to transformation: how cultural innovation enhances regional revitalization through culinary appeal, brand equity and EWOM
latest.venue: Asia Pacific Journal of Marketing and Logistics
latest.abstract: Purpose This study investigates how cultural inheritance-based innovation (CIBI) enhances coastal revitalization by strengthening destination brand equity (DBE) and culinary attraction (CA) and how these effects translate into tourists' electronic word of mouth (EWOM). It further examines the moderating roles of emotional value (EV) and in-person word of mouth (IWOM) in shaping tourists' perceptions and advocacy behaviors. Design/methodology/approach A quantitative survey was conducted with 692 tourists visiting Penghu, Taiwan. Structural equation modeling (SEM) and bootstrapping were applied to test the proposed mediating and moderating framework linking CIBI, DBE, CA, EWOM, EV and WOM. Robustness checks were performed using SEM to validate the results. Findings Results demonstrate that DBE mediates the relationship between CIBI and CA, while CA mediates the link between DBE and EWOM. EV and IWOM have significant direct effects on DBE and CA but do not moderate the CIBI–DBE or DBE–CA relationships. These findings suggest that emotional engagement and interpersonal advocacy contribute directly to brand equity and culinary appeal rather than amplifying the effects of cultural innovation. Originality/value This research advances destination branding and cultural tourism literature by integrating cultural innovation, brand equity and culinary appeal into a unified framework. It further examines emotion and interpersonal communication as moderating mechanisms and shows that they operate as direct drivers rather than as amplifiers of these effects, offering theoretical and managerial insights for sustainable tourism-driven regional revitalization.

latest.title: Reverse logistics decisions, supply chain resilience and blockchain-enabled environmental performance
latest.venue: International Journal of Industrial Engineering and Operations Management
latest.abstract: Purpose This study examines whether strategic and tactical reverse-logistics decisions relate to environmental performance through supply chain resilience (SCR) and whether blockchain technology (BCT) conditions these indirect relationships. Design/methodology/approach Data were collected through an online survey of senior supply-chain and logistics professionals in manufacturing firms in Egypt (n = 890) and Jordan (n = 836), treated as two Middle Eastern settings for testing the same mechanism. Covariance-based structural equation modelling in AMOS 28 assessed the measurement model, multi-group structural equivalence, mediation and first-stage moderated mediation. Indirect effects were evaluated using 5,000-resample, 95% bias-corrected bootstrap intervals. Findings Across both samples, SCR partially mediates the strategic and tactical reverse-logistics decision–environmental performance relationships. BCT strengthens both first-stage relationships; all four moderated-mediation indices are significant and the conditional indirect effects increase with BCT adoption. One strategic pathway is non-significant at low BCT but becomes significant at mean and high levels. Structural weights do not differ significantly across the two samples. Originality/value The study separates strategic and tactical reverse-logistics decisions, specifies SCR as the adaptive capability through which their environmental value is partly realised, and tests BCT as a first-stage boundary condition across two Middle Eastern manufacturing settings.

latest.title: DMT-induced aberrant salience and suggestibility correlate with mystical experiences and positive emotionality
latest.abstract: Historically, psychedelics have been investigated both as models of psychosis and therapy. We previously proposed mystical experiences as a link between psychosis- and therapy-relevant processes, as measured by aberrant salience and suggestibility, respectively, for lysergic acid diethylamide (LSD). Here, we aimed to extend and refine this framework for N , ​N -dimethyltryptamine (DMT). In a randomised, placebo-controlled, double-blind, crossover study, 25 healthy participants received inhaled DMT (60 mg) and an active placebo (0.6 mg DMT), separated by two hours. We measured aberrant salience (State Aberrant Salience Inventory [ASI-S])​ and suggestibility (Creative Imagination Scale [CIS]), including also a newly developed, exploratory item of suggestion-induced mystical experiences. Psychedelic experiences were measured via Six Dimensions and Eleven Factors of Altered States of Consciousness Questionnaire (6D-ASC and 11-ASC), Hallucinogen Rating Scale (HRS), and Mystical Experiences Questionnaire (MEQ). Compared to placebo, DMT increased all aberrant salience factors, most suggestibility modalities, and most psychedelic factors. Aberrant salience showed widespread correlations with psychedelic experiences, particularly mystical experiences (MEQ factors) and positive emotionality (e.g., Joyfulness [6D-ASC], Blissful State [11-ASC]). Suggestibility correlated with the same positive emotionality factors and inversely with unpleasant emotionality (Dysphoria [HRS]) and mystical experience aspects (i.e., the factor Ineffability [MEQ]). In conclusion, DMT induced both psychosis- and therapy-relevant processes of aberrant salience and suggestibility. Their link may be indirect with respect to mystical experiences, with emotionality playing a more crucial role. Importantly, su

latest.title: Conceptualising brand purpose as a multidimensional marketing and management construct: a qualitative framework
latest.abstract: Brand purpose has been explored across organisational, stakeholder, authenticity, sustainability and brand-equity research but remains difficult to define consistently. This paper aims to create a combined multidimensional model of brand purpose and create an initial set of items for further validation. By conducting a concept-based literature review we identified eleven tentative domains. Through an iterative two-round expert consultation process these domains were questioned and adjusted. We used a combination of deductive-inductive and grounded theory coding techniques when analysing the data from our 15-member panel of experts (made up of both academics and practitioners). An additional expert panel of 11 provided written input which was used to inform initial item creation. As the focus of the expert round was to challenge and improve upon our domains, this should not be considered validation of the items. Our domains can be grouped into four themes: a beyond-profit core, internal embedding, stakeholder experience, and impact and brand outcomes. Theoretically, our paper integrates these domains and clarifies boundaries between similar concepts. Managerially, it provides a structured basis for reflecting on brand purpose. Lastly, we created a set of items that require future validation.

latest.title: Exploring the relationship between consumer religiosity and perceptions of corporate social responsibility in tobacco companies: Does smoking status matter?
latest.venue: Asia Pacific Journal of Marketing and Logistics
latest.abstract: Purpose Corporate social responsibility (CSR) has become an essential component of corporate strategy, aiming at improving social and environmental outcomes. It is increasingly recognized as a powerful tool for shaping public perceptions of businesses' fair treatment of employees and consumers, addressing social issues, profit orientation, and overall commitment to ethical practices. However, controversial industries are frequently accused of exploiting CSR initiatives. These range from the core “sin” sectors of tobacco, alcohol, and gambling to more contested categories such as fast food and fossil fuels. Such firms often establish their own permissive guidelines under the guise of social responsibility, potentially undermining genuine efforts for positive change. Tobacco, the most consistently classified sin industry, provides the focal context for this study. This study examines how different types of religiosity affect consumers' views on tobacco companies' CSR and their support for these companies, with consumer corporate identity (CCI) serving as a mediator. It also explores how smoking status moderates the relationship between religiosity and CCI. Design/methodology/approach Using a survey of consumers in Indonesia (n = 331), our findings reveal a complex relationship between consumers' religiosity, smoking status, and their perceptions of tobacco companies. Findings Intrinsic religiosity positively shaped CSR perceptions across four of five domains: employee, social, profit, and ethics, with no significant effect on consumer-focused initiatives. Smokers who are more likely to identify with tobacco companies were more inclined to support the CSR initiatives, even disregarding their detrimental effects on society. Extrinsically religious people also show a positiv

latest.title: Reskilling female entrepreneurs for knowledge spillovers: a KSTE perspective on SMEs in lagging regions
latest.abstract: Purpose The research focuses on how territorial innovation aids the process of reskilling and training female entrepreneurs in small and medium-sized enterprises (SMEs) through knowledge application and spillover in disadvantaged areas. Based on the knowledge spillover theory of entrepreneurship (KSTE), this study aims to investigate the role of institutional help as an essential tool tying together the development of entrepreneurial competence and application of knowledge. Design/methodology/approach The study uses quantitative research techniques based on structural equation modeling that help identify the correlations between obtaining skills by female entrepreneurs and getting managerial training and implementing innovations in their region concerning knowledge gain and usage. Findings The findings show that territorial innovation enhances entrepreneurial capabilities through reskilling and managerial education, while institutional support facilitates the translation of these capabilities into knowledge application and knowledge spillovers. Firm size and firm age significantly influence knowledge spillovers but do not significantly affect knowledge application. Practical implications The findings of this study will assist policymakers and institutions in developing inclusive reskilling and management education programs for female-owned SMEs based upon knowledge spillovers that lead to true innovations and development in the region. Originality/value The study extends KSTE by embedding it in the context of female-led SMEs in lagging regions, linking entrepreneurial education and territorial innovation to knowledge outcomes.

latest.title: Towards a gender responsive framework to guide social marketers in designing campaigns featuring social media influencers
latest.abstract: Purpose This paper aims to examine how gender norms shape the experiences of social media influencers (SMIs) and consumers when engaging in pro-social initiatives and to develop a conceptual and practical framework to guide social marketers in designing gender responsive campaigns that feature SMIs. This is important because SMIs operating in the pro-social domain face gendered marginalisation that can undermine both campaign effectiveness and SMI safety, yet practical guidance on how to address these dynamics remains limited. Design/methodology/approach The research draws on intersectionality, interpreted using a Caribbean feminist theoretical lens. The authors conducted a multi-method feminist critical discourse analysis of content posted by 40 SMIs, alongside qualitative interviews with 21 SMIs and 20 consumer followers in Trinidad & Tobago. Findings Gender norms rooted in colonial legacies shape how SMIs and consumers experience, interpret and evaluate SMI-led pro-social messages. These dynamics influence perceptions of credibility and effectiveness for both groups. Drawing on participants’ accounts, this study proposes key considerations for a gender-responsive framework focused on SMI follower congruence, stronger representation, leveraging SMIs’ cultural intelligence to enhance engagement with pro-social causes and ensuring consistency in their self-presentation. Originality/value This paper makes a dual contribution. Theoretically, it extends understanding of SMI authenticity and gender-based marginalisation by demonstrating how gendered power, shaped by race, sexuality and class within a Global South context, determines whose voices are seen as credible in pro-social messaging. Practically, it offers the first empirically grounded, gender responsive framework f

latest.title: Queer(y)ing gender in entrepreneurial action through the experiences of transgender women entrepreneurs in Tasmania
latest.venue: International Journal of Entrepreneurial Behaviour & Research
latest.abstract: Purpose This study examines and queers entrepreneurial action theory using queer phenomenology, showing how gender affirmation reshapes entrepreneurial action. While entrepreneurial action theory traditionally focuses on decision-making within uncertain environments, it rarely accounts for experiences of transgender women. Design/methodology/approach This research combined narrative inquiry and visual methods to collect data from two transgender women entrepreneurs in Tasmania, Australia. Research on transgender women entrepreneurs is limited, so combined methods capture emotional nuances: (1) drawings of self-perception before and after starting the business and (2) an in-depth interview. Findings Findings suggest considering temporal dynamics across different industries when entrepreneurs seek to reveal their identity. Louise is a mechanical engineer, and being a mechanic in a masculine-dominated industry significantly influences the perceptions of family, friends and customers. Meanwhile, Sally, a comedian, was provided with space for creativity and fluid perceptions. The women's experiences are not uniform, with industries entrepreneurs are aligned with shaping their negotiation of entrepreneurship. Research limitations/implications This study advances entrepreneurial action theory by integrating queer phenomenology to account for transgender women entrepreneurs' lived experiences. It challenges the assumption of time as a neutral construct in entrepreneurial action theory. This study shows how cisnormative expectations within transgender women's space shape entrepreneurial decision-making timing, pacing, and sequencing. Originality/value This article challenges existing discourses around entrepreneurial action theory and gender in entrepreneurship. Transgender wome

latest.title: Reverse logistics in electronics industry: a bibliometric analysis, challenges and future research prospects
latest.venue: Journal of responsible production and consumption.
latest.abstract: Purpose The proliferation of electronic goods has increased challenges for global e-waste; thus, reverse logistics (RL) and closed-loop supply chains (CLSC) in the electronics sector have become very challenging research areas. This study aims to provide a substantial bibliometric and systematic overview of the RL and CLSC research in electronics, with a particular emphasis on identifying potential barriers to implementation and synthesising findings into a conceptual framework for future empirical investigation. Design/methodology/approach Data analysis was performed using the PRISMA 2020 protocol, extracted from the Scopus database through searching the terms reverse logistics, closed-loop supply chain and electronics. The search occurred from 2010 to 2024 and after applying structured inclusion and exclusion criteria resulted in a final corpus of 94 peer-reviewed journal articles. Bibliometric methods, such as trends in publication, keyword co-occurrence, co-citation analysis and thematic mapping, were then used. Findings The volume of publications has grown sharply since 2019, with a combination of the regulators’ attention, the global e-waste crisis and COVID-19 supply chain disruption. Keyword analysis shows a new paradigm shift from operational efficiency to strategic sustainability. There are four dimensions where barriers to RL and CLSC introduction cluster: technical infrastructure gaps, policy and regulatory weaknesses, strategic and organisational resistance and market and consumer behaviour factors. Research limitations/implications Policymakers need to enhance extended producer responsibility (EPR) enforcement and implement market-based incentives. Electronics manufacturers should invest in a phased digital transformation, from RFID-based tracking to AI-en

latest.title: Normalizing sustainable fashion innovations: environmental messages and dynamic norms in circular fashion adoption
latest.abstract: Purpose This study aims to investigate whether informational messages promote interest in fashion products made from agri-food waste and whether dynamic norm cues strengthen persuasion in a trend-sensitive, ambiguous market. Design/methodology/approach Overall, 183 Italian adults were randomly assigned to control, environmental message or environmental plus dynamic norm message conditions. Participants reported purchasing intention and willingness to pay a premium price. Pro-environmental self-identity and identification with sustainable fashion consumers were tested as moderators. Findings Only the combined environmental and dynamic norm message increased purchasing intention, whereas neither message affected willingness to pay, suggesting a distinction between motivational interest and financial commitment. Exploratory analyses suggested that the environmental message was more effective among participants with low identification with sustainable fashion consumers. Pro-environmental self-identity did not moderate message effects. Research limitations/implications Self-reported intentions and a highly educated Italian sample limit generalisability. Future studies should use behavioural measures, field experiments, longitudinal designs and diverse samples to test whether initial openness persists and translates into purchasing and price acceptance. Practical implications Environmental messages combined with dynamic norm cues can increase initial interest in agri-food waste fashion, but the promotional strategy did not increase willingness to pay, highlighting the importance of product, price and audience segmentation. Originality/value The study shows that integrating dynamic norm cues into environmental appeals can increase initial openness toward novel sustainable fash

latest.title: Effects of green business practices on business relationships: evidences from the automotive industry
latest.venue: Journal of Business and Industrial Marketing
latest.abstract: Purpose The study aims to investigate how the implementation of green business practices (GBPs) – efforts undertaken by firms to reduce their negative impact on the environment, while simultaneously supporting economic and social value creation – influence the substance of business relationships. Design/methodology/approach A qualitative, in-depth single case study methodology is applied. Research is carried out within the automotive industrial sector; the unit of analysis is a Portuguese business network which is undergoing a green transition, analyzed through the actors, resources and activities model of the Industrial Marketing and Purchasing approach. Findings The empirical investigation identifies six main effects of GBPs on business relationships: Economic, Innovation, Stability, Leverage, Power and Singularity effects. In addition, elements facilitating the implementation of GBPs are recognized and critically discussed. Originality/value The present research contributes theoretically to widen knowledge on GBPs by examining how their implementation reshapes the substance of business relationships. By exploring how GBPs reconfigure business networks, original managerial implications arise that provide useful directions for practitioners dealing with GBPs.

latest.title: Integrating artificial intelligence into business management: implications for intellectual capital development
latest.abstract: Purpose This study explores the implications of artificial intelligence (AI) integration into business management practices, emphasizing its impact on intellectual capital components. Specifically, it examines how AI integration influences the interaction between human, structural and relational capital in managerial processes. Design/methodology/approach The study adopts a rigorous thematic analysis conducted in NVivo. Data collected through an online qualitative questionnaire administered to managers from multiple sectors were analyzed to identify key dimensions of AI integration in business contexts and to develop a conceptual model explaining their interactions. Findings The findings reveal four key dimensions: the role of AI in managerial processes, the challenges associated with AI, the strategies and best practices required to integrate AI into management and the strategies needed to adapt and train human resources in organizations integrating AI. While AI enhances efficiency, automation and decision-making processes, sustainable integration requires strategic planning, gradual implementation and investment in human capital. Overall, AI integration appears to enhance the interaction between human, structural and relational capital rather than radically restructuring intellectual capital. Practical implications The link between technological implementation and human-centered challenges provides practical guidance for organizations undergoing digital transformation. Gradual AI integration through pilot projects, employee training and governance structures supports responsible human–AI collaboration and strategic decision-making. Originality/value This research extends the traditional technology–organization–environment framework by conceptualizing AI integration as

latest.title: Sub-Saharan African agribusiness SMEs' export: What can the resource-based view tell us?
latest.venue: Journal of Agribusiness in Developing and Emerging Economies
latest.abstract: Purpose This paper investigates the explanatory power of the resource-based view (RBV) of the firm on the agribusiness exports of Sub-Saharan African (SSA) small and medium-sized enterprises (SMEs). Design/methodology/approach Using a qualitative research design, we identify and interpret resources and capabilities by analyzing 16 selected cases describing agribusiness exports by SMEs from SSA. Findings The three most influential resource categories that explain SSA agribusiness exports by SMEs are: (1) Managerial resources, (2) production, technological and R&D resources and (3) marketing-related resources. In most cases, we find resources to drive export decisions and performance in complementary resource “sets”, rather than as singular resources. Research limitations/implications There is potential in moving research beyond the categorization of resources and start working on (contextualized) categorization of resource “sets” that increase the effectiveness of companies' exports. As stipulated by Prahalad and Hamel, the theory of core competencies might be a helpful starting point for investigating complementary resources in the export context. In addition, the complementary resource sets add a dimension of constant change to the RBV discourse. Originality/value We contribute by (1) arguing that the theoretical work of RBV's impact on export needs to move beyond single resources and capabilities towards complementary sets of resources. (2) adding resources not covered prominently in the export literature and (3) investigating a new context (SSA) for the RBV–agribusiness export nexus.

latest.title: Exploring the potential of green waqf as an alternative instrument for climate financing
latest.venue: International Journal of Climate Change Strategies and Management
latest.abstract: Purpose This study aims to investigate the determinants of Indonesian Muslims’ intentions to donate to green waqf, an Islamic financial instrument increasingly used for climate financing. Design/methodology/approach Survey data from 550 cash-waqf donors were analysed using partial least squares structural equation modelling. The model extends the theory of planned behaviour (TPB) by incorporating knowledge, trust, religiosity and environmental awareness into the traditional constructs of attitude, subjective norms and perceived behavioural control (PBC). Reliability, convergent validity and discriminant validity were confirmed. Multicollinearity and predictive relevance were also assessed. Findings The study reveals that knowledge, trust, religiosity and environmental awareness positively influenced attitudes towards green waqf donations. Attitude, subjective norms, PBC and knowledge also directly influence intentions to donate to green waqf, with knowledge emerging as the primary driver. Research limitations/implications The findings suggest that green waqf should be repositioned from traditional philanthropy as a more dedicated climate-financing instrument. This requires strengthening waqf literacy, institutional transparency, impact disclosure and seamless digital channels to translate knowledge, trust and environmental awareness into sustained donation behaviour. These implications are particularly relevant for waqf institutions (nazhirs), waqf authorities and policymakers seeking to mobilise Islamic social finance for climate action. Originality/value This study advances the green waqf literature by extending the TPB to include environmental awareness, knowledge, trust and religiosity. By using a larger and more diverse sample than previous studies, it provides a c

latest.title: The forensic loom: weaving trust and sincerity into the corporation as complex adaptive system
latest.abstract: Purpose This paper introduces the Forensic Loom, a diagnostic framework that treats organizational trust as something that can be verified rather than assumed. It proposes that leadership sincerity, whether a leader is performing the scope they claim, can be examined systematically instead of judged impressionistically. Trust is grounded in what a leader does, not in what a leader is believed capable of doing. Design/methodology/approach The paper is conceptual. It proceeds phenomenologically, grounding a Bohrian complementarity account of the corporation as simultaneously unitary and multiple. It extends Elliott Jaques' stratified systems theory by arguing that five functions are inevitable in any viable corporation. This claim is grounded in Ashby's Law of Requisite Variety. A cybernetic and telemetric architecture, drawn from the tradition of Wiener, Ashby and Beer, operationalizes the framework for measurement. Findings The paper argues that a form of recurring and inevitable failure, which it terms the corporate mask, involves actively performing a scope above one's function and span of discretion. This failure is a rational, locatable source of coordination loss that propagates across hierarchical levels. It is a structural consequence of how formal and functional scopes diverge and never fully close. It proposes level-specific and seam-specific instruments that render this failure measurable and correspond structurally with Beer’s viable system model. Research limitations/implications This paper is conceptual and does not include a case study. The correspondence with Beer's viable system model is structural rather than recursive. A full demonstration that each level recursively embeds the viable system model's own five systems is noted as a direction for future r

latest.title: Interactive Digital Catalog Gamification for Donut Bouquet Innovation to Accelerate MSME Revenue
latest.abstract: Purpose: This community service program (PKM) aims to implement a gamification-based Interactive Digital Catalog to enhance product attractiveness, strengthen digital marketing, and support the marketing performance of Donat Duo Putri MSME in Padang City. Method: This program employed a qualitative descriptive approach through several stages, including observation, interviews, partner needs identification, product innovation, Interactive Digital Catalog development, gamification feature integration, training, mentoring, and evaluation to assess the effectiveness of the program implementation. Practical Applications: The program resulted in the development of an innovative Donut Bouquet product supported by an Interactive Digital Catalog integrated with WhatsApp ordering services, a Spin Discount feature, Reward Points, and Voucher Discounts. These innovations simplified product promotion, increased customer engagement, expanded digital marketing reach, and provided a more engaging shopping experience for consumers. Conclusion: The gamification-based Interactive Digital Catalog was developed as a digital marketing innovation for Donat Duo Putri MSME. The program has the potential to enhance product attractiveness, strengthen digital marketing efforts, and provide a more interactive and engaging customer experience.

latest.title: Citra Merek Pakaian Bekas Impor Berkaitan Positif dengan Minat Generasi Z Membeli Fesyen Lokal
latest.abstract: The growing trend of purchasing imported secondhand (thrifting) items among Generation Z has introduced a new dynamic to the competition within the fashion market, particularly in relation to local fashion brands. The relatively affordable prices and the brand image associated with these imported secondhand items can shape consumer perceptions and influence their preferences toward local fashion products. This study aims to analyze the impact of the price and brand image of imported secondhand items on the purchase intention for local fashion among Generation Z in Parepare City, both partially and simultaneously. A quantitative approach was employed, involving 100 Generation Z respondents from Parepare City, selected through purposive sampling. Data were collected via a Likert-scale questionnaire and analyzed using multiple linear regression. The results indicate that the price of imported secondhand items has a positive and significant effect on the purchase intention for local fashion, with a regression coefficient of 0.291 (p = 0.001). Similarly, the brand image of imported secondhand items has a positive and significant effect on the purchase intention for local fashion, with a regression coefficient of 0.843 (p = 0.001). Simultaneously, both price and brand image significantly influence purchase intention, with an F-value of 189.350 (p = 0.001). An R-square value of 0.796 suggests that price and brand image account for 79.6% of the variation in purchase intention for local fashion, while the remaining 20.4% is attributed to factors outside the model. Brand image exerts a relatively stronger influence than price, as evidenced by their respective standardized beta coefficients of 0.616 and 0.307. These findings underscore the importance of price perception and the st

hot.title: How generative AI Is shaping the future of marketing
hot.venue: Journal of the Academy of Marketing Science
hot.abstract: Generative AI (Gen AI) is shaping the future of marketing. In the next decade, Gen AI will influence how marketers interact and communicate with customers, help create and deliver marketing content (text, images, and video), and inform methods for researching and developing new products and services. In both service and sales settings, Gen AI will affect customers directly and significantly. Therefore, marketers, researchers, and public policy makers require a clear understanding of Gen AI and its potential, as well as its limitations. To assist marketers in thinking through the adoption and implementation of Gen AI, the current article presents a four-quadrant organizing framework that highlights trade-offs in both the nature of Gen AI inputs and the extent of human augmentation needed to deliver Gen AI–generated outputs. This framework provides guidance for the selection and implementation of Gen AI tools, as well as recommendations for further research.

hot.title: Artificial Intelligence and Its Role in Shaping Organizational Work Practices and Culture
hot.abstract: The advent of Artificial Intelligence (AI) is profoundly transforming organizational landscapes, significantly influencing work practices and triggering cultural shifts. This study explores the role of AI in reshaping organizational work practices and examines the resulting cultural transformation. Through a systematic literature review, this study synthesizes existing research to provide a comprehensive understanding of AI’s impact on organizational landscapes. A systematic literature review was conducted, analyzing peer-reviewed articles, books, and conference papers to identify key themes related to AI-driven changes in work practices, including automation, decision making, and employee roles. It also explores how these changes influence organizational culture, particularly shifts toward innovation, agility, and continuous learning, alongside challenges like resistance to change and ethical concerns. While AI adoption promises benefits such as enhanced efficiency, productivity, and innovation, it also presents significant challenges related to cultural alignment, employee resistance, ethical concerns, and leadership communication. Effective leadership, transparent communication, and investments in skills development emerge as pivotal strategies for overcoming these obstacles and ensuring successful AI implementation. The findings offer insights into the complex interplay between AI adoption and cultural transformation, highlighting gaps in the current research and suggesting directions for future studies. This study serves as a valuable resource for academics and practitioners seeking to understand the broader implications of AI on organizational structures and culture.

hot.title: Interaction with AI companions and psychological well-being
The evolving field of digital mental health: current evidence and implementation issues for smartphone apps, generative artificial intelligence, and virtual reality
hot.abstract: The expanding domain of digital mental health is transitioning beyond traditional telehealth to incorporate smartphone apps, virtual reality, and generative artificial intelligence, including large language models. While industry setbacks and methodological critiques have highlighted gaps in evidence and challenges in scaling these technologies, emerging solutions rooted in co-design, rigorous evaluation, and implementation science offer promising pathways forward. This paper underscores the dual necessity of advancing the scientific foundations of digital mental health and increasing its real-world applicability through five themes. First, we discuss recent technological advances in digital phenotyping, virtual reality, and generative artificial intelligence. Progress in this latter area, specifically designed to create new outputs such as conversations and images, holds unique potential for the mental health field. Given the spread of smartphone apps, we then evaluate the evidence supporting their utility across various mental health contexts, including well-being, depression, anxiety, schizophrenia, eating disorders, and substance use disorders. This broad view of the field highlights the need for a new generation of more rigorous, placebo-controlled, and real-world studies. We subsequently explore engagement challenges that hamper all digital mental health tools, and propose solutions, including human support, digital navigators, just-in-time adaptive interventions, and personalized approaches. We then analyze implementation issues, emphasizing clinician engagement, service integration, and scalable delivery models. We finally consider the need to ensure that innovations work for all people and thus can bridge digital health disparities, reviewing the evidence on ta

hot.title: Sustainable Consumption and Branding for Gen Z: How Brand Dimensions Influence Consumer Behavior and Adoption of Newly Launched Technological Products
hot.abstract: Generation Z is emerging as a powerful force in shaping global consumer behavior, particularly in the market of digital and technological products. This study examines how specific branding dimensions, such as online brand experience, engagement, image, trust, loyalty, awareness, behavioral intention, and brand knowledge, influence Gen Z’s purchase intention, emphasizing sustainable consumption. Sustainable consumption, in this context, refers to the preference for tech products that minimize the environmental impact through eco-friendly design, energy efficiency, and responsible sourcing. Using a quantitative approach, this cross-sectional research explores the effects of online brand experience, engagement, image, trust, loyalty, awareness, behavioral intention, and knowledge on purchasing newly launched technological products that align with sustainability. Data were collected from a Gen Z sample using a combination of convenience and systematic sampling, and multiple regression analysis identified the most significant predictors of purchase intention. The results indicate that online brand experience, brand image, brand trust, and brand loyalty play the most crucial roles, having a greater effects on Gen Z’s purchase intention, while brand awareness and knowledge also contribute. However, brand engagement and behavioral intention have weaker effects. These findings suggest that brands targeting Gen Z should prioritize building a strong, trustworthy, and engaging online presence while highlighting their sustainability efforts, and when Gen Z consumers have favorable digital interactions with a brand, perceive its image positively, trust it, and feel loyal to it, they are more likely to consider purchasing its sustainable offerings. This study enhances the understandi

hot.title: Leading in the Digital Age: The Role of Leadership in Organizational Digital Transformation
hot.abstract: In the modern digital age, organizations face unprecedented challenges and possibilities while managing the intricacies of digital transformation. Accelerated technological developments, changing customer preferences, heightened competition, and dynamic regulatory environments necessitate companies to synchronize their business goals with technological innovations. Leadership is crucial in steering businesses through changes, requiring a deep understanding of change processes and the capacity to adjust leadership accordingly. This research addresses the central question: How does leadership effectively promote organizational digital transformation? The study examines how leaders can effectively promote the adoption of advanced technologies and the promotion of innovation, by first exploring the nature of digital transformation within organizations and then analyzing the evolving dynamics of leadership in this context. An integrative review of the Web of Science (WoS) and Scopus databases was conducted, using the search terms: “Leadership” and “Digital Transformation”. The findings emphasize that effective leadership is crucial for managing the minutiae of digital transformation, integrating technology into organizational processes to facilitate learning, collaboration, and agility, enabling companies to adapt to market shifts, reduce uncertainty, and enhance decision-making for sustainable growth. By using the right tools and with the right frequency, leaders may develop team cohesion—even at a distance. Attentive digital-age leaders will know how to leverage the right mechanisms, and herein, we hope to give some indication of how that may be achieved, so that digital transformation increases rather than decreases team motivation levels.
