latest.title: Exploring the Impact of Demographic Variables on Consumer Perception Toward Green Marketing Strategies: A Study of the FMCG Sector in India
latest.abstract: The objective of the present study is to investigate the effect of demographic variables on consumer perception of Green marketing strategies of Fast Moving Consumer Goods (FMCG) in India. The present study adopted a survey research methodology to collect data from 337 consumers in India, both online and offline, through a survey method. The main methodology used by the researcher in the present study is that of a structured questionnaire. A random sampling technique was employed to select a diverse sample for the present study. Descriptive and inferential statistical techniques have been used to study the effect of demographic variables such as gender, age, income, and education on consumer perception of Green marketing strategies. The present study showed a significant difference in consumer perception of Green marketing strategies based on demographic variables. The current study highlights the importance of demographic variables while formulating effective Green marketing strategies for the FMCG sector in India. The findings of the current study are significant for businesses and policymakers to formulate effective Green marketing strategies to promote green consumers for the FMCG sector. JEL Classification: M31, Q56, D12

latest.title: What drives social entrepreneurial intention? An integrated model of cognitive, moral, and social antecedents among university students in India
latest.abstract: Social entrepreneurship is pivotal in addressing social and environmental challenges, yet the psychological mechanisms underlying social entrepreneurial intention (SEI), especially in developing nations, remain underexplored. This study, grounded in the Theory of Planned Behaviour and the social entrepreneurial intention framework, investigates the cognitive, moral, normative, and experiential determinants of SEI among higher education students. Employing a quantitative methodology, a cross-sectional design was utilized, involving 349 postgraduate and undergraduate participants. The analysis was conducted using partial least squares structural equation modelling (PLS-SEM). The findings reveal that opportunity recognition competency (ORC) is the most significant predictor of SEI, underscoring the importance of entrepreneurial cognition in SEI. SEI is positively correlated with social entrepreneurial self-efficacy and subjective norms, indicating the significance of perceived entrepreneurial capability and social endorsement. However, SEI does not exhibit significant associations with empathy, moral obligation, perceived sustainability values, perceived social support, perceived behavioural control, or prior experience. Notably, prior experience is indirectly linked to SEI through social entrepreneurial self-efficacy, despite its direct and total associations with SEI being non-significant. Overall, the findings suggest that opportunity recognition competency, social entrepreneurial self-efficacy, and subjective norms hold greater relative importance for SEI when antecedents are evaluated concurrently.

latest.title: Sustainability in Charity Retail: Conflicts in (In)Sufficiency
latest.abstract: Sufficiency has been receiving attention as a means to achieve sustainability. Insights on how to operationalise sufficiency in practice are limited and absent in the context of ecologically constrained organisations, such as, charities. Charities are viewed as critical to sustainability due to their reuse business model; however, charity income is dropping due to the saturation of low-quality and value clothing donations generated by ever-increasing production and consumption of (ultra)fast fashion. This is placing resource (e.g. reliance on volunteer labour) and ecological (e.g. finding reuse routes) burdens on an already constrained sector, highlighting the urgency for charities to future proof the retail businesses foundational to their fundraising efforts. To address this challenge, this research adopts an ethic of sufficiency to introduce business model innovation to charity retail. Drawing on interviews and observations with charity staff, collaborating experts and consumers as donor and retail users, we examine transition to a clothing rental model offering social and ecological sufficiency. We find that the two competing ethics of: (1) sufficiency representing enough and driving deceleration and (2) insufficiency representing not enough and driving acceleration, compete for primacy. While sufficiency can counter challenges arising from insufficiency, competition between them creates contradictory pressures for the charity. This is further exasperated by a misalignment between organisation and consumer experiences of sufficiency. The theoretical and practical implications of the findings for sufficiency, charity retail, rental and consumption are discussed.

latest.title: The Role of Green Marketing of Electric Vehicles in Influencing Buying Intention in Indonesia
latest.venue: International Journal of Social Science and Human Research
latest.abstract: This study investigates the role of green marketing in influencing the buying intention of electric vehicles (EVs) in Indonesia. Using a quantitative approach with Structural Equation Modeling (SEM), data from 330 respondents across Indonesia were collected via an online questionnaire to assess the relationship between the 4Ps of green marketing (Product, Price, Place, Promotion), Electric Vehicle Knowledge, and Environmental Attitude toward Green Buying Intention. The findings reveal that Green Product, Green Price, and Green Place have a significant and positive effect on EV buying intention, while Green Promotion and Electric Vehicle Knowledge did not show a statistically significant impact. Furthermore, although Environmental Attitude was found to have a strong direct influence on Green Buying Intention, it did not significantly moderate any of the tested relationships. The results imply that while Indonesians with strong environmental attitudes are more inclined to purchase EVs, promotional campaigns and general product knowledge from the 4Ps of green marketing may not yet be powerful enough to shift consumer behavior alone.

latest.title: Environmental Practices and Household Green Purchasing Behavior among College Students
latest.venue: International Journal of Research and Innovation in Social Science
latest.abstract: The purpose of this study was to determine which domain of environmental practices significantly influenced the household green purchasing behavior of college students at a higher education institution. In this study, a quantitative, non-experimental research design using descriptive-correlational techniques was used. The Simple Random Sampling was utilized, which involved the two hundred forty-five (245) students who were officially enrolled in the second semester of the 2024-2025 school year. The contextualized questionnaire was used for data collection, and the statistical tools employed for data analysis included the Mean, Standard Deviation, Pearson Product-Moment Correlation, and Linear Regression. The results showed that the level of environmental practices was high, which implied that it is often manifested and the household green purchasing behavior as high, which implied that it is often manifested by the students as well. Additionally, the study revealed a significant relationship between environmental practices and the green purchasing behavior of college students. Moreover, all the domains of environmental practices, awareness of environmental concepts, awareness of environmental issues, and practices on the need to solve environmental problems significantly influenced the household green purchasing behavior of college students. This only means that environmental practices are integral to the household green purchasing behavior of college students.

latest.title: Institutional Drivers and Constraints of Green Entrepreneurship in Saudi Arabia under Vision 2030: An Integrated Analytic Hierarchy Process
latest.venue: International Journal of Research and Innovation in Social Science
latest.abstract: Although there is increasing academic interest in green entrepreneurship, there are few empirical studies on the enablers and barriers of green entrepreneurship in Gulf Cooperation Council (GCC) economies. This creates a knowledge gap on how oil-dependent and resource-dependent nations can transition to sustainable business ecosystems. This study investigates the institutional, social and economic drivers and barriers to the development of green entrepreneurship in the Kingdom of Saudi Arabia (KSA) in the strategic context of Vision 2030. The study uses a hybrid methodological design of a SWOT-based survey of 62 civil servants working in Saudi Regional Authorities, an Entrepreneurial Ecosystem Framework (EEF) domain-mapping exercise, and a further Analytic Hierarchy Process (AHP) prioritization exercise with 18 experts from regional authorities, development finance institutions, and green entrepreneurship practitioners. The integrated EEF-AHP analysis shows that the domain with the highest priority weight is the Policy and Regulatory Environment (0.28), followed by Finance (0.22) and Human Capital (0.18). This suggests that institutional and financing gaps are the main systemic constraints. In the SWOT survey, the highest-rated strengths are natural resource endowments and environmentally protected areas. The highest-rated weaknesses are limited natural resource management capacity and a low level of existing green infrastructure, followed by the absence of an appropriate regulatory regime. The highest-rated opportunities are new business start-ups, better environmental quality and higher local income. Key threats are demand-side pressures, especially the perception of green products as luxury goods. The highest-rated green entrepreneurship strategies are organic farmin

latest.title: The Effect of Product Availability, Service Quality, Price Fairness and Store Trust on Repurchase Intention (A Study at Sari Jaya Tani Agricultural Store)
latest.abstract: This study analyzes the effects of product availability, service quality, price fairness, and store trust on repurchase intention among customers of Sari Jaya Tani, an agricultural input store in Brebes Regency. A quantitative survey was conducted with 100 customers selected through purposive sampling, and the data were analyzed using multiple linear regression. The four variables jointly had a significant effect on repurchase intention and explained 86.5% of its variance. Service quality, price fairness, and store trust each had a positive and significant effect, whereas product availability had no significant partial effect. Price fairness was the strongest predictor. The non-significant effect of product availability is discussed in relation to its overlap with store trust and the predominance of loyal customers in the sample. Agricultural input retailers should prioritize fair pricing, advisory service, and trust building while keeping stock reliable during planting seasons.

latest.title: Barriers to the Transition from Intention to Green Consumption Behavior: An Empirical Study in Ho Chi Minh City
latest.venue: OIDA International Journal of Sustainable Development
latest.abstract: pace, helping consumers translate positive environmental intentions into actual green consumption behavior has become increasingly important, particularly for advancing responsible production and consumption. Yet the persistent gap between green intention and green behavior suggests that a positive attitude and intention alone are not always enough to produce sustainable consumption. This study therefore examines the factors that shape green purchase intention and green consumption behavior, and analyzes the conditions that can either facilitate or hinder the translation of intention into actual consumer behavior in Ho Chi Minh City, Vietnam. Specifically, drawing on the Theory of Planned Behavior (TPB), the study tests the effects of attitude (ATT), subjective norm (SN), and perceived behavioral control (PBC) on green purchase intention (GPI); the effect of GPI on green consumption behavior (GCB); the mediating role of GPI; and the moderating roles of price sensitivity (PS) and green product availability (PA). The study adopted a mixed-methods design. A preliminary qualitative phase was conducted through interviews and group discussions with 13 consumers to refine and finalize the observed variables. The quantitative phase was carried out through a face-to-face survey of consumers aged 18 and above who had lived in Ho Chi Minh City for at least six months and were involved in their household's purchasing decisions. Of the 400 questionnaires distributed, 354 valid responses were retained for analysis, corresponding to a response rate of 88.5%. The data were processed using SPSS 26.0 and AMOS 24.0. Scale reliability and construct validity were assessed through Cronbach's Alpha and confirmatory factor analysis (CFA), including standardized factor loadings, composite relia

latest.title: From Organizational Strategy to Sustainable Consumption: An Integrated NRBV–TPB Model of Green Market Orientation and Organic Food Choice
latest.venue: Zenodo (CERN European Organization for Nuclear Research)
latest.abstract: Global environmental pollution, problems associated with food safety, and growing awareness about health issues have raised the demand for sustainable consumption; however, the uptake of organic foods has been relatively low in developing countries such as Bangladesh. In this conceptual research, an integrative theoretical model is proposed that links attitude to behavior in organic food consumption by connecting organizational-level green marketing strategies and consumer psychology. Grounded in natural resource-based view (NRBV) and theory of planned behavior (TPB), the model takes green market orientation as the strategic antecedent, which affects consumer attitude toward sustainability and, in turn, organic food consumption. It is posited that consumer attitude toward sustainability acts as the mediating variable between green market orientation and organic food consumption; environmental concern works as the moderating variable for all three direct relationships in the model. Theoretically, this study offers a novel multilevel integration of NRBV and TPB in the sustainable food consumption research area. Practically, it emphasizes the role of genuine green marketing in forming consumers’ sustainability attitudes and organic food consumption in emerging markets. Keywords: green market orientation, organic food consumption, consumer attitude toward sustainability, environmental concern, sustainable consumption, SDG 12, responsible consumption and production Citing This Article (APA Style): Peris, S. F., Gupta, P. D., Purnima, F. H., Rahman, M., & Haque, A. (2026). From organizational strategy to sustainable consumption: An integrated NRBV–TPB model of green market orientation and organic food choice. Global Empirical Marketing Studies, 2(1), Article e2.2026.11.21. ht

latest.title: Assessing environmental indicators for green supply chain success using a structured decision-making framework: a case study of the ceramic industry
latest.abstract: Green Supply Chain Management (GSCM) provides an integrative platform to reduce environmental harm across production systems. This study applies an integrated CRITIC–ARAS multi-criteria decision-making framework to evaluate and prioritize environmental indicators for green supply chain management in the ceramic industry, using the Amin Meybod Tile and Ceramic Factory in Yazd, Iran, as a real-world case study. Environmental criteria were first identified and weighted using the CRITIC method, which quantifies the relative importance of criteria based on contrast intensity and information entropy. These weighted factors were then used to rank the mining sites using the ARAS method. The results indicate that Waste Recycling, Noise Pollution, Waste Level, Gas Emission Levels, and Green Transportation practices are the most influential indicators driving green supply chain performance in the case study. To show the stability of the proposed framework, the results were compared with those obtained from WASPAS, TOPSIS, and MOORA methods, and a high level of consistency in rankings confirmed the stability and reliability of the CRITIC–ARAS approach. The study concludes by offering practical green management strategies and operational recommendations aligned with the identified environmental priorities. The findings contribute theoretically by extending hybrid MCDM applications to resource-intensive industries and practically by providing managers with a structured tool and actionable insights for industries aiming to integrate sustainability principles into supply chain design and resource procurement.

latest.title: Determinants of Green Purchase Intention and Green Purchase Behavior Among College Students in Fujian, China
latest.abstract: Purpose: This study addresses the limited evidence on factors influencing green purchase intention and green purchase behavior among college students in a regional vocational education context in China. Research design, data and methodology: A quantitative survey was conducted among 500 students from the Department of Automation Engineering at Meizhouwan Vocational Technology College. A non-probability sampling approach combining purposive, quota, and convenience sampling was adopted. A pilot test involving 30 participants was conducted, and content validity and reliability were assessed using the Item Objective Congruence method and Cronbach’s alpha. Confirmatory factor analysis and structural equation modeling using AMOS were employed to evaluate the measurement model and test the hypothesized relationships. Results: Perceived behavioral control, subjective norms, attitude, environmental concern, and environmental knowledge significantly influenced green purchase intention (p < .05). Perceived behavioral control showed the strongest effect (β = 0.577), followed by subjective norms (β = 0.369). Green purchase intention significantly predicted green purchase behavior (β = 0.516). Conclusions: The findings demonstrate the importance of perceived behavioral control, social influence, and environmental awareness in strengthening green purchase intention, which subsequently promotes green purchase behavior. Universities and policymakers should implement targeted educational and campus-based initiatives to encourage sustainable consumption among students.

latest.title: Message Framing Strategies in Sustainability Communication: An Analysis in Türkiye
latest.abstract: Sustainability communication has become a strategic priority for organizations demonstrating their environmental, social, and economic commitments, and social media makes audience reactions observable. This study asks whether the framing characteristics of corporate sustainability messages affect consumer engagement in Türkiye. A total of 166 sustainability-related Instagram posts published in 2025 by companies in the BIST Sustainability 25 Index were content-analyzed across five framing variables; gain/loss framing, message direction, tonality, emotional appeal, and temporal focus, and engagement was measured through likes, comments, and shares. Three hypotheses were tested with independent samples t-tests on log-transformed engagement. Only temporal focus was significant: present-focused messages attracted higher engagement than future-focused ones, whereas tonality and emotional appeal did not. The immediacy of a message, rather than its tone, appears to drive engagement.

latest.title: From Circular Production to Consumer Value: Transparency and Layered Consumer Information as Market Mechanisms in Circular Agri-Food Systems
latest.abstract: Circular production systems can reduce resource dependency, retain nutrients and bio-mass in productive use, and valorize unavoidable side-streams, but their economic viability de-pends partly on whether consumers recognize and reward circular attributes that are often invisible at purchase. This conceptual article develops a Circular Value Translation Framework linking circular production to verified transparency and traceability, trust, perceived consumer value, willingness to pay (WTP), and value transmitted back to producers. Its two core contributions are a layered consumer information architecture combining a visible standardized verified core with optional channel-appropriate depth under realistic low-involvement food-choice conditions, and a value-capture feedback loop making producer adoption conditional on premium pass-through, bargaining power, and transition costs. Ten falsifiable propositions specify causal links, label substitution or complementarity, individual moderators, situational frictions, and value transmission. The synthesis integrates circular-food evidence with agricultural-economics research on technology adoption, credence labeling, market power, and vertical price transmission, and proposes prioritized empirical tests and practical implications for producers, cooperatives, certification bodies, retailers, and policymakers.

latest.title: Long‐term Orientation and Proactive Environmental Strategies in Emerging Markets: Evidence From India
latest.abstract: This study examines how emerging market firms characterized by a long‐term orientation (LTO) develop the organizational routines that support proactive environmental strategies (PES). These strategies are essential for sustaining operations within evolving institutions and for adopting environmentally friendly practices in institutionally weak settings. Thus, building on the perspective of organizational routines, this study establishes a positive association between firms' LTO and their likelihood of adopting PES in emerging markets. Furthermore, drawing on informal institutions and transaction‐cost reasoning, the findings suggest that informal competition and crime in emerging markets discourage firms from investing in PES, thereby weakening the baseline relationship. Based on a sample of 6547 Indian firms, we find support for all hypotheses. This research advances the literature on PES by providing insights into how firms' LTO, industry‐level informal competition, and societal‐level crime collectively influence their sustainability strategies in emerging markets.

latest.title: Circular Supply Chain Strategies for Mitigating Partial and Full Disruptions in Distribution Centres
latest.abstract: Supply chain disruptions are unwanted events that can create problems in maintaining the flow of goods and services, delivering and fulfilling demand, managing costs, and potentially hurting resilience performance. Adopting appropriate strategies and the use of precise decision‐making models can help mitigate the disruptions and improve profitability and resilience performance. Previous studies developed models and generated mitigation plans using resilience strategies. However, there are limited studies that quantitatively investigate the usefulness of circular strategies in mitigating disruptions. This study makes the first attempt to develop quantitative models and generate supply chain mitigation plans for mitigating partial and full disruptions in distribution centres (DCs). To do so, we develop a mathematical modelling and simulation approach to develop models under three situations: an ideal plan when there is no disruption, the impacts of disruptions when no strategies are used, and mitigation plans with circular strategies. We use a distribution plan of a smartphone in Australia to demonstrate the results and findings. The results reveal that full disruptions in multiple DCs have the most damaging impacts on demand fulfilment and total profit. Results also reveal that the use of circular strategies, such as utilisation of spare capacity, repair and reuse of products, can improve demand fulfilment and total profit by reducing penalty costs for not meeting the demand. We also compare the results under different situations, such as when no strategies are implemented vs. when strategies are implemented in case of partial and full disruptions in single and multiple DCs. In all situations, circular strategies show a positive influence on demand fulfilment and total p

latest.title: From measurement to message in cultural tourism: a comparative multi-case analysis linking sustainable tourism indicators to stakeholder communication at heritage destinations
latest.abstract: Sustainability indicator systems tell the managers of cultural tourism destinations what to measure, but not what to say, to whom, or through which channel. This study addresses that gap by linking the UNWTO sustainability indicator framework to Integrated Marketing Communication (IMC) theory and applying the combined lens to 74 documented case-indicator observations of sustainability communication in cultural heritage tourism, drawn from more than 30 countries across five world regions. Cases were identified from four institutional compendia of documented practice, screened against explicit inclusion and exclusion criteria, and coded on six dimensions: sustainability pillar, measurement issue, strategic communication objective, IMC method and channel, target stakeholder group, and feedback or data collection mechanism. Each observation was additionally coded on a four-level outcome-evidence ladder, distinguishing communication outputs, stakeholder engagement, attitudinal or knowledge change, and documented behavioral or operational change, so that interpretive claims are calibrated to the strength of the underlying evidence. A subsample was independently double-coded and intercoder agreement is reported. The case analysis is complemented by a semi-systematic review of 25 empirical studies of sustainability communication effectiveness, which supplies the warrant for statements about effects. Three dimension-specific communication logics are identified: economic communication is predominantly supplier-oriented and transactional; environmental communication is education-centered and intermediary-dependent; socio-cultural communication is participatory and the most channel-diverse. Four principles recur across all three dimensions: communication as a data collection instru

latest.title: Moderating role of religiosity in islamic banking intentions and behaviours within the decomposed theory of planned behaviour
latest.abstract: While Islamic banking is becoming more important in Türkiye its market share is still small compared to many other Muslim majority countries. This gives rise to a big question as to how religiosity affects individuals’ intentions and behavior use of Islamic banking services. Therefore, this study investigates the moderator role of religiosity on the individuals’ intentions and behaviors towards Islamic banking in the Decomposed Planned Behavior Model. Survey data from 790 individuals were analyzed using confirmatory factor analysis and structural equation modeling. The results show that attitude is the strongest predictor of intention, while perceived behavioral control also has a positive and significant effect; subjective norm, however, does not significantly predict intention. Intention is the strongest predictor of Islamic banking behavior, with perceived behavioral control also exerting a positive effect. The moderation results further indicate that religiosity does not operate uniformly across the DTPB relationships: it positively moderates the attitude–intention relationship, negatively moderates the subjective norm–intention relationship, does not significantly moderate the PBC–intention or intention–behavior relationships, and shows a weaker moderating effect on the PBC–behavior relationship. These findings extend DTPB-based Islamic banking research by showing that religiosity operates in a path-dependent manner across intention formation and behavioral enactment.

latest.title: Exploring global and regional research trends in sustainable food consumption with a focus on North Africa: a bibliometric analysis
latest.abstract: This bibliometric analysis presents a comprehensive examination of the evolving landscape of consumer behavior toward sustainable food products, encompassing organic, biological, and agroecological items, both within North Africa and on a global scale. The methodology followed PRISMA guidelines to examine and select relevant publications addressing consumer behavior and/or sustainable food products within the Scopus and Web of Science databases. Through meticulous scrutiny of historical emergence, publication trends, Sustainable Development Goals, research areas, author contributions, and bibliometric analyses, this review aims to define the present status and highlight areas that require further exploration. Initial observations highlight the existing literature on sustainable food consumption—identified using selected keywords-within the Web of Science (1,120 documents globally, including 14 for North Africa) and Scopus (1,043 documents globally, including 15 for North Africa) databases. This relatively low frequency of scientific publications in North Africa underscores the need to step up research initiatives and collaborative projects to strengthen regional practices regarding sustainable food systems. Highlighting the interdisciplinary nature of sustainable food studies, this review underscores the urgency of collaborative efforts to nurture sustainable practices, both regionally and globally. Disparities in research outputs between global and regional scales offer opportunities for capacity building and knowledge exchange, urging strategic interventions to bridge gaps and propel sustainable food agendas. Additionally, the review consolidates the research findings, identifies unexplored areas, and delineates future research pathways within consumer studies, concen

latest.title: Modeling Digital-Green Support Systems for Sustainable Franchise Performance: The Interplay of Relational Quality and Management Participation
latest.venue: OIDA International Journal of Sustainable Development
latest.abstract: The simultaneous pressures of digital transformation and sustainable development are reshaping franchise governance, yet limited empirical research has examined how digital, environmental, and reputational resources jointly contribute to sustainable performance, particularly in emerging markets. This study develops and tests an integrated framework explaining how Green Franchising (GF), Digital Franchising (DF), and Brand Reputation (BR) influence Sustainable Franchise Performance (SFP), with Relationship Quality (RQ) serving as a relational mechanism and Franchise Typology (FT) capturing heterogeneity across franchise systems. Drawing on agency theory, resource scarcity logic, signaling theory, social exchange theory, the resource-based view, the natural-resource-based view, and contingency theory, the study conceptualizes sustainable franchise performance as a multidimensional outcome encompassing operational, market, and environmental, social, and governance (ESG) considerations. A quantitative cross-sectional survey was conducted among 314 franchise owners and managers directly involved in operating food and beverage (F&B) franchise outlets in Ho Chi Minh City, Vietnam. Data were analyzed using partial least squares structural equation modeling (PLS-SEM) and multi-group analysis (MGA). The results show that GF (β = 0.246, p < 0.001), DF (β = 0.231, p = 0.001), and BR (β = 0.425, p < 0.001) significantly strengthen RQ, while RQ has a substantial positive effect on SFP (β = 0.493, p < 0.001). BR also directly improves SFP (β = 0.187, p = 0.010). In contrast, the direct effects of GF and DF on SFP are not statistically significant, suggesting that green and digital support resources do not automatically translate into sustainable performance but depend substantially on

latest.title: Persepsi Produk Hijau dan Kemasan Ramah Lingkungan terhadap Advokasi Merek Gentle Gen melalui Nilai Hijau di Malang Raya
latest.abstract: Penelitian ini menganalisis pengaruh Green Product Perception dan Eco-Friendly Packaging terhadap Brand Advocacy melalui Green Perceived Value pada konsumen detergen Gentle Gen di Malang Raya. Kerangka Stimulus–Organism–Response digunakan untuk menjelaskan hubungan atribut produk dan kemasan dengan evaluasi nilai serta advokasi konsumen. Penelitian menggunakan survei kuantitatif potong lintang dengan purposive sampling. Dari 400 kuesioner terkumpul, dokumen sumber melaporkan 387 respons layak dianalisis menggunakan PLS-SEM melalui SmartPLS 4.1 dengan 5.000 sampel bootstrap. Hasil menunjukkan bahwa persepsi produk hijau dan kemasan ramah lingkungan berpengaruh positif terhadap nilai hijau, masing-masing dengan koefisien 0,632 dan 0,321. Nilai hijau berpengaruh positif terhadap advokasi merek dengan koefisien 0,951. Kedua pengaruh langsung atribut terhadap advokasi tidak signifikan, sedangkan pengaruh tidak langsungnya signifikan, sebesar 0,601 dan 0,305. Pola tersebut menunjukkan mediasi melalui nilai hijau dalam model yang dilaporkan. Implikasi manajerialnya adalah perlunya menjelaskan manfaat penggunaan yang relevan bagi konsumen. Interpretasi dibatasi oleh dominasi responden mahasiswa, ketidaksamaan basis data deskriptif dan struktural, serta keterbatasan dokumentasi instrumen. Temuan merepresentasikan persepsi konsumen dan tidak membuktikan keamanan atau dampak ekologis produk secara teknis.

latest.title: Social Media Influencers in Corporate Social Responsibility and Sustainability Communication: A Hybrid Bibliometric and Thematic Review
latest.abstract: Addressing global sustainability challenges and advancing the United Nations Sustainable Development Goals (SDGs), particularly SDG 12 and SDG 13, requires communication that can support pro‐environmental behaviour and responsible consumption. Social media influencers (SMIs) increasingly mediate such communication by translating CSR and sustainability issues into messages linked to everyday practices. This study conducts a hybrid bibliometric and systematic thematic review following the SPAR‐4‐SLR protocol. The bibliometric corpus comprised 206 peer‐reviewed journal articles and reviews indexed in Scopus and Web of Science. Six citation communities comprising 129 documents were retained for interpretation of the citation network, while 86 studies were selected for full‐text thematic synthesis. Performance analysis and science mapping using Bibliometrix (R), VOSviewer, and Gephi were integrated with full‐text thematic synthesis. The review identifies three themes, namely influencer‐driven sustainable communication from a communication perspective, influencer‐driven sustainable consumption from a marketing perspective, and influencer‐driven CSR communication. Across these themes, source credibility, authenticity, congruence, and parasocial relationships form recurring persuasion mechanisms, while the salience and involvement of the organisation vary. The evidence base is concentrated on environmental issues, responsible consumption, and short‐term audience outcomes, with less attention to social equity, economic and legal CSR responsibilities, and verifiable sustainability outcomes. By using organisational involvement to integrate the three streams while preserving CSR's corporate boundary, the review extends embeddedness theory and proposes a potential tension between or

latest.title: Greenwashing and Climate Change Concerns in the Sustainable Development Agenda: Definition, Communication Strategies and Underlying Reasons
latest.abstract: In the tourism and hospitality industry, greenwashing related to the climate is leading to deceptive environmental communication. Mass media play a critical role in providing information and shaping public opinions. Hence, this calls for accountability for greenwashing and its impact on climate change. This study examines 230 online news articles and 50 videos using Gioia's approach to present a multi‐dimensional examination of greenwashing in the tourism and hospitality industry. The data analysis revealed four aggregate dimensions: the meaning and concerns about greenwashing, the types of communication claims and the reasons for greenwashing, representing key themes of greenwashing conversations in popular media discourse related to the tourism and hospitality industry. Each dimension and its underlying constructs unfold the layers of greenwashing, which are exceedingly ambiguous. The study found that the media content presents different types of greenwashed claims. They range from absolute lies to misleading visual imagery. The findings of the study present an inherently contested, evolving and context‐dependent nature of the concept of greenwashing. The media discourse notably highlights ‘passing the buck’ as an important underlying reason for greenwashing in the tourism and hospitality industry.

latest.title: Building a Bridge to Better Buying: Reimaging Marketing for Sustainable Consumption
latest.venue: DigitalCommons - Kennesaw State University (Kennesaw State University)
latest.abstract: The conflict between increasing consumption to increase profits seems at odds with the new trends of more sustainably created products.The discipline of marketing has a long tradition of trying to increase consumer consumption but also is currently poised to shift consumer viewpoints.What would switching that focus to build a more sustainable bridge between consumers and firms look like?In this theoretical paper, the Sustainable Development Goals put out by the United Nations, specifically SDG 12, is looked at using a marketing lens on how consumer behavior can shift the perspective of organizations to promote sustainable practices.Technology developments, such as Generative Artificial Intelligence (Gen AI), can enhance the message delivery and strategy of this goal.Practical examples are given from both an academic and managerial understanding for classroom and workplace usage.

latest.title: Integrating Green Marketing and Digital Marketing Strategies: The Mediating Role of Consumer Perception in Eco-Friendly Accommodation Purchase Intention in Bali, Indonesia
latest.venue: JEMBA JURNAL EKONOMI MANAJEMEN BISNIS DAN AKUNTANSI
authors: Anak Agung Ayu Rika Putri Supartha
latest.abstract: This study analyzes the effects of green marketing and digital marketing on purchase intention, with consumer perception as a mediating variable, in the choice of eco-friendly accommodation in Bali. A quantitative survey approach was applied to 400 domestic tourists who had visited Bali, selected through purposive sampling, and data were collected using a five-point Likert-scale questionnaire in June–July 2026. The data were analyzed using Partial Least Squares–Structural Equation Modeling (PLS-SEM) with SmartPLS, within the Stimulus–Organism–Response (S-O-R) framework that positions marketing strategies as stimuli, consumer perception as the internal evaluation process, and purchase intention as the behavioral response. The results show that green marketing and digital marketing have positive and significant effects on both consumer perception and purchase intention. Consumer perception also has a positive and significant effect on purchase intention and mediates the relationships between green marketing and digital marketing and purchase intention. These findings emphasize the importance of integrating sustainability-oriented and digital marketing strategies to build positive perceptions and increase domestic tourists' intention to choose eco-friendly accommodation in Bali.

hot.title: Sustainable Consumption and Branding for Gen Z: How Brand Dimensions Influence Consumer Behavior and Adoption of Newly Launched Technological Products
hot.abstract: Generation Z is emerging as a powerful force in shaping global consumer behavior, particularly in the market of digital and technological products. This study examines how specific branding dimensions, such as online brand experience, engagement, image, trust, loyalty, awareness, behavioral intention, and brand knowledge, influence Gen Z’s purchase intention, emphasizing sustainable consumption. Sustainable consumption, in this context, refers to the preference for tech products that minimize the environmental impact through eco-friendly design, energy efficiency, and responsible sourcing. Using a quantitative approach, this cross-sectional research explores the effects of online brand experience, engagement, image, trust, loyalty, awareness, behavioral intention, and knowledge on purchasing newly launched technological products that align with sustainability. Data were collected from a Gen Z sample using a combination of convenience and systematic sampling, and multiple regression analysis identified the most significant predictors of purchase intention. The results indicate that online brand experience, brand image, brand trust, and brand loyalty play the most crucial roles, having a greater effects on Gen Z’s purchase intention, while brand awareness and knowledge also contribute. However, brand engagement and behavioral intention have weaker effects. These findings suggest that brands targeting Gen Z should prioritize building a strong, trustworthy, and engaging online presence while highlighting their sustainability efforts, and when Gen Z consumers have favorable digital interactions with a brand, perceive its image positively, trust it, and feel loyal to it, they are more likely to consider purchasing its sustainable offerings. This study enhances the understandi

hot.title: Mapping the greenwashing research landscape: a theoretical and field analysis
hot.abstract: This study provides a comprehensive overview of greenwashing research in business and management, focusing on its conceptual and theoretical foundations. Through a systematic literature review of 97 peer-reviewed articles from Scopus and Web of Science, we use bibliometric analysis to map the evolution of greenwashing studies and network analysis and identify four thematic clusters: (1) symbolic management and CSR communication, (2) environmental regulations and institutional complexity, (3) performance and sustainable practices, and (4) marketing, perception, and trust. Additionally, we perform a full-text analysis to map the theoretical frameworks employed across these clusters, revealing the dominance of macro-level theories (e.g., legitimacy, institutional, and stakeholder theories) and their cross-level interactions with meso- and micro-level approaches. By developing a multi-level theoretical framework, we provide a structured approach to understanding greenwashing across different analytical layers. Then, focusing on the theories used to investigate greenwashing, we identify some avenues for future research. This study has practical implications for understanding how greenwashing affects corporate governance, financial performance, and stakeholder trust, providing insights for enhancing transparency and accountability in sustainable business practices.

hot.title: Greenwashing and market value of firms: An empirical study
hot.abstract: In today's business environment, green or sustainable claims are rising as companies strive to strengthen environmental practices in response to climate change and sustainable development challenges. However, with increasing expectations of sustainable performance, companies encounter mounting financial pressure to adopt more efficient sustainable practices, which may lead some to exploit sustainability efforts for their own gain. Many companies make environmentally friendly assertions to conceal or mask their actual activities—a phenomenon known as greenwashing—which fosters public scepticism about the authenticity of their green messaging. This study employs an event study methodology to examine how the stock market values greenwashing news, drawing on 121 global greenwashing news since the 2015 Paris Agreement . Our findings reveal a negative correlation between greenwashing news and stock market reactions. The market reactions to greenwashing news are more negative for firms with greater ESG performance than for weak ESG performance. Additionally, greenwashing news supported by concrete evidence elicits stronger adverse reactions. Companies operating in the manufacturing industry experience more significant market value losses than those in the service sector . The findings also indicate that the Asia-Pacific market demonstrates particularly strong negative responses to greenwashing news compared to other stock markets. This study contributes to the signalling theory and advances the literature on corporate sustainability practices by providing empirical insights in a global context.

hot.title: The Impact of Green Perceived Value Through Green New Products on Purchase Intention: Brand Attitudes, Brand Trust, and Digital Customer Engagement
hot.abstract: This study examines how the introduction of green new products (GNPs) by luxury brands contributes to building brand equity (i.e., brand attitude and trust) through green perceived value (GPV) and empirically assesses its impact on consumers’ purchase intentions. Furthermore, it explores the moderating role of digital customer engagement (DCE) in the relationship between GPV and building brand equity. To verify the hypothesis, we performed the partial least squares structural equation model (PLS-SEM) as an analytical technique using 572 datasets from luxury consumers in China. The results revealed that GPV through GNPs significantly influences both brand attitude and brand trust. In addition, brand attitude and brand trust were found to have a significantly positive effect on purchase intention. Moreover, DCE was observed to positively moderate the relationship between GPV and brand trust. To enhance the purchase intentions for luxury brands, it is essential to foster brand attitude and brand trust by developing a multidimensional GPV through GNPs. Furthermore, DCE plays a crucial role in strengthening the brand trust component of GPV.

hot.title: The Role of Environmental Certification in the Hospitality Industry: Assessing Sustainability, Consumer Preferences, and the Economic Impact
hot.abstract: Hotel certifications have become increasingly vital in promoting sustainability within the hospitality industry, providing frameworks that guide hotels toward reducing their environmental footprint, enhancing operational efficiency, and gaining a competitive edge in the marketplace. This review explores the development, types, and impact of hotel certifications, with a focus on prominent schemes, such as LEED, Green Key, and EarthCheck. Through an analysis of case studies from globally recognized hotels, we highlight how certifications contribute to significant reductions in energy and water use, improved waste management, and enhanced biodiversity protection, while also delivering economic benefits through cost savings and increased guest loyalty. Our paper also examines consumer perceptions of certifications and their willingness to pay (WTP) for certified hotels. The findings suggest that eco-conscious travelers, particularly younger generations, are willing to pay a premium for hotels that demonstrate a commitment to sustainability; however, consumer awareness of certification schemes remains limited. The barriers to adopting certifications, such as high initial costs, resource limitations, and management resistance, are also discussed, along with the challenges posed by greenwashing and the proliferation of certification schemes. Looking to the future, this review identifies key trends that will shape the evolution of hotel certifications, including increased transparency, the integration of smart technologies, the expanding role of social responsibility, and their alignment with global sustainability goals, such as the United Nations Sustainable Development Goals (SDGs). hot.title: Impact of social media advertising on consumer behavior: role of credibility, perceived authenticity, and sustainability
hot.abstract: Introduction Social media advertising is a crucial factor for predicting consumer behavior. Further credibility, authenticity, and sustainability of social postings enhance consumer purchase intentions in general and online shopping in particular. This empirical study investigated the impact of social media advertising on consumer behavior and the role of credibility, perceived authenticity and sustainability. The study also investigated the mediating effect of trust in the relationship between social media advertising and consumer behavior. Methods To measure the impact of the social media advertising effect on consumer behavior, eight reflective constructs, namely, credibility, sustainability, perceived authenticity, social media advertising effectiveness, satisfaction, purchase intentions and perceived value, were assessed. For the mediation analysis, consumer behavior was modeled as a higher-order construct with three sub-dimensions: satisfaction, perceived value and purchase intentions. Furthermore, the construct social media effectiveness is also modeled as a higher-order construct with four sub-dimensions: credibility, sustainability, authenticity and social media advertisement effectiveness. The data were collected from active social media users who engage in brand advertising and online shopping. A total of 500 valid responses were subjected to exploratory and confirmatory factor analysis, and the hypotheses were tested via structural equation modeling. Results and discussion The SEM results reveal that constructs credibility and sustainability are strong predictors of consumer behavior in the context of social media advertising effectiveness. The mediating variable of trust partially mediated the relationship between social media effectiveness and consumer beh

hot.title: Exploring the role of health consciousness and environmental awareness in purchase intentions for green-packaged organic foods: an extended TPB model
hot.abstract: Background: With the increasing rise of green consumption concepts, consumers are becoming more concerned with the health and environmental attributes of products. However, research on purchase intentions for green-packaged organic foods remains relatively limited, particularly regarding the specific impact of health consciousness and environmental awareness. There is a clear gap in the literature addressing these factors. Method: Based on the Theory of Planned Behavior (TPB), this study constructs a relationship model between health consciousness, environmental awareness, attitude, subjective norms, perceived behavioral control, and purchase intentions for green-packaged organic foods. A total of 372 valid survey samples were collected, and data analysis was performed using SPSS 26.0 and AMOS 28.0 software to validate the theoretical model and research hypotheses. Results: Structural equation modeling (SEM) analysis reveals that all hypotheses are significantly supported, and the model demonstrates good fit. Mediation effect analysis further reveals the impact of health consciousness and environmental awareness on purchase intentions, indicating that they influence consumer intentions indirectly through attitudes, subjective norms, and perceived behavioral control. Conclusion: Health consciousness and environmental awareness not only significantly affect consumers' purchase intentions for green-packaged organic foods through direct paths but also have important indirect effects through attitudes, subjective norms, and perceived behavioral control. This study provides a new perspective for the theoretical development of green consumer behavior and offers valuable practical insights for businesses and policymakers in promoting green consumption and sustainable products.

hot.title: Artificial Intelligence in Digital Marketing Within the Framework of Sustainable Management
hot.abstract: Artificial Intelligence (AI) is not only revolutionizing digital marketing through personalized customer experiences and optimized advertising strategies, but it is also contributing to sustainability initiatives. As AI reshapes digital marketing, its impact on sustainability is becoming increasingly significant. This dynamic highlights the necessity of exploring how AI can be utilized to foster more sustainable marketing practices. This study seeks to answer the pivotal question: “How does AI impact the sustainability of digital marketing?” A systematic literature review was conducted in this study, following the PRISMA (Preferred Reporting Items for Systematic Reviews and Meta-Analyses) framework to identify various relevant articles in the areas of sustainability and marketing. Furthermore, this study examines the crucial role of AI in enhancing sustainable business practices, highlighting a significant increase in adoption among enterprises. The findings demonstrate that the effective integration of AI into digital marketing enhances environmental sustainability, supports the attainment of economic sustainability objectives, and contributes positively to social sustainability outcomes. This study contributes to the field by providing a comprehensive analysis of the intersection between AI and sustainable marketing practices and offers valuable insights for marketers, businesses, and policymakers.

hot.title: Digital Tourism and Smart Development: State-of-the-Art Review
hot.abstract: The intersection between digital technologies and tourism emerges as a prominent area of research within the tourism industry. This is primarily driven by the immense complexity of digital tourism itself as a multifaceted social, economic, and cultural phenomenon. This paper reveals the future implications of tourism in the context of digital intelligence. To gain insights into the latest applications of digital tourism, this work reviews 278 studies spanning from 2012 to 2024. A systematic literature analysis method is proposed to identify the research hotspots and trends. Through value co-creation theory and Schumpeter’s innovation theory, five key trajectories are suggested, as follows: in-depth application of digital technologies in tourism, spawning new scenarios, new forms and new modes of digital tourism, and deep integration of digital economy and tourism real economy. This state-of-the-art review will help to reflect the efforts towards promoting the smart development of digital technologies in tourism.

hot.title: The Evolution of Digital Tourism Marketing: From Hashtags to AI-Immersive Journeys in the Metaverse Era
hot.abstract: This study examines how social media platforms influence tourism marketing strategies, consumer perceptions, and travel behaviors, addressing their sustainability implications. It aims to evaluate the current state of research on social media in tourism marketing, identify dominant trends, assess empirical evidence of impact, and critically highlight research gaps. The analysis focuses on three core marketing outcomes: destination image, travel intention, and user engagement—and includes a section examining sustainability considerations across environmental, sociocultural, and economic dimensions. The study uses a systematic critical review of 147 peer-reviewed academic articles published between 2015 and 2025, combined with a meta-analysis of 38 quantitative studies that report statistical effect sizes. The meta-analysis uses a random-effects model to compare the influence of different platforms and study contexts. Moderator variables include geographic region, platform type, and methodological design. Findings show that social media marketing has a statistically significant positive effect on destination image (Cohen’s d = 0.61), travel intention (d = 0.54), and user engagement (d = 0.43). The analysis also reveals geographic bias, limited research on emerging platforms, and a lack of longitudinal and ethical inquiry. Findings suggest that tourism researchers and marketers may have to adopt more context-sensitive, interdisciplinary, and ethical approaches. Critical sustainability concerns emerge, including “overtourism”, cultural commodification, digital inequities, and algorithmic biases. hot.title: Artificial Intelligence Influencers’ Credibility Effect on Consumer Engagement and Purchase Intention
hot.venue: Journal of theoretical and applied electronic commerce research
hot.abstract: In the evolving world of influencer marketing, Artificial Intelligence (AI) influencers are creating significant impact and transforming the approach to brand promotions on social media platforms. In recent times, many popular brands have partnered with AI influencers to engage with their social media audiences. AI influencers have become popular as a novel method for brands to increase customer engagement and create purchase intention, but there is a scarcity of research on this emerging trend of marketing. The AI-based virtual influencers effect on consumer engagement and purchase intention remain largely unexplored. This study used a questionnaire-based survey method and 414 responses were collected. The result from the research shows that credibility, informative value and human-likeness are the major factors influencing consumer engagement purchase intention towards brands promoted through AI-based virtual influencers. The attractiveness and entertainment value of AI influencer’s social media posts affect consumer engagement but exhibit no effect on purchase intention. Theoretical and managerial recommendations related to AI influencers’ marketing are presented.

hot.title: Artificial Intelligence-Driven Recommendations and Functional Food Purchases: Understanding Consumer Decision-Making
hot.abstract: Amid rapid advancements in artificial intelligence (AI), personalized recommendation systems have become a key factor shaping consumer decision-making in functional food purchases. However, the influence of AI recommendation characteristics on purchase intention, particularly the underlying mediating mechanisms, remains underexplored. This study aims to investigate how AI recommendation features (personalization and transparency), along with functional food attributes (perceived health benefits and perceived naturalness), influence purchase intention through the mediating roles of perceived packaging and perceived value. Grounded in the Stimulus-Organism-Response framework, data were collected via a structured questionnaire survey, and structural equation modeling was employed for hypothesis testing and model validation. The results indicate that AI recommendation personalization significantly enhances purchase intention both directly and indirectly, while transparency influences purchase intention only through perceived value, emphasizing its role in fostering trust rather than directly driving purchasing behavior. Additionally, perceived health benefits positively influence purchase intention both directly and through mediation, whereas perceived naturalness affects purchase intention only indirectly via perceived value. These findings contribute to consumer behavior research by elucidating psychological mechanisms underlying AI-driven purchase decisions while also providing insights for functional food marketers on how to effectively integrate AI recommendation systems to enhance consumer engagement.

hot.title: Digital Leadership and Sustainable Development: Enhancing Firm Sustainability Through Green Innovation and Top Management Innovativeness
hot.abstract: This study examines the crucial role of digital leadership in advancing sustainable development by fostering green innovation and enhancing firm sustainability. Building on Organizational Learning Theory (OLT) and Dynamic Capabilities Theory (DCT), this research fills a key gap by examining how digital leadership integrates digitalization with sustainable development, particularly within the Chinese information technology sector. The study investigates the impact of digital leadership on green innovation and sustainable performance, moderated by top management innovativeness. To enhance analytical robustness and minimize bias, a three‐phase time‐lagged data collection approach was employed to mitigate common method bias and ensure robust analysis, with responses from 413 employees representing diverse roles. The results indicate that digital leadership positively influences the green innovation process, which partially mediates the relationship between digital leadership and firm sustainability. Furthermore, the findings reveal that top management innovativeness amplifies the positive effects of digital leadership on green innovation, reinforcing the importance of leadership‐driven sustainability strategies. These insights contribute to the expanding discourse on corporate digital sustainability, demonstrating that digital transformation not only enhances operational efficiency but also serves as a catalyst for long‐term sustainable development. The study offers valuable implications for policymakers, business leaders, and researchers committed to leveraging digital leadership for corporate sustainability and the achievement of Sustainable Development Goals (SDGs).

hot.title: A Comprehensive Micro, Small, and Medium Enterprise Empowerment Model for Developing Sustainable Tourism Villages in Rural Communities: A Perspective
hot.abstract: This study investigates the factors driving micro, small, and medium enterprise (MSME) empowerment, tourism development, and sustainable tourism villages, focusing on Ponggok Tourism Village as a case study. The purpose is to address gaps in understanding how leadership, innovation, governance, collaboration, capacity building, and technology contribute to empowering MSMEs and achieving sustainability in rural tourism contexts. Using a mixed-methods approach, the study combines quantitative analysis of survey data and thematic analysis of interviews with MSME actors, facilitators, and local government officials. Key findings reveal that leadership and innovation are critical drivers of MSME empowerment, with technology in service quality significantly impacting tourism development. However, technology in governance and transparency shows limited direct influence on tourism, emphasizing the need for better alignment with tourism strategies. Additionally, MSME empowerment strongly influences both tourism development and the sustainability of tourism villages, creating a mutually reinforcing relationship. This study provides a novel framework for integrating leadership, technological advancements, and governance improvements with local tourism strategies. By highlighting Ponggok’s village potential as a model, the findings offer practical insights for policymakers and practitioners seeking to enhance rural tourism through MSME empowerment. Future research could explore scaling this framework to other contexts and refining technological tools for governance in tourism.

hot.title: Unveiling the future of responsible, sustainable, and ethical consumption: a bibliometric study on Gen Z and young consumers
hot.venue: Young Consumers Insight and Ideas for Responsible Marketers
hot.abstract: Purpose This study aims to investigate the key research themes and their evolutionary trajectory within the Gen Z and young consumers (GZYC) field, focusing on the interconnected dimensions of responsible, sustainable and ethical consumption. By using thematic maps and co-occurrence networks, the research seeks to identify significant trends and interconnections that shape sustainable behavior among this demographic. Design/methodology/approach This study used a bibliometric analysis of 546 papers sourced from the Scopus and Web of Science databases, following the framework established by Zupic and Cater (2015), Donthu (2024), Donthu et al. (2021) and Lim et al. (2024). Using R and Biblioshiny, the authors conducted performance analysis and science mapping to examine scientific output and conceptual themes within the GZYC field. Findings The performance analysis reveals an annual growth rate of 22.02% in publications, highlighting the increasing research interest in this area. The keyword co-occurrence analysis revealed eight distinct research clusters within the GZYC field, each representing key dimensions of responsible, sustainable and ethical consumption. These clusters encompass themes such as corporate social responsibility, gender and generational differences, green products, food sustainability, pro-environmental behaviors, the sharing economy and collaborative consumption, among others. The thematic maps and evolution revealed that over time, the focus has shifted. The first decade centered on sustainability and young consumers, while the second decade broadened to corporate social responsibility, green advertising and the sharing economy. By 2024, the focus has shifted toward more systemic and psychological perspectives, emphasizing the circular economy, susta

hot.title: Factors influencing Generation Z’s intention to purchase sustainable clothing products in Vietnam
hot.abstract: The increasing awareness of environmental challenges has significantly influenced consumer behavior, with sustainable products, particularly sustainable clothing, becoming a top priority for Generation Z consumers. This study aims to investigate the factors influencing Generation Z's purchase intentions toward sustainable clothing in Vietnam, guided by the Stimulus-Organism-Response (SOR) model and Theory of Planned Behavior (TPB) frameworks. Specifically, it examines the effects of green perceived value, green perceived quality, perceived price, social influence, product design, environmental concern, and environmental knowledge on purchase intentions. The study also explores the mediating roles of environmental attitude and product attitude in these relationships. The research employed a quantitative approach, using a Likert scale questionnaire to gather data from 641 Vietnamese Generation Z consumers. The study utilized exploratory factor analysis (EFA), confirmatory factor analysis (CFA), and structural equation modeling (SEM) to analyze the data. The results revealed that all proposed hypotheses were supported, indicating that all factors significantly impact environmental attitude and product attitude, which, in turn, influence purchase intention. The results emphasize the strong mediating role of environmental attitude and product attitude, suggesting that consumers with positive attitudes toward the environment and products are more likely to intend to purchase sustainable clothing. This research provides valuable insights into the psychological and contextual factors that influence Generation Z's sustainable consumption behavior. For marketers, these findings underscore the need to promote transparency in sustainable practices, emphasize high product quality an

hot.title: Impact of green advertisement and environmental knowledge on intention of consumers to buy green products
hot.abstract: In recent years, the rising concern for environmental sustainability has reshaped consumer preferences, driving a growing interest in eco-friendly products. Green advertising, which promotes products based on their environmental benefits, has emerged as a powerful tool in influencing consumer intentions and encouraging sustainable choices. Green advertising has transformative impacts on buying intention of consumers towards green products, and this leads to advancement of economic sustainability. This study explorese the impact of green advertising and environmental knowledge on consumers' intentions to purchase eco-friendly products, addressing a critical gap in understanding the psychological factors that drive sustainable consumer behavior. Additionally, the study discusses the role of eco-branding, eco-labelling, and consumer innovativeness as moderators of the intention of green product purchase. The data was collected from 512 Chinese individuals and employed structural equation model for empirical analysis. Our findings reveal that green advertising has a significant positive influence on consumers' intention to buy green products, with environmental knowledge amplifying this effect. Additionally, factors such as eco-branding, eco-labelling, and consumer innovativeness further enhance consumers' inclination towards sustainable purchases. These insights highlight the importance of integrating educational elements into green advertising strategies and suggest that companies should invest in eco-labelling and branding to reinforce consumer trust and engagement with sustainable products. The empirical findings carry implications for refining green advertising strategies, suggesting increased investments in both green production and advertising initiatives.

hot.title: A critical review of the theory of planned behaviour in tourism research
hot.abstract: The Theory of Planned Behaviour (TPB) has received considerable attention across various academic disciplines and remains one of the most widely applied – yet increasingly critiqued – theoretical frameworks in tourism research. Despite its widespread use, there is a notable lack of critical reflection on its adequacy in capturing the complexity of tourist behaviour and a limited exploration of alternative theoretical pathways. This paper addresses this gap by critically evaluating the appropriateness and limitations of the TPB in tourism research. Special attention is given to the Theory of Reasoned Goal Pursuit (TRGP), a recent extension of the TPB, alongside complementary frameworks from parent disciplines and emerging methodological innovations. The paper concludes that an overreliance on the TPB may constrain theoretical advancement in the field. Future research on tourist decision-making and human behaviour should therefore consider broader, interdisciplinary approaches that more effectively account for emotional, contextual, and cognitive complexities.

hot.title: Circular Economy: Literature Review on the Implementation of the Digital Product Passport (DPP) in the Textile Industry
hot.abstract: The development of a system to store and share key information about productlifecycles offers a key opportunity to improve the textile and apparel industry. Theintroduction of the digital product passport (DPP) serves as an inclusive tool that enablesindustry stakeholders—companies, suppliers, stakeholders, government organizations,public institutions, and consumers—to more accurately track the journey, characteristics,components, and environmental impact of products. This study explores the implementationand potential of the DPP, highlighting its transformative role as a bridge betweentechnological innovation and sustainability in the textile and apparel sector. By providingunprecedented transparency and traceability, the DPP disrupts conventional industryparadigms and facilitates sustainable practices. The findings highlight the DPP’s ability toconsolidate disparate data into a unified system that provides stakeholders with actionableinsights that were previously unavailable. In addition, the study identifies regulatory andoperational gaps and positions the DPP as a pioneering solution to these challenges. This issignificant progress toward operationalizing the principles of the circular economy andfostering innovation along the entire value chain. In line with the European Commission’s2020 Circular Economy Action Plan, the DPP complements initiatives such as the Ecodesignfor Sustainable Products Regulation (ESPR) and improves product traceability. By providingstakeholders with reliable, comparable data, it supports informed decision making andpromotes transparency, decarbonization, and sustainability. This analysis underlines thepotential of the DPP to transform the sector into a better informed and environmentallyconscious industry.

hot.title: From Asymmetry to Satisfaction: The Dynamic Role of Perceived Value and Trust to Boost Customer Satisfaction in the Tourism Industry
hot.abstract: The study investigates how information asymmetry affects customer satisfaction in the tourism industry by examining trust and perceived value as mediating factors. The research implements an integrated model to test and prove information asymmetry’s direct and mediating effects on customer satisfaction by examining the literature gap. The research used a quantitative approach based on opinion polls distributed to 408 customers of hotels, tourism companies, and travel agencies who were in Egypt. SmartPLS 3 software implemented the data analysis process using partial least squares structural equation modeling (PLS-SEM). Previous studies have developed scales to measure information asymmetry and its related constructs, including customer trust, perceived value, and customer satisfaction. Multiple tests showed that the measurement tools possess both reliability and validity. Results strongly support all hypotheses: information asymmetry demonstrated significant direct negative effects on customer satisfaction (β = −0.187), trust (β = −0.520), and perceived value (β = −0.453). Conversely, customer satisfaction received significant positive direct effects from both trust (β = 0.273) and perceived value (β = 0.263). Importantly, trust (indirect effect β = −0.142) and perceived value (indirect effect β = −0.119) acted as powerful mediators, confirming that information asymmetry diminishes satisfaction largely by eroding these crucial factors. Crucially, the results demonstrate that the negative impact of information asymmetry on customer satisfaction is significantly mediated jointly through two parallel pathways: the erosion of customer trust and the impairment of perceived value. The research adds theoretical support to information asymmetry theory with its findings while als

hot.title: Cyber Shopping Beyond Boundaries: The Metaverse Revolution in e‐Commerce and Consumer Behavior
hot.abstract: The metaverse is swiftly flattering an important player in the e‐commerce domain. It provides innumerable opportunities and indicates a revolutionary paradigm shift in e‐commerce. Online businesses can now create virtual storefronts that enable immersive, lifelike product exploration within the metaverse, in contrast to traditional brick‐and‐mortar stores that cater to local customers. Current research offers a novel conceptual framework based on theories of interactive media effects and the stimulus–organism–response paradigm to understand consumer purchase intentions in the metaverse. Carefully gathered data from 342 survey participants were then examined using the analytical tools of structural equation modelling (SEM) and importance–performance map analysis (IPMA). The results of the study shed light on how much perceived augmentation and interaction affect consumers’ cognitive and emotive reactions, including feelings of realism, immersion, and telepresence. Remarkably, these reactions have a significant influence on how customers behave. The study’s distinctive worth is found in its creative recommendations, which can help tech firms and metaverse developers improve the purchasing experience in this dynamic digital environment.

hot.title: Greenwashing and consumer skepticism toward eco-labels in Croatia: challenges and policy directions
hot.abstract: Purpose This study investigates the roots of consumer skepticism toward eco-labels in Croatia, a market increasingly shaped by greenwashing and regulatory frailty. Grounded in the theory of planned behavior and signaling theory, it analyzes the psychological and communicative mechanisms that underpin trust in sustainability labeling. Design/methodology/approach A survey of 252 Croatian consumers was conducted using regression analysis. Data were collected via the tablet-assisted intercept method in five stores. The questionnaire had 13 Likert items, demographics and one open-ended question. A pilot test preceded fieldwork. In-store context allowed for real-time consumer insight. Findings Four determinants – eco-label visibility, institutional support, credibility of labels and consumer knowledge – emerged as significant predictors of purchase intention. The findings imply that standardized visual placement and transparent messaging are pivotal in reducing skepticism, bolstering trust and fostering environmentally responsible purchasing behavior. Research limitations/implications The study covers one country with a limited sample, mostly younger consumers. It uses a survey, so it does not capture deeper attitudes. Future work should add qualitative methods, include older age groups and compare with other countries in similar transitions. Practical implications Policy suggestions include standardized label placement, better consumer education and digital tools for transparency. Retailers should support eco-labels through loyalty programs and in-store efforts to strengthen trust and encourage sustainable choices.
